## The reading feed's revisit list, against both records

*2026-10-01 05:20:45 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-377 — Rejected on its proofs, and named here to record why it is held in both records -->


The anthology's issue 180
(https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/issues/180) works through the
owner's reading feed by how often a paper was returned to: papers opened on
three or more separate days, ranked from the papers-feed snapshot of 30
September. Twenty-nine of them were absent from the anthology. This entry
records what that list meant for this record.

**The trap: the ranking checked one record.** The worklist was computed
against the anthology's `arxiv:` ids only, so six papers already held here
looked unfiled: the work capacity of channels with memory ([LIT-041](../../record/literature.d/LIT-041.md)),
collective intelligence ([LIT-046](../../record/literature.d/LIT-046.md)), community detection with Ricci flow
([LIT-004](../../record/literature.d/LIT-004.md)), spectral networks ([LIT-017](../../record/literature.d/LIT-017.md)), sharing disinformation incidents
([LIT-083](../../record/literature.d/LIT-083.md)) and ZipNN ([LIT-268](../../record/literature.d/LIT-268.md)). Any future pass over the feed should
check both records' ids before calling a paper absent.

**Filed here.** Chuai & Zhao's *Anger makes fake news viral online*
([LIT-379](../../record/literature.d/LIT-379.md)) came here at the owner's direction: how emotion drives the
spread of false news is not something an anthology topic holds. It is a
`Deferred` seed, read for triage only.

Döring & Isham's *'What is a Thing?': Topos Theory in the Foundations of
Physics* ([LIT-378](../../record/literature.d/LIT-378.md), with [NOTE-326](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-326.md)) was first set aside as out of
scope for both records. The owner corrected that: it is the one-volume
statement of the topos programme whose four papers ([LIT-343](../../record/literature.d/LIT-343.md), [LIT-335](../../record/literature.d/LIT-335.md),
[LIT-299](../../record/literature.d/LIT-299.md), [LIT-310](../../record/literature.d/LIT-310.md)) this record already holds, and it is filed `Active` and
read in full. By the authors' own account it is mostly those four papers
reprinted. It does not settle [THEORY-037](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-037.md), because it again leaves the
Heyting implication unwritten.

**Held in both, under [ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md).** Two works now have an entry on each side,
and each side reads them for a question of its own:

- *On Context-Content Uncertainty Principle* ([LIT-377](../../record/literature.d/LIT-377.md), with
  [NOTE-325](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-325.md)). This record holds the v1 the owner read, a cognitive and
  information-theoretic framework, and rejects it on its proofs: a theorem
  stated backwards, a false KL inequality (q = (.5, .25, .25),
  p = (.8, .1, .1) gives 0.322 bits against the 0.578 the inequality needs),
  and simulations the abstract promises and the paper does not contain. The
  anthology holds the author's v2, a different paper under a new title that
  makes claims about generalization, mixture-of-experts routing and
  alignment, as a seed with no experiments.
- *ZipNN* ([LIT-268](../../record/literature.d/LIT-268.md)). This record reads it for where the redundancy in stored
  weights sits; the anthology files it as a systems paper on checkpoint
  storage and transfer.

The entries name each other once the anthology's codes are permanent: its
side is filed with temporary codes and is renamed when it merges, so the
`ANTH-LIT-…` citations [ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md) asks for are a follow-up.

**Also held in the anthology now.** The work-capacity, collective
intelligence and Ricci-flow papers were first read on the anthology side and
not filed there, because no anthology topic held them honestly. The owner
approved the topics its reader proposed (`agents-and-environments` and
`graphs-and-networks`), and they are filed there as well, each read for what
it says about agents or graph models, where this record reads them for
information theory, complex systems and network science.

**Also found:** [LIT-041](../../record/literature.d/LIT-041.md)'s arXiv id now serves a v2 (30 September 2026) under a
new title, which failed the source check on `main`. The note records both
titles, and its reading covers v1 only.

## Xin Li's structural-learning programme, read as one

*2026-10-01 16:48:51 · curation · record*

**What changed and why.** [LIT-373](../../record/literature.d/LIT-373.md) and [LIT-374](../../record/literature.d/LIT-374.md) were first read one at a time, and each was filed `Rejected` largely on
mathematical slips. Those slips included an "if and only if" that should be "if", a pseudo-dimension that should be
fat-shattering, a bouquet built with open covers where partitions were wanted, and a word used in two senses. The owner
objected on two counts. The papers are pieces of one research programme and must be read together, and the slips were
minutiae: what matters is whether the major takeaways are argued well.

One reader then read both papers together. It also read the author's two companion papers, which are filed here:
- [LIT-375](../../record/literature.d/LIT-375.md), arXiv 2602.07974 v2, the fullest formal statement;
- [LIT-376](../../record/literature.d/LIT-376.md), arXiv 2603.15412 v1, "Local Urysohn Width".

It read charitably: a technical error counts only if a major takeaway depends on it and its sensible repair does not
save it.

**The programme.** Structure is discovered by costly search, condensed into frozen context tokens, and then reused
cheaply. Discovering structure and using it are separate problems, with separate complexities (width against VC
dimension) and separate mechanisms (scaffold against flow, router against experts). [LIT-373](../../record/literature.d/LIT-373.md) is the cognitive and
neural statement of it. [LIT-375](../../record/literature.d/LIT-375.md) and [LIT-376](../../record/literature.d/LIT-376.md) are the formal statements, and [LIT-374](../../record/literature.d/LIT-374.md) is the alignment and
architecture statement.

**Verdicts on the takeaways.**
- **Width is incomparable with VC dimension.** Established in repaired form. [LIT-376](../../record/literature.d/LIT-376.md)'s bouquet is the consistent
  construction the others lacked. The moral drawn from it, that "scaling cannot repair structure", is undermined: the
  comparison is with a per-cell smooth predictor class, not with what a model can represent. Width is in effect a
  covering number at scale, and [LIT-376](../../record/literature.d/LIT-376.md)'s own Remark 8.11 concedes that the obstruction is metric, not topological.
- **An error floor below width (the "phase transition").** Established in repaired form, but close to definitional.
- **Width is estimable from data.** The Ω(w log w) discovery cost is established. The spectral estimator is plausible
  but under-argued: it converges to a count relative to a given predictor, not to width.
- **Decouple router training from task loss, and freeze settled contexts.** Plausible but under-argued. It is a
  testable design hypothesis with continual-learning precedent, but the additive bound it is said to follow from holds
  for joint training too.
- **Amortisation: stored search makes inference cheap.** Argued well enough to take seriously, once "Savitch" is read
  as memoisation. The idea is borrowed. The exponential-reach scaling law ([LIT-373](../../record/literature.d/LIT-373.md) Theorem 2) is not argued.
- **Collapse defeats the curse of dimensionality, and equals free-energy minimisation.** Plausible but under-argued,
  because it moves the curse into the cost of learning the collapse. The equivalence with free-energy minimisation is
  asserted.
- **The neural instantiation.** Plausible but under-argued: the predictions do not discriminate it from standard
  consolidation accounts.
- **Alignment is a scaffold property.** Not argued.

**Standings.**
- **[LIT-373](../../record/literature.d/LIT-373.md)** stays `Rejected`, on new grounds. After repair its core restates amortised inference and complementary
  learning systems, its predictions do not discriminate, and its one original quantitative claim is unargued.
- **[LIT-374](../../record/literature.d/LIT-374.md)** goes from `Rejected` to `Proposed`. It is the only place the decoupling and safety material appears, so it
  is not superseded, though its learning theory is better read in [LIT-375](../../record/literature.d/LIT-375.md).
- **[LIT-375](../../record/literature.d/LIT-375.md)** and **[LIT-376](../../record/literature.d/LIT-376.md)** are `Proposed`.
- [NOTE-321](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-321.md) and [NOTE-322](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-322.md) carry new summaries and a superseding "Joint re-reading" section. Their first readings stay in
  place below, as the record of what was said.

What would settle the programme is one set of synthetic benchmarks of known width:
- a sweep of the number of contexts, comparing routed learners with capacity-matched monolithic models;
- recovery of width from a cold start;
- decoupled against joint router training, compared on forgetting and on boundary error.

A THEORY is not yet warranted. The proved results are a covering number and a coupon-collector bound, and the
explanatory claim (that forgetting is router drift, and that decoupling prevents it) has no evidence in the record. A
draft is held for when an empirical source is filed.

**Versions.** Both companion identifiers now serve different papers from the ones read.
- arXiv 2602.07974 v1 is "Beyond Optimization", so the entry is dated by v2.
- arXiv 2603.15412 v2 (2026-09-14) is "The Metric Slingshot", a grid-cell paper. The entry is v1, the paper the owner
  asked for, with a `source-ok` directive. Its NOTE judges v2 separately, and v2 would be `Rejected`: its grid-ratio
  result depends on a free capacity parameter, and its anaesthesia "confirmation" is post hoc.

**Lesson.** Read a programme's papers together, and judge a hypothesis paper by whether its takeaways are argued, not by
whether every statement survives a referee's pen. Both first readings were right about the slips and wrong about what
they implied.

## Antonio Damasio: six works, and a word for emotion

*2026-10-01 21:17:52 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-385 LIT-386 LIT-387 — Unavailable, unread for want of a full text; listed here as filed seeds -->

The owner asked for "some Antonio Damasio" in this record. Six works came
in, chosen to cover the line of his thought from memory to consciousness:

| work | filed | read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Damasio 1989, time-locked retroactivation (*Cognition*) | [LIT-385](../../record/literature.d/LIT-385.md) | no: Deferred, abstract only |
| Damasio 1996, the somatic marker hypothesis (*Phil. Trans. B*) | [LIT-384](../../record/literature.d/LIT-384.md), [NOTE-332](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-332.md) | in full |
| Bechara, Damasio, Tranel & Damasio 1997, deciding advantageously (*Science*) | [LIT-383](../../record/literature.d/LIT-383.md), [NOTE-331](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-331.md) | in full |
| Damasio & Carvalho 2013, the nature of feelings (*Nat. Rev. Neurosci.*) | [LIT-388](../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md), [NOTE-330](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-330.md) | in full |
| Man & Damasio 2019, homeostasis and feeling machines (*Nat. Mach. Intell.*) | [LIT-386](../../record/literature.d/LIT-386.md) | no: Deferred, abstract only |
| Damasio & Damasio 2023, feelings as the source of consciousness (*Neural Comput.*) | [LIT-387](../../record/literature.d/LIT-387.md) | no: Deferred, abstract only |

**Three are unread because no full text could be reached.** The 1989 paper is
behind ScienceDirect with no open copy. Man & Damasio has no arXiv version and
no open copy. The 2023 paper has a free PDF at MIT Press, but its bot
challenge refused every request. Each is a `Deferred` seed whose
`status_note` says what it rests on.

**A word for emotion ([ADR-014](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-014.md)).** Damasio's subject had no tag, so the owner
asked for one and `emotion-and-affect` joined the vocabulary.

**What the readings found.**

- **Bechara et al. 1997 claims more in its abstract than its statistics show.**
  All 10 controls and none of the 6 patients developed anticipatory skin
  conductance responses. But the controls' preference for the good decks
  before any hunch is not significant. The early skin-conductance effect is
  reported only as a group-by-period interaction, with no test of bad decks
  against good. "Before knowing" holds for the stated strategy, not for
  awareness in general. The record does not yet hold Maia & McClelland's 2004
  critique of the awareness timing.
- **The 1996 paper is a hypothesis paper.** Its evidence is summarised from
  other work without statistics. Two corrections are in its NOTE.
- **The 2013 paper's one shown result** is that feeling survives bilateral
  insula damage, from a single patient. The evolutionary account, animal
  feeling and the cellular proposal are asserted.

**Two things checked along the way.**

- **[NOTE-120](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-120.md) does not cite the 2023 *Neural Computation* paper.** Its
  "Damasio & Damasio 2023" is a different commentary, *Sensing is a far cry
  from sentience* (*Animal Sentience* 33(16)), cited through [LIT-193](../../record/literature.d/LIT-193.md). [NOTE-120](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-120.md)
  reports it correctly. That commentary is the natural next filing for the
  plant-sentience thread.
- **Man & Damasio carries `anthology-candidate`.** Its abstract proposes a
  class of machines without building or measuring one. The anthology's
  `agents-and-environments` topic could hold it, so under [ADR-001](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-001.md) it may be
  theirs. Whether to transfer it is for whoever reads the paper.

The owner asked for Marvin Minsky's Society of Mind programme and for Douglas
Hofstadter. Sixteen works came in, eight from each.

## Minsky

| work | filed | read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "A Framework for Representing Knowledge", AI Memo 306 (1974) | [LIT-410](../../record/literature.d/LIT-410.md), [NOTE-337](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-337.md) | in full, OCR of the DSpace scan |
| "Plain Talk About Neurodevelopmental Epistemology", AI Memo 430 (1977) | [LIT-399](../../record/literature.d/LIT-399.md), [NOTE-344](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-344.md) | in full, IJCAI-77 text |
| "K-Lines: A Theory of Memory", AI Memo 516 (1979) / *Cognitive Science* (1980) | [LIT-402](../../record/literature.d/LIT-402.md), [NOTE-352](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-352.md) | in full, the memo |
| "Jokes and the Logic of the Cognitive Unconscious", AI Memo 603 (1980) | [LIT-408](../../record/literature.d/LIT-408.md), [NOTE-361](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-361.md) | in full, the memo |
| *The Society of Mind* (1986) | [LIT-429](../../record/literature.d/LIT-429.md) | no: Deferred |
| "Society of mind: a response to four reviews" (1991) | [LIT-418](../../record/literature.d/LIT-418.md) | no: Deferred, closed |
| *The Emotion Machine* (2006) | [LIT-432](../../record/literature.d/LIT-432.md), [NOTE-348](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-348.md) | in full, the author's posted 2005 draft |
| Singh, "Examining the Society of Mind" (2003) | [LIT-444](../../record/literature.d/LIT-444.md), [NOTE-339](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-339.md) | in full |

The memos form a line by their own account. "Plain Talk" calls itself in part
a sequel to the frames memo, and K-lines complements "Plain Talk". The
filings declare that line as `extends:`, and *The Emotion Machine* extends
*The Society of Mind*.

- **"Plain Talk" does not claim to be first.** It presents the theory, then
  called "The Society of Minds", as unpublished work in progress with Papert.
  K-lines credits one principle to their 1974 lectures, which were not seen.
  Priority is left open.
- **The jokes memo is titled "Jokes and the Logic of the Cognitive
  Unconscious".** The Freud-like title in circulation is wrong.
- ***The Emotion Machine* disagrees with Damasio** ([LIT-383](../../record/literature.d/LIT-383.md) to [LIT-388](../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md)).
  - The draft treats the body as one more resource. It takes "the opposite
    view" to the bodily account.
  - It reverses the causal direction for Damasio's patient Elliot, without
    evidence.
  - It makes feelings depend on self-models, where Damasio has feelings
    ground consciousness.
  - The two agree only that emotion-free reasoning is a myth.

Seven of the eight are unread, because the lawful full texts were not

list somebody actually saw, and what was tried.

- **[NOTE-136](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-136.md)'s "argues nearly the opposite" is not yet supported.** As
  [NOTE-136](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-136.md) itself reports, Hofstadter's essay gives a criterion (a Turing
  test of consistent understanding suffices) and a forecast (conscious AI
  "perhaps even by 2033"). Neither says present systems are conscious. He
  plainly dissents from the editors' framing, but "opposite" needs the essay
  read. [NOTE-136](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-136.md) is left unchanged until it is.
- ***Fluid Concepts* reprints the 1992 critique as its chapter 4**, and its
  chapters 5–6 are on Copycat.

## Possible topic words, not added

Two readers proposed words, and neither was needed: `cognition` holds every
work. They are recorded here for when a second line of work wants them:

- `knowledge-representation`: frames, scripts, semantic networks and default
  reasoning, read outside machine learning.
- `cognitive-architecture`: designs for a whole mind, natural or artificial.

*2026-10-02 00:21:43 · curation · record*

The owner asked for a bridge between Minsky's society of mind ([LIT-429](../../record/literature.d/LIT-429.md)
and the memos) and Schwitzgebel's "If materialism is true, the United States
is probably conscious" ([LIT-159](../../record/literature.d/LIT-159.md), [NOTE-131](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-131.md)). Schwitzgebel was already held.
Eleven works came in to fill the seam between them, and one THEORY,
[THEORY-043](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md), states the bridge.

| Putnam, "Psychological Predicates" (1967) | [LIT-396](../../record/literature.d/LIT-396.md), [NOTE-335](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-335.md) | skim (excerpt) | the anti-nesting stipulation |
| Block, "Troubles with Functionalism" (1978) | [LIT-407](../../record/literature.d/LIT-407.md), [NOTE-366](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-366.md) | in full | the China brain; first critic of anti-nesting |
| Lycan, "Form, Function, and Feel" (1981) | [LIT-419](../../record/literature.d/LIT-419.md) | no: Deferred | homuncular functionalism |
| Brooks, "Intelligence without representation" (1991) | [LIT-436](../../record/literature.d/LIT-436.md), [NOTE-351](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-351.md) | in full | decomposition, built and run |
| List & Pettit, *Group Agency* (2011) | [LIT-391](../../record/literature.d/LIT-391.md) | no: Deferred | group agency |
| Huebner, *Macrocognition* (2013) | [LIT-426](../../record/literature.d/LIT-426.md) | no: Deferred | collective minds |
| Oizumi, Albantakis & Tononi, IIT 3.0 (2014) | [LIT-445](../../record/literature.d/LIT-445.md), [NOTE-365](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-365.md) | in full | the exclusion postulate |
| Kammerer, reply to Schwitzgebel (2015) | [LIT-409](../../record/literature.d/LIT-409.md), [NOTE-362](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-362.md) | in full | a functional anti-nesting principle |
| List, "What is it like to be a group agent?" (2016) | [LIT-401](../../record/literature.d/LIT-401.md), [NOTE-340](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-340.md) | in full | group agency yes, group experience no |
| Levin, "The computational boundary of a 'self'" (2019) | [LIT-439](../../record/literature.d/LIT-439.md), [NOTE-341](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-341.md) | in full | nested selves at every scale |

**The bridge, as the readings support it.** Agency is granted in both
directions, by Block, List and Levin. The dispute is over experience. Every
way to accept Minsky's downward move while refusing Schwitzgebel's upward
one takes one of two routes:

- an anti-nesting principle, stipulated by Putnam, postulated by IIT, or
  weakly justified by Kammerer;
- an architectural criterion, which would have to spare a loosely coupled
  society of mind while excluding a nation.

Nobody here computes that difference. [THEORY-043](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md) is `Proposed`, and its
`promote_when` names the criterion that would settle it.

**Corrections to [NOTE-131](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-131.md) the readings found**, held in the readings and
not yet applied to [NOTE-131](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-131.md) itself:

- Block's counterexample to Putnam is elementary-particle people, not tiny
  people as neurons.
- Schwitzgebel's Putnam "quotation" is a paraphrase, and the first
  appearance is 1967, from a 1965 colloquium.
- The "Brooks (1986)" of the group-mind tradition is D. H. M. Brooks, not
  Rodney Brooks.

Kammerer's reader also found that [NOTE-188](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-188.md)'s gloss of his principle omits
its second condition.

**Next on this seam, not filed:** Schwitzgebel's reply to Kammerer
(*Philosophia* 44, 2016) and D. H. M. Brooks, "Group minds" (1986). Reading
Huebner would most likely move the THEORY.

## What changed in the record's threads

- **[THEORY-043](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md)** (the bridge from Minsky to Schwitzgebel) gains a
  section from these readings:
  - Dennett's discharge of homunculi explains why the downward move is
    licensed for intelligence and the upward one is not.
  - Chalmers's organisational invariance narrows the dispute to
    architecture.
  - The combination-problem paper reaches the account's two routes
    independently.
  - Two new candidates for a principled line are named: Dennett &
    Kinsbourne against a conscious central part, and Chalmers 2019's
    "not mediated" condition. Neither yet meets `promote_when`.
  - Searle and "Quining Qualia" are recorded as refusing the framing.
- **[THEORY-023](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-023.md)** (AI consciousness) gains candidate evidence, not yet
  added to it:
  - Chalmers's LLM paper, a fifth prior: under 10% for current models, 25%
    or more within a decade;
  - footnote 26 of the meta-problem paper;
  - Turing's other-minds reply;
  - Searle's concession that behaviour licenses ascription until the
    program is known.

## Corrections the readings found

Each is held in the reading that found it; none is applied to the older
note it concerns.

- **Adams & Aizawa 2001 does not contain "coupling-constitution
  fallacy".** The phrase is from their later work; [NOTE-180](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-180.md) misattributes
  it.
- **Clark's 2005 quotation of the parity principle differs from [LIT-097](../../record/literature.d/LIT-097.md)'s
  text.**
- **Chalmers's fading-qualia paper misdates Block** (1980/1981; it is 1978).
  It also says Block finds group minds "bizarre", which Block's n. 19
  disclaims.
- **Levin's "Chalmers 2013" is *Panpsychism and Panprotopsychism*, not the
  combination paper.**
- **"Artificial Intelligence as Philosophy and as Psychology" appeared first
  in *Brainstorms* (1978), not in Ringle (1979).**

- Zuboff, "The Story of a Brain".

abstract; [NOTE-362](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-362.md) v2 and [THEORY-043](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md) v2 take the reply in. The Adams &
Aizawa draft lists a December 2005 paper as under review and already names
the "coupling–constitution fallacy", so [NOTE-180](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-180.md) v4 dates the name to late
2005 rather than to "later work".

## How the record stood on the self

`identity` carried 39 works about three different things: the identity and
individuation of things (structural realism, quasi-sets, the Yoneda lemma),
biological individuality, and personal identity and the self. A reader
looking for the self met quasi-set theory first. No THEORY touched the
self, and the personal-identity literature the record's cognitive-science
and AI readings answer to was almost entirely missing: no Locke, Hume,
Parfit, Williams, Lewis, Olson, Schechtman, Strawson, Gallagher, Zahavi or
Metzinger.

## The vocabulary

- **`self-and-personhood`** ([ADR-015](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-015.md)) holds what a self or a person is and
  what makes one persist. Fifteen existing works took it, and every self
  filing above leads with it.
- **`identity` became `individuation`** ([ADR-015](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-015.md), at the owner's
  suggestion). With the self moved out, what was left was the
  individuation of things, and "identity" read alone invites the personal
  sense. The 41 bearers changed in place.
- **`phenomenology`** ([ADR-016](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-016.md)) is for the first-person description of
  experience as a method. A filing agent proposed it for Zahavi, and the
  owner accepted. Six works carry it, none first.

## For the next person

Three agents filed the self literature into one checkout at once, each
running only `luria new`. A `luria link --fix` run by the integrator spells
targets into their in-progress files too; that is harmless, since it only
spells links. Integrating each batch in a separate worktree at HEAD, with
`repair`, `link --fix`, `index` and `lint` run there, kept every commit
linted without waiting for the slowest agent.

## What it did to the record

[THEORY-043](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md) v3 takes a scoping note from Ritchie and Epstein: groups with
the same members can be distinct, only organised groups are concrete
wholes, and a group's facts may depend on non-members. So any criterion
for group minds has to say which group it is applied to. None of these
readings discusses group experience, so the account itself does not move.

The filing agent for Haslanger and Ásta noted that nothing in the
vocabulary names gender, race or feminist philosophy, and proposed
`feminist-philosophy`. Two works do not make a topic. It is left for a
filing that brings more.

## Prigogine's programme and the canonical systems (7)

| work | filed | read |

The lecture is explicit that the minimum-entropy-production theorem holds
only in the strictly linear regime near equilibrium, and that far from it
behaviour can be "even opposite": Bénard convection raises entropy
production. Cross & Hohenberg quote Glansdorff & Prigogine conceding that
"the search for a universal kinetic potential has proved to be
unsuccessful", and correct the lecture's history: Bénard's own hexagons
were driven by surface tension, not buoyancy.

Maximum entropy production is contested as these texts show it: Kleidon,
its advocate, writes that "no one would argue that MEP is well
established", and Grinstein & Linsker show Dewar's derivation holds only

Still et al. cite them only as background, and take their setup from
Crooks 1998, which the record does not hold. Jarzynski's dissipated work
and Still et al.'s are different quantities, and both notes say so.

## What it did to the record

[LIT-192](../../record/literature.d/LIT-192.md)'s demarcation question is still open. The canonical dissipative
structures are the counter-examples any definition of life must exclude,
and none of the readable texts excludes them on principle. Friston alone
names the candle flame, in one sentence. The two accounts that claim a
real line, Deacon's teleodynamics and Moreno & Mossio's closure, are
unread. [NOTE-094](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-094.md) v3 says so.

Perunov, Marsland & England and [THEORY-026](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md) use "adaptation" in opposite
senses (dissipating more against dissipating less), and the record should
keep them apart. Friston's free energy is variational, so he is not a
second source for [THEORY-026](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md), nor for the equivalence Seth ([LIT-135](../../record/literature.d/LIT-135.md))
assumes.

## For the next person

Moreno & Mossio's *Biological Autonomy* has an authors' CC BY-NC deposit
in HAL (hal-01151449) behind a bot challenge aimed at scrapers; a person
can open it lawfully, and it is the cheapest way to answer the
demarcation question. Crooks 1998 (J. Stat. Phys. 90:1481) is the paper
[THEORY-026](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md)'s source is actually built on, and is not yet in the record.

they point to is a 2020 thalassemia article that carries Bandura's DOI by
mistake.

## What the batch says together

Two independent lines say that a treatment working is not evidence for
its theory of change: Beckian CBT (Salkovskis et al., [LIT-538](../../record/literature.d/LIT-538.md)) and
contextual behavioural science (Hofmann & Hayes, [LIT-544](../../record/literature.d/LIT-544.md)). Only
specific, ordered mediation is evidence, and moving the theorised process
without moving the outcome disconfirms the theory. Three lines, none
citing the others, put self-reinforcing maintenance loops where a latent
cause would be: Borsboom's among symptoms ([LIT-547](../../record/literature.d/LIT-547.md)), Salkovskis et
al.'s between threat appraisals and safety-seeking, and Kendler's across
levels ([LIT-539](../../record/literature.d/LIT-539.md)). Salkovskis et al. call their common mechanism
"psychological flexibility", but cite none of the ACT literature that uses
the term. Nothing is filed as a THEORY yet. The proposals are in the pull
request.

## For the next person

These are the cheapest openings for a human with library access:

- Lazarus 1991, *American Psychologist* 46(8):819–834. It would make
  appraisal theory readable in the record.
- Macri & Rogge 2024, *Clinical Psychology Review* 110:102432. It is the
  test of whether ACT's processes change before outcomes do.
- Engel 1977, *Science* 196:129–136. It is the canonical biopsychosocial
  citation.

## Theories from the psychopathology batch, and self-determination theory

*2026-10-03 05:29:54 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: THEORY-044 THEORY-045 THEORY-047 THEORY-048 THEORY-049 THEORY-050 THEORY-051 THEORY-052 THEORY-054 THEORY-055 THEORY-056 THEORY-057 THEORY-058 THEORY-029 THEORY-040 LIT-556 — Proposed theories and Unavailable works, listed as filed -->

The owner asked for theories to be filed from the psychopathology, emotion
and psychotherapy batch ([ADR-021](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-021.md)). The owner especially wanted ones that
support or engage the record's philosophy-of-mind holdings, and asked
explicitly for an account of ACT's theory of the self. Midway the owner
asked how the record covered self-determination theory, and then asked
for it to be filed in the same contribution. The record held none, so
`motivation` was added ([ADR-023](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-023.md)).

## Fifteen theories

One is Active. [THEORY-053](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-053.md) holds that a treatment's efficacy is not
evidence for its theory of change. It is close to a logical point, and
both wings of CBT state it while disagreeing about mechanism. The other
fourteen are Proposed, each with what would settle it.

**Emotion and affect.**

- [THEORY-045](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-045.md): felt affect is the body's regulatory state. Barrett
  ([LIT-542](../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md)) and Damasio & Carvalho ([LIT-388](../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md)) agree on that much. They
  disagree on whether what is felt is a prediction or a map, and on where
  it is generated. The theory records the disagreement instead of
  choosing. On the question of AI consciousness ([THEORY-023](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-023.md)), it shows
  where the open question lies for affect.
- [THEORY-057](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-057.md) (emotion categories are perceiver-constructed
  populations) and [THEORY-055](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-055.md) (appraisal elicits action readiness)
  are declared `rivals`.
- [THEORY-056](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-056.md): regulation is not a process separate from generation.
  The two rival theories of emotion agree on it, and Deci & Ryan argue
  against it.

**Psychopathology.**

- [THEORY-048](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-048.md): biology implements psychological function and does not
  replace it. It is tied to Pernu on mental causation and to the
  record's emergence holdings.
- [THEORY-058](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-058.md): disorders persist through self-reinforcing loops.
  Three traditions say this without citing one another.
- [THEORY-050](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-050.md): psychological inflexibility is transdiagnostic.

**The self.**

- [THEORY-044](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-044.md) gives RFT's three selves. Self-as-content is the
  narrative self. Self-as-context is what Hume could not find and what
  Metzinger calls the transparent perspective. The open seam is
  Gallagher's minimal self: if self-as-context were that, RFT's claim
  that it is learned would contradict the neonatal evidence.
- [THEORY-051](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-051.md): strengthening self-as-context is how ACT helps. It
  extends [THEORY-050](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-050.md). Nothing in the record tests this directly.

**Motivation.**

- [THEORY-054](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-054.md): autonomy is graded integration, not order. It agrees
  with [THEORY-029](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-029.md)'s negative claim but does not escape Velleman.
- [THEORY-047](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-047.md): a regulation's history of acquisition fixes how
  autonomous it is. This is a historical condition with experimental
  support, beside [THEORY-040](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-040.md).
- [THEORY-049](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-049.md): whether a reward undermines intrinsic motivation
  depends on whether it is experienced as controlling or as information
  about competence.
- [THEORY-046](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-046.md): expected engagement-contingent rewards lower free
  choice.
- [THEORY-052](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-052.md): need frustration is transdiagnostic. It can hold
  alongside [THEORY-050](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-050.md).

## Model comparison and Fisher geometry

*2026-10-03 13:15:58 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-354 — Unavailable, listed as filed -->

The owner sent sixteen readings that run from evidence-based model
comparison to the Fisher geometry of trained networks. They asked that any
already held be checked and the rest filed here, in both records where the
anthology held one.

## The check against both records

Only one was held anywhere: Watanabe's 2009 book, here, as a Deferred seed
([LIT-354](../../record/literature.d/LIT-354.md)). The anthology holds later Shampoo and K-FAC derivatives and SAE
work, but none of these papers. So nothing needed a second, [ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md) entry.

The owner's question here, which the anthology does not ask, is how one
line of inquiry connects:

- Bayesian model comparison: evidence, Savage–Dickey, model reduction,
  singular learning theory;
- the spectra of the Fisher information in trained models, the object
  their thresholding acts on;
- the kernel and feature eigenstructure beside them.

The machine-learning works carry `anthology-candidate` ([ADR-005](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-005.md)).

The check also found that CLAUDE.md still said "nothing is filed in
both", eight days after [ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md) narrowed that rule. The map was corrected
in the same contribution. Two topics were added for the line ([ADR-026](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-026.md)):
`model-comparison` and `information-geometry`.

## What was filed

Eighteen LITs and seventeen NOTEs. All are read except Dickey 1971, which
Project Euclid serves only behind a bot challenge.

- **Model comparison:**
  - Wagenmakers et al. on Savage–Dickey;
  - Friston & Penny on post hoc model selection;
  - Bayesian model reduction. It has three authors, Friston, Parr and
    Zeidman, not "et al.";
  - Smith et al. on structure learning, which adds and removes levels of a
    factor rather than whole factors;
  - MacKay's evidence framework;
  - Watanabe's WBIC paper, read in place of the book, which now names it.
- **Fisher geometry and spectra:**
  - Amari's natural gradient, from the author's RIKEN deposit;
  - K-FAC and Shampoo;
  - Papyan's three spectra papers. Both 1811.07062 and 1901.08244 were
    filed, because both carry the class structure;
  - neural collapse.
- **Kernel spectra and features:**
  - Bietti & Bach, which is "Deep Equals Shallow", not Bietti & Mairal;
  - Cao et al.;
  - Basri et al.;
  - Gemma Scope.

## What the readings say together

The filing agents found the links that make this one line, and each
marked them as its own reading where the papers do not draw them:

- Savage–Dickey is the point-mass case of Bayesian model reduction.
- The Occam factor is a volume ratio, set by curvature in regular models
  and by the real log canonical threshold (RLCT) in singular ones.
- Amari's efficiency result needs an invertible Fisher, the same
  regularity WBIC's account drops.
- Papyan finds the Fisher's top outliers in class-mean directions, and
  K-FAC's single Kronecker factor misplaces them.
- The NTK Gram matrix and the Gauss–Newton Fisher share their non-zero
  spectrum. So the harmonic-degree blocks of the kernel papers should
  appear as Fisher plateaus, and a spectral threshold is well posed only
  between blocks.

## For the next person

- **Dickey 1971.** A human with a browser can open it at Project Euclid
  and promote the entry.
- **Supervised structure learning.** Friston et al. (arXiv 2311.10300) is
  the broader paper on adding and removing whole factors. It was named
  and not filed.

## Neural dynamics, animal consciousness and Orch OR biophysics

*2026-10-03 15:15:00 · curation · record*

The owner sent eight readings: four on large-scale neural dynamics and the
neural correlates of seeing, and four on theories of consciousness and the
biophysics that Orch OR leans on. None was held in either record, so
nothing needed an [ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md) second entry, and none carries an instruction
for machine-learning practice.

## What was filed

Eight LITs and six NOTEs. Six works were read in full from lawful copies:
publisher open access, PMC, arXiv, or a co-author's own deposit.

- **Neural dynamics:**
  - Verzhbinsky et al. 2026 on co-ripple co-firing ([LIT-633](../../record/literature.d/LIT-633.md));
  - Xu et al. 2023 on interacting cortical spirals ([LIT-638](../../record/literature.d/LIT-638.md)). It
    `rivals` the discrete-substate account of Vohryzek et al. ([LIT-080](../../record/literature.d/LIT-080.md)).
    Neither tests the other, and the two may yet prove to be two levels of

  - Vishne et al. 2023 on sustained conscious visual perception
    ([LIT-644](../../record/literature.d/LIT-644.md)).
- **Consciousness and biophysics:**
  - Babcock et al. 2024 on tryptophan superradiance ([LIT-645](../../record/literature.d/LIT-645.md)). The
    paper never mentions consciousness, and the record does not read it as
    evidence for Orch OR;
  - Maldarelli & Güntürkün 2025, "Conscious birds" ([LIT-650](../../record/literature.d/LIT-650.md));
  - Newen & Montemayor 2025, the ALARM theory ([LIT-626](../../record/literature.d/LIT-626.md)). It `rivals`
    Veit ([LIT-105](../../record/literature.d/LIT-105.md)) on what consciousness was first for.
- **Deferred, because no lawful full text exists:**
  - Muller et al. 2026, the traveling-waves review ([LIT-647](../../record/literature.d/LIT-647.md)). Its
    accepted manuscript opens in September 2027;
  - Derakhshani et al. 2022 on spontaneous radiation and Orch OR
    ([LIT-627](../../record/literature.d/LIT-627.md)). It is closed access.

## Theories

Seven, all Proposed. Each rests on one paper.

- [THEORY-088](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-088.md): slow cortical activity organised by interacting
  spiral defects, as in a pattern-forming medium. The title does not say
  "excitable": the paper's model is an oscillator lattice, and the
  evidence does not decide between the two kinds of medium.
- [THEORY-097](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-097.md): long-range forebrain coordination carried by co-ripples.
- [THEORY-102](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-102.md): a stable ventral population code while amplitude
  decays, with prefrontal content arriving at onset only.
- [THEORY-090](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-090.md): basic affective consciousness is subcortical and
  serves as an alarm. It extends [THEORY-045](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-045.md).
- [THEORY-101](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-101.md): Veit's valence-as-currency account, filed so that the
  ALARM rivalry has a counterpart. The two `rivals` each other.
- [THEORY-100](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-100.md): conscious report does not need laminar cortex (corvid
  NCL).
- [THEORY-099](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-099.md): collective superradiant states in microtubule
  tryptophan networks. It says explicitly that this is not evidence for
  Orch OR.

One candidate was declined: "Orch OR in its simplest gravity-collapse form
is excluded by spontaneous-radiation bounds". Its only source is the
Deferred Derakhshani paper. The record holds no reading of the underground
collapse test (Donadi et al. 2020), and Gao ([LIT-121](../../record/literature.d/LIT-121.md)) argues against
Penrose's collapse on theoretical grounds, not with radiation bounds.

## Gaps noticed

## Ned Block, the global workspace, and homeostatic feeling

*2026-10-03 16:00:00 · curation · record*

The owner asked to improve the record's coverage of Ned Block, which held
only "Troubles with Functionalism" ([LIT-407](../../record/literature.d/LIT-407.md)). Notes already cited "Block
1995", "Block 1987", "Block 2009" and "Block 2023" with nothing to point
to. The anthology holds no Block, so nothing needed an [ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md) second
entry. One work, "Psychologism and Behaviorism", carries
`anthology-candidate`: the anthology's evaluation topic could hold what it
says a behavioural test cannot establish.

Block's own site (nedblock.us) links his author copies of every work
filed. Each was read in full from those copies, except *The Border Between
Seeing and Thinking*, which was read through its PPR précis and seeded
Deferred.

## Two groups

- **Consciousness.** Seven papers, 1995 to 2019. They make one argument:
  access and phenomenal consciousness are distinct, phenomenology overflows
  access, and the neural basis is sensory rather than prefrontal. The 2007
  paper rivals Dennett ([LIT-431](../../record/literature.d/LIT-431.md), [LIT-433](../../record/literature.d/LIT-433.md)).
- **Functionalism, meaning and perception.** Block & Fodor 1972,
  Blockhead, two-factor conceptual role semantics, "Inverted Earth",
  "Mental Paint", the mind as software, and the précis on the border
  between seeing and thinking.

## The global workspace, filed beside Block

The owner then added two readings:

- **Mashour et al. 2020.** The record had no global-workspace source until
  now. The review rivals Block's overflow paper and his no-report paper,
  and it rivals IIT.
- **Damasio & Damasio 2022.** It rivals both IIT and the workspace.

The Damasio essay's publisher page answers automated requests with a
challenge. It was reached only through a fetch tool that summarises
pages, so its NOTE is Skimmed rather than Read, and its quotes are
unchecked. Damasio & Damasio 2023 ([LIT-387](../../record/literature.d/LIT-387.md)) is still Deferred for the same
reason. Its abstract matches the 2022 essay's opening nearly sentence for
sentence.

## Theories

Four theories come from Block's consciousness papers:

- overflow;
- a sensory, not prefrontal, basis;
- the limits of no-report designs;
- the confounded inference from a deficit to a function.

[THEORY-023](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-023.md) takes Block 2002 and Block 2009 as sources.

Candidates not yet filed:

- psychologism;
- the failure of long-arm accounts of experience;
- two-factor content;
- global availability by ignition;
- consciousness supplied by homeostatic feeling.

<a id="20261003200000"></a>

## Mode connectivity, loss landscapes and model merging

*2026-10-03 20:00:00 · curation · record*

The owner sent 33 readings. Most are on mode connectivity and model
merging; the rest are on statistical-mechanics and random-matrix accounts
of generalization, and on where in a network generalization is carried.

Nucleation held none of them. The anthology holds two, Git Re-Basin
([ANTH-LIT-333](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-333.md)) and Entezari et al. ([ANTH-LIT-251](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-251.md)), which are filed here as
[ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md) second readings. This record's question is how the solutions
training finds are arranged in weight space, and what that arrangement
says about what a trained network is. Every work carries
`anthology-candidate`.

No topic covered that question, so `loss-landscapes` was added
([ADR-027](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-027.md)).

## What was filed

33 LITs and 33 NOTEs, every one read from a lawful copy: 31 from arXiv, one
from PMLR, and one from the NeurIPS Bayesian Deep Learning workshop site.
Three LITs are Proposed rather than Active, because the reading found
them too thin to stand on:

- Yao et al. on generative and contrastive models: one pair of modes per
  model, and inconsistent numbers;
- Li et al. on GNNs: no proofs, and an unfilled placeholder in the text;
- Zhang & Blei on the ELBO: no results.

The groups were:

- **Foundations** (8): Garipov, Draxler, Frankle, Kuditipudi, Entezari,
  Git Re-Basin, Ferbach, Benton.
- **Extensions** (9): mechanistic connectivity, layerwise feature
  connectivity, geodesic and star-shaped connectivity, the symmetry
  account, star domains, transformers, mixtures of experts, and
  adversarial robustness.
- **Merging and other settings** (9): weight-space regions of fine-tuned
  models, ZipIt!, TIES-Merging, continual and class-incremental learning,
  generative models, GNNs, federated learning, and the ELBO.
- **Landscape theory and generalization** (7): Yang et al.'s taxonomy,
  Martin & Mahoney, Liao et al. and Dereziński et al. on double descent,
  and three papers on where in depth generalization is carried.

## Findings for the anthology, reported not edited

- **[ANTH-LIT-251](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-251.md) / [NOTE-131](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-131.md) (Entezari) state a "no dead neurons"
  condition.** The paper's only theorem (3.1) has no such condition. It is
  for one-hidden-layer networks at random initialization, and it bounds
  the output difference, not a loss barrier. The paper's own permutation
  search did not lower barriers for VGG or ResNet.
- **[ANTH-LIT-333](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-333.md) / [NOTE-116](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-116.md) (Git Re-Basin) describe weight matching as
  greedy, layer by layer.** The paper uses coordinate descent over all
  layers, and its Appendix A.7 argues against greedy single-pass matching.
  It also has a merge-many algorithm. The quoted figures ("within 1–2%",
  "2–5×", "H > 10,000") were not found in the text.
- **[ANTH-THEORY-010](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/theory.d/THEORY-010.md) (most of the barrier is permutation).** Its
  promote_when asks for a transformer demonstration. Theus et al. give
  one. Permutation alignment alone removes 63–90% of the transformer
  barrier, which supports the theory, but reaching zero needs an
  orthogonal map on the residual stream, which is not a permutation. Lubana et al. bound the theory with
  barriers that reflect real differences in mechanism.
- **[ANTH-SOTA-217](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/practices.d/SOTA-217.md) (align permutations before averaging).** ZipIt! narrows
  it to models trained on the same task.
- **[ANTH-SOTA-012](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/practices.d/SOTA-012.md) (sharpness correlates with test error).** Yang et al.
  give counterexamples.
- **The anthology holds no task-arithmetic paper.** TIES-Merging's main
  baseline is therefore absent from both records.

## Gaps noticed

- **Vocabulary.** There is no word for statistical mechanics of learning,
  random-matrix theory, ensembling, pruning, or adversarial robustness.
  TIES-Merging argues about parameter updates, not connectivity. A second
  work like it would meet [ADR-027](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-027.md)'s condition for a separate
  `model-merging` word.
- **Unfilled works the readings lean on:**
  - Martin & Mahoney's heavy-tailed self-regularization (1810.01075),
    which Papyan ([LIT-617](../../record/literature.d/LIT-617.md)) names;
  - Fort & Jastrzębski on "tunnels";
  - Juneja et al. 2023;
  - Annesi et al. 2023;
  - Seung, Sompolinsky & Tishby 1992;
  - task arithmetic.

    [LIT-694](../../record/literature.d/LIT-694.md));

## Theories

Two theories, Proposed:

## Posani et al. 2026, a second reading

*2026-10-04 04:00:00 · curation · record*

The owner asked for Posani, Wang, Muscinelli, Paninski & Fusi (2026),
"Rarely categorical, highly separable representations along the cortical
hierarchy", to be read and filed here. The anthology already holds it as
[ANTH-LIT-696](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-696.md), so this is an [ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md) second reading ([LIT-708](../../record/literature.d/LIT-708.md), with a
read NOTE).

The anthology reads the paper for what cortex implies about concept
geometry in machine learning. This record re-reads it for a different
question: do neurons within a cortical area form discrete functional types
or a mixed-selectivity continuum, and what does that do to the
separability of what the area represents? The paper is not read as
evidence about abstraction, because it measures separability, not
generalisation. No `anthology-candidate` flag is added, because the work
is already held there.

One Proposed theory, [THEORY-124](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-124.md): neurons within a single mouse
cortical area rarely form discrete functional types, yet the task
conditions the area distinguishes are linearly separable in nearly every
way. Its scope is the IBL task and the paper's categoricality test. The
contrast with neural collapse ([THEORY-083](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md)) is explained in prose. The two
senses of "categorical" differ: here it means neuron types, and there it
means the arrangement of conditions.

## Corals as composite systems

*2026-10-04 17:00:00 · curation · record*

The owner sent four coral readings, each with a note on why it matters.
The notes are the questions this record reads the papers for. Neither
record held any of the four.

All four were read in full, from PMC copies or, for Hughes, the
publisher's PDF posted on a Bennington College course page. Hughes is in
Elsevier's open archive.

Papers 1 and 2 are reviews and are weighed as reviews. Papers 3 and 4 are
experiments.

## How each paper meets the owner's note

- **Goulet et al. 2020 ([LIT-709](../../record/literature.d/LIT-709.md)).** The brief named Stévenne et al.;
  the paper with this title is Goulet et al. It makes the conceptual case
  for the holobiont as a composite system. The physiological case is thin:
  its one "not the sum of its parts" result comes from a sea anemone, not
  a coral. "Establishes" is too strong.
- **Boilard et al. 2020 ([LIT-712](../../record/literature.d/LIT-712.md)).** It is a proposed account of
  breakdown and reorganisation, as the owner says. Its use for the
  regulatory-disruption example is its account of who regulates whom. The
  authors themselves say microbial causation is untested.
- **Kaniewska et al. 2015 ([LIT-710](../../record/literature.d/LIT-710.md)).**
  - **The environmental cue is shown experimentally.** The natural
    night-light pattern is necessary, not moonlight specifically.
  - **The endogenous cascade is correlational.**
  - **No coordination between colonies is tested.** The "coordination" is
    colonies responding to a shared cue.
- **Hughes et al. 2007 ([LIT-711](../../record/literature.d/LIT-711.md)).** It supports the note, and more
  strongly than stated: even established colonies survived better where
  herbivores grazed. Its limits:
  - plot scale;
  - all large fishes excluded, not herbivores alone;
  - the phase shift reversed within 30 days.

## Theories

Three Proposed theories:

- **Bleaching ([THEORY-130](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-130.md)).** Bleaching is the breakdown of a
  regulated host–symbiont exchange, reached by more than one route. The
  microbiome clause was declined as untested.
- **Spawning ([THEORY-129](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-129.md)).** The night-light regime is necessary for
  spawning, and a signalling programme tracks it. The cascade is held as a
  hypothesis.
- **Reef recovery ([THEORY-128](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-128.md)).** Recovery after bleaching depends on
  herbivorous fishes keeping macroalgae down.

No relation is declared, because none of the papers cites or tests
anything the record holds. [THEORY-072](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md) sets the holobiont boundary aside,
and [THEORY-111](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md)'s "spawning" is the machine-learning term.

## Vocabulary

`ecology` joins the topics ([ADR-028](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-028.md)). Chronobiology was considered and
deferred: one paper is too few to name a topic.

<a id="20261005062829"></a>

## Sources an essay on will cites

*2026-10-05 06:28:29 · curation · record*

The owner's essay on organizational will (§§5–9) cites four bodies of work
the record did not hold: Aubin on viability, Longino on social knowledge,
Ostrom on polycentric governance, and "research on epistemic networks".
The owner asked for them to be filed. Neither record held any of them.

## What was read and what was not

Each author's main book is closed, so each was registered `Deferred` from
Crossref, and a shorter lawful work by the same author was read in its
place:

- **Aubin.** *Viability Theory* (1991) is behind Springer's bot challenge,
  and the HAL copy of a later paper is behind one too. Neither was passed.
  His 1999 UC Davis mini-course notes are on arXiv. Their introduction and
  chapters 1–2 give the definitions first-hand: viable, invariant, the
  viability kernel and the capture basin.
- **Longino.** Her two books are closed. Her own SEP entry, which she wrote,
  states the argument and the four community norms.
- **Ostrom.** *Governing the Commons* is closed. The Nobel lecture, read in
  full from the Nobel Foundation's PDF, gives the design principles in
  their updated form and defines polycentricity.
- **Epistemic networks.** The essay names no work, so the founding papers
  were filed: Zollman 2007 and 2010, his 2013 survey, all from his own
  site, and the robustness critique by Rosenstock, Bruner & O'Connor
  (2017), from O'Connor's site. Longino's entry pointed to the critique.

## What the readings say about the essay

- **Aubin.** The notes define viability but never compare it with
  stability. Their "stability properties" are about limits of sets. The
  essay's §6.1 contrast follows from the definitions, but it is the
  essay's step. It also needs the essay to say what the constraint set is
  for an organization.
- **Longino.** Her norms concern how a community comes to know, not how it
  decides. The essay's list of what makes criticism "consequential" maps
  onto her norms, and uptake is the one it most needs. Naming them would
  turn §8.2's suggestion into a test.
- **Ostrom.** Her principles describe users governing a resource they
  share. A firm governing itself is a further step. Her own last lesson is
  "no panaceas", so polycentricity is not good in itself.
- **Epistemic networks.** The essay's sentence is as strong as the evidence
  allows, and no stronger. Sparse networks help only where inquiry is hard.
  Even there, Rosenstock et al. prefer an evidence standard to less
  communication. The robust result is Zollman's transient diversity.

One correction to the record's own summary of a source. Longino's entry
says Zollman "proves" the network result; the 2007 paper is a simulation
study. The NOTE on the entry records it.

## Theories

- [THEORY-134](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-134.md), Active. Viability is relative to a constraint set
  fixed apart from the dynamics; the viability kernel is its largest viable
  part. The contrast with stability is marked as not the source's.
- [THEORY-151](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-151.md), Proposed. Longino's account of objectivity
  through the four norms. Proposed because the books are unread and the
  norms' benefit is argued, not shown.
- [THEORY-149](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-149.md), Active. Users can govern commons durably, and lasting
  institutions share design principles, not rules. It says the principles
  are correlates, not causes, and are not shown for firms.
- [THEORY-143](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-143.md), Proposed. The Zollman effect, stated with
  Rosenstock et al.'s scope: it holds only where evidence is scarce.
- [THEORY-148](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-148.md), Proposed, extending the last. Transient diversity.

No new topic was needed. The networks papers take `epistemology`,
`network-science` and `philosophy-of-science`. Ostrom takes
`society-and-governance`, `social-science` and `game-theory`, and Aubin
takes `mathematics` and `complex-systems`.

## Supplements to the essay sources

*2026-10-05 06:49:39 · curation · record*

After the essay's own sources were filed, the owner asked what else the
record would need given the draft's weaknesses. I recommended six works,
and the owner said to file them. Each answers one gap:

- §5.3 has no criterion for an agentive explanation: List & Menzies.
- §§7–8 need corporate endorsement and corporate responsibility: Pettit.
- §6.1's stability-versus-viability claim has an older source: Holling.
- §5.4's lock-in needs a standard of evidence: Scheffer.
- §6 needs an empirical mechanism of precariousness: Rasmussen.
- §8.3 describes double-loop learning without naming it: Argyris.

## Copies

- **Read from lawful copies:**
  - List & Menzies, from List's LSE page;
  - Holling, from IIASA's authorised reprint;
  - Scheffer & Carpenter 2003, from a UC Berkeley course page;
  - Rasmussen, from DTU's repository.
- **Read in place of the original:** Pettit's 2017 chapter "The
  Conversable, Responsible Corporation", from a manuscript the European
  University Institute posted for his master class. *Responsibility
  Incorporated* (2007) could not be reached, since SSRN blocks this client,
  so it is registered.
- **Registered, read in a follow-up:** Scheffer et al. 2001 (Nature) had no
  lawful open copy. The 2003 review by two of its authors restates its
  theory and adds the evidential criteria, which are what the essay needs.
- **Argyris.**
  - The University of Georgia library copy of his 1991 HBR article carries
    a notice restricting it to enrolled students, plus a purchaser's
    watermark. It was discarded unused.
  - infed.org's account redirected in a loop.
  - His 2002 AMLE article is posted as a Word file by Action Design, a
    practice founded by his co-authors. Whether they may post it could not
    be confirmed, and I first left it unused. The owner then told me to use
    it, and it was read in full.
  - The 1977 HBR article stays registered only.

## What the readings say about the essay

- **List & Menzies give §5.3 its missing test.** A higher-level property is
  the cause, and its realizer is not, when the outcome would survive
  re-realizing it. For Northstar: would the outcome survive different
  people in the same roles? The answer can go either way, which is the
  point. Pernu ([LIT-147](../../record/literature.d/LIT-147.md)), already held, disputes the paper's main example.
  It is declared as a rival.
- **Pettit grounds corporate endorsement without a regress.** What makes an
  attitude the corporation's is authorised avowal plus procedures that
  correct its aggregate, not a higher-order attitude. He also attributes
  normative competence to corporations with an argument, which is what the
  essay's §8 does with Wolf without one. His fitness to be held responsible
  is not legitimacy, a distinction the essay already draws.
- **Holling is the older source for §6.1.** His resilience is not Aubin's
  viability. Resilience concerns a domain of attraction of the system's
  own dynamics, and viability concerns a constraint set given apart from
  them. A regime can be resilient while violating what it needs, which is
  protective lock-in exactly.
- **Scheffer & Carpenter set the bar for §5.4.** A persistent regime is
  not thereby a self-maintaining alternative state. It needs hysteresis,
  or a lasting shift after a temporary push, against the confound of slow
  return. Hughes's reef plots fail the test, and Lake Zwemlust's six clear
  years before slipping back show the confound.
- **Argyris names §8.3 and explains §8.5.** The essay's procedures for
  reconsidering the standards through which policies acquire authority
  are double-loop learning. His Model I and organizational defensive
  routines explain why an organization that espouses revisability fails
  at it: the inconsistency is made undiscussable, and so is the
  undiscussability. The evidence is his own workshops.
- **Rasmussen supplies §6's mechanism.** Under cost and effort gradients,
  work migrates toward the edge of acceptable performance, and redundant
  defences erode unseen. That is a different route from Northstar's
  lock-in, and the essay could use both.

## Theories

Six, one for each read work:
- [THEORY-133](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-133.md) (List & Menzies), Proposed;
- [THEORY-139](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-139.md) (Pettit), Proposed, extending [THEORY-127](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-127.md);
- [THEORY-132](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-132.md) (Holling), Active;
- [THEORY-136](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-136.md) (Scheffer & Carpenter), Active;
- [THEORY-144](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-144.md) (Rasmussen), Proposed.

No new topic was needed. Pettit's tags are `social-ontology`, `agency` and
`free-will`, the last because the topic's blurb names responsibility.

## Auditing the THEORY relations after presupposes

*2026-10-05 17:15:00 · curation · record*

The owner asked for the audit [ADR-029](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-029.md) left open: whether the theories that
name each other without a declared relation are missing one, and whether
any declared `extends` is really a `presupposes`.

## How

A script listed every unordered pair of theories where one names the
other outside backticks and neither declares a relation to the other: 250
pairs. For each pair it collected both titles, statuses and tags, and
every paragraph in which one names the other. Five agents classified 50
pairs each against the four definitions, defaulting to none. A sixth
judged the 60 declared relations, defaulting to keep. I read the text
behind every proposal before taking it.

The pair count includes five false matches. A citation of an anthology
theory renders as a link whose target path ends in that anthology code's
file name, so the regular expression `THEORY-\d+` found this record's code
inside the anthology's link, and a theory citing the anthology's [THEORY-004](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md)
looked as if it named this record's. A second run of the count has to drop
`ANTH-` citations and their targets first.

## What changed

- **Declared relations re-filed.** The audit of the 60 proposed 11
  `extends` → `presupposes`. I took seven: [THEORY-098](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-098.md) on [THEORY-103](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-103.md) (the
  mesh argument takes overflow as its premise, and says so), [THEORY-126](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-126.md) on
  [THEORY-055](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-055.md) (only the baseline clause needs appraisal), [THEORY-079](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-079.md) on
  [THEORY-087](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md), [THEORY-084](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md) on [THEORY-086](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-086.md), [THEORY-051](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-051.md) on [THEORY-050](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-050.md),
  [THEORY-002](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-002.md) on [THEORY-004](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md) and [THEORY-019](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-019.md) on [THEORY-017](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md). I kept four as
  `extends`, because each is a refinement or a widening of the same
  account rather than a claim about something else: [THEORY-121](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-121.md) on
  [THEORY-119](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-119.md) (guidance control is the positive half of the same claim
  about what responsibility requires), [THEORY-084](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md) on [THEORY-019](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-019.md) (it works
  the near-degenerate case that account leaves open), [THEORY-085](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-085.md) on
  [THEORY-078](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-078.md) (the class-mean outliers, followed into each layer) and
  [THEORY-090](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-090.md) on [THEORY-045](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-045.md) (it widens the same felt-affect account, in its
  own words).
- **Undeclared pairs.** The five agents proposed eight relations among
  the 250. I took four: [THEORY-077](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-077.md) presupposes [THEORY-054](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-054.md), [THEORY-115](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-115.md)
  presupposes [THEORY-114](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-114.md) and [THEORY-098](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-098.md) presupposes [THEORY-094](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-094.md), where the
  prose already said so or said the equivalent; and [THEORY-080](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-080.md) extends
  [THEORY-087](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md), which both documents' Connections stated and neither
  frontmatter declared. That last is the only plain oversight the audit
  found.
- **Proposals held back.** [THEORY-079](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-079.md) on [THEORY-081](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-081.md): the identity is what
  is being evaluated, not a premise. [THEORY-080](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-080.md) on [THEORY-086](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-086.md): the spectral
  fact is cited to [LIT-608](../../record/literature.d/LIT-608.md) directly. [THEORY-023](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-023.md) on [THEORY-092](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-092.md): the
  dependency is [THEORY-092](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-092.md)'s reading of [THEORY-023](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-023.md), and [THEORY-092](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-092.md) itself
  calls the bearing indirect. [THEORY-095](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-095.md) on [THEORY-089](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-089.md): the text draws an
  analogy, asking the functionalist to do for qualia what the two-factor
  theory does for content.

## What it says about the gap

Of the 245 real pairs, 241 stay undeclared, and in almost every case the document
already says why: a contrast, a parallel in another domain, a shared
source, a test not yet run. The gap the owner noticed is mostly the record
naming its neighbours, not the record failing to declare dependencies.

The part that was a real gap was the missing word. Most of the eleven
changes were already in the prose as "presupposes", "relies on" or "if it
fell, the argument would lose its premise", written before there was a
relation to declare them with.

<a id="20261006233728"></a>

## Design-rationale literature, as evidence for an argument scheme

*2026-10-06 23:37:28 · curation · record*

The owner is considering extending this record with argument-development
schemes: questions, claims and objections, in the manner of IBIS. Systems
of that kind have a fifty-year history, and most of it is a history of
not being used. The owner asked for that literature to be held here, as
the cautionary evidence the extension should be weighed against. The
failure modes it documents are these:

- the cost of capture falls on the author while the benefit goes to a
  later reader;
- users will not commit early to a formal structure;
- explicit structure has a cognitive overhead.

*Correction (2026-10-14, [NOTE-835](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-835.md)):* the first is not Grudin's
disparity as his 1994 article states it ([LIT-757](../../record/literature.d/LIT-757.md)). His is between people
in different roles at the same time, typically subordinate and manager,
not between an author and a later reader. The author-against-later-reader
form is closer to the design-rationale literature than to Grudin.

## What entered

Nine works, all registered and none read, so none has a NOTE ([ADR-025](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-025.md)):

- the notations and tools: Kunz and Rittel's 1970 working paper that
  introduced IBIS ([LIT-758](../../record/literature.d/LIT-758.md)), gIBIS ([LIT-762](../../record/literature.d/LIT-762.md)) and QOC
  ([LIT-763](../../record/literature.d/LIT-763.md));
- the success case: Conklin and Burgess Yakemovic's field trial, where an
  indented-text IBIS captured more than 2,300 decisions ([LIT-755](../../record/literature.d/LIT-755.md));
- the failure modes: Grudin on who does the work and who benefits
  ([LIT-759](../../record/literature.d/LIT-759.md), [LIT-757](../../record/literature.d/LIT-757.md)), Buckingham Shum and Hammond on what
  argumentation-based rationale is for and what it costs ([LIT-761](../../record/literature.d/LIT-761.md)),
  Lee's seven practical issues ([LIT-760](../../record/literature.d/LIT-760.md)), and Shipman and Marshall
  on why users will not formalize ([LIT-756](../../record/literature.d/LIT-756.md)).

The owner's list had eight. I added Conklin and Burgess Yakemovic,
because a body of failure evidence needs the case that did not fail, and
its abstract says what made the difference: capture with little
disruption of the normal process. I considered Grudin's chapter
"Evaluating opportunities for design capture" in Moran and Carroll's
*Design Rationale* (1996), and left it out: the only DOI is the 2020
reissue's, and the 1996 first appearance could not be dated from a
source.

No topic held these works, so `design-rationale` joins the topics
([ADR-030](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-030.md)). They are not anthology material. None is about machine
learning, and the anthology's nearest topic, `human-ai-interaction`, is
about working with a model. A grep of the anthology's record for every
author and DOI found nothing.

## How deeply

Every bibliographic detail was checked against Crossref, and the dates
follow [ADR-002](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-002.md). What the entries say about content comes from abstracts.
For Kunz and Rittel, the abstract came from the eScholarship scan, whose
title page was seen. For Grudin 1988, Buckingham Shum and Hammond, and
Shipman and Marshall, publishers refused this client. Their takeaways
come from secondary descriptions of the abstract, or, for Shipman and
Marshall, from an outline of the authors' web version, and each entry
says so. Two dates need a word:

- Grudin 1988 takes the CSCW '88 opening day, because Crossref gives
  the paper only a year.
- Grudin 1994 takes 2 January 1994, which is the date Crossref gives.

## What a reading should check

Whether the record's own experience bears out the first failure mode.
Here the person filing an entry is usually also its later reader, which
is the condition Grudin's argument says is missing. Buckingham Shum and
Hammond, and the Conklin and Burgess Yakemovic field trial, are the
places to look for whether that changes the cost-and-benefit balance.

## Four works cited by The Organization of Will

*2026-10-07 01:06:16 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-805 — Unavailable: registered unread, filed in this entry -->
<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-817 — Unavailable: registered unread, filed in this entry -->
<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-832 — Unavailable: registered unread, filed in this entry -->

The owner's essay "The Organization of Will" cites four works the record
did not hold. They entered because the essay cites them, and because the
record of the essay's argument, being built alongside it, needs something
to point at when a step of the argument leans on one of them. That is the
whole reason. None of them was read, and none was filed for its merit.

- Fraenkel, *The Dual State* (1941), [LIT-805](../../record/literature.d/LIT-805.md): the normative and the
  prerogative state, and authority over whether the rules apply.
- Ashby, *Design for a Brain* (1952; the essay cites the 1960 edition),
  [LIT-787](../../record/literature.d/LIT-787.md): ultrastability, regulation against alteration of the
  parameters of regulation.
- Canguilhem, *On the Normal and the Pathological* (1943; English 1978,
  reissued by Zone Books in 1989), [LIT-817](../../record/literature.d/LIT-817.md): health as a capacity to
  change norms. The essay uses it interpretively.
- Craver, *Explaining the Brain* (2007), [LIT-832](../../record/literature.d/LIT-832.md): constitutive against
  causal relevance, and mechanistic explanation.

## How deeply

Registered only. Each entry is `Deferred` and says in its body that it was
written from secondary description: Crossref's records and chapter lists,
the publisher's abstract (Fraenkel), library catalogues (Canguilhem) and
reviews (Craver). No NOTE or THEORY was filed.

## Choices worth knowing

- **Dates.** `published:` is the first appearance, as in [LIT-738](../../record/literature.d/LIT-738.md): 1941
  for Fraenkel (the English edition is the first publication), 1952 for
  Ashby, 1943 for Canguilhem's thesis. None of these has a known day, so
  each is the first of January. Craver's is Crossref's 2007-06-07.
- **DOIs are of later editions** where the first has none: Oxford's 2017
  reissue of Fraenkel, Springer's digitization of Ashby's 1960 edition,
  and Reidel's 1978 translation of Canguilhem. Canguilhem's title follows
  that DOI (*On the Normal and the Pathological*), not Zone's.
- **Tags.** Ashby has no cybernetics word in the vocabulary; he is filed
  under complex-systems, as Beer's Viable System Model works are, with
  behavioral-integration for the feedback-control reading of adaptation.
  Canguilhem is filed under philosophy-of-biology, since his question is
  what biological norms are; psychopathology-and-treatment was not used,
  because the book is about disease in general, not mental disorder.

## Boundary

None is held in the Anthology of the SOTA, and no anthology topic could
hold them: they are political and legal theory, cybernetics, philosophy of
medicine and philosophy of neuroscience. A grep of the anthology's record
for the authors, titles and DOIs found no entry.
