## How deeply

Nine readers worked in parallel, one per group, under a common brief. The
brief required a lawful full text, a reading on the work's own merits
without the manuscript, honesty about depth, and no NOTE where no copy
could be reached. Thirteen works now have a NOTE and are Active:

- **Read:** Shannon ([NOTE-591](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-591.md)), Blackwell ([NOTE-595](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-595.md)), Fritz
  ([NOTE-588](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-588.md)), Baez and Fong ([NOTE-598](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-598.md)), Dzhafarov and Kujala
  ([NOTE-600](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-600.md)), GenEval ([NOTE-593](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-593.md)), T2I-CompBench ([NOTE-592](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-592.md)),
  Composable Diffusion ([NOTE-597](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-597.md)), conditional Schrödinger bridges
  ([NOTE-589](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-589.md)), Griffiths and Kalish ([NOTE-599](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-599.md)), Saussure
  ([NOTE-594](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-594.md)), and Du Bois ([NOTE-590](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-590.md)).
- **Skimmed:** Kirby, Cornish and Smith ([NOTE-596](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-596.md)). PNAS, PubMed Central
  and the Edinburgh repository all refused this client. The reading went
  through a fetch tool that paraphrases, and its NOTE says so.

Nine works are still Deferred, now worded "filed, not read". Each LIT lists
the sources tried and what they returned. Most of these are books still in
copyright, which the Internet Archive lends but does not show and
HathiTrust searches but does not show: Austin, Goffman, Hofstadter, Gutt,
Lévi-Strauss, Bartlett, Cover and Thomas, and Torgersen. Wyner and Ziv is
an IEEE article with no repository copy.

Points the readers raised:

- **Sources worth noting.**
  - Saussure was read in French from Wikisource. That text follows the 1931
    third edition, because no scan of the 1916 edition was reachable.
  - Blackwell was read from page images on Project Euclid.
  - Du Bois was read from his own upload of the chapter, through a Wayback
    Machine capture, because ResearchGate refused the request.
  - Shannon was read from the Harvard posting of the corrected reprint.
- **Corrections to what was first filed from abstracts.**
  - Blackwell 1953 does not contain the whole "more informative iff garbling"
    equivalence. Part is Blackwell 1951 and part is Sherman and Stein. The
    1953 paper extends it to arbitrary outcome spaces and adds the
    two-state result.
  - Saussure says a sign as a whole is "un fait positif". Only signifier and
    signified, taken separately, are purely differential.
  - In Kirby, Cornish and Smith, compositional structure appeared only under
    the experimenter's homonym filter. Without it, the languages collapsed.
  - Composable Diffusion loses to its baseline at composing relations.
- **Claims the papers' own tables contradict.** The NOTEs record these.
  - CDSB: "lowest error consistently" in filtering.
  - T2I-CompBench: GORS's drop on unseen pairs, which the paper calls
    "slightly lower".
- **A finding against an older entry.** [LIT-317](../../record/literature.d/LIT-317.md) credits Shannon's 1949
  paper with the sampling theorem and the Gaussian capacity formula. Both
  are already in the 1948 paper. [NOTE-591](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-591.md) reports this, and [LIT-317](../../record/literature.d/LIT-317.md) is
  left for its own reading to correct.
- **Options for the owner.** Each of these is a separate work that could be
  filed on its own if wanted:
  - Goffman's "Footing" (Semiotica 1979), once a copy is supplied;
  - Lévi-Strauss's "The Structural Study of Myth" (Journal of American
    Folklore 1955);
  - Gutt's 1989 thesis.

THEORY: five new, all Proposed:

- [THEORY-156](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md), Blackwell's comparison of experiments;
- [THEORY-157](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-157.md), the sufficiency theorems in Markov categories;
- [THEORY-158](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-158.md), Noether for Markov processes;
- [THEORY-159](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-159.md), linguistic value;
- [THEORY-155](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-155.md), iterated learning converges to the prior.

One existing THEORY changed. [THEORY-014](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-014.md) gains Contextuality-by-Default as a
third instance of its signed-solution pattern, and the claim itself is
unchanged.

Two readers reported gaps in the vocabulary independently, and the owner
authorised extending it. `compositionality` and `mathematical-statistics`
join the topics by [ADR-031](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-031.md).

## What a reading should check

These entries deliberately say nothing about the manuscript. The owner wants
each work read first on its own merits, so that the reading is not tilted by
the use the owner expects to make of it. So a reading of any of these works
answers what the work itself establishes, and leaves the manuscript out. How
a work serves the manuscript is a later and separate question.

The four text-to-image works have been read, and the move to the anthology
can now be decided on what they are. Each NOTE marks the ML-practice content
in it as anthology material. The CDSB filtering experiments are probabilistic
modelling outside deep learning, and they belong here whichever way the
move goes.

  translation theory are now held.

  reported both gaps, and the works they cover had been under the nearest
  wrong word.

## How the readings bear on the argument

The coordinator added grounds and notes to the claims of the manuscript's
argument (line `pragmatic-transport`). Several readings change those claims.

- **The conceded prior art is stronger than the exchange knew.** Zhao et
  al. already formalise preserving the posterior over interpretations,
  which is the information bottleneck under KL divergence.
- **The quantum-cognition evidence counts against quantum contextuality.**
  Its strongest result, the QQ equality, counts against reading order
  effects that way, which is what the manuscript claims.
- **The Δ_CF claim needs restating.** It is undefined under signalling and
  cannot rise along free operations. Its premise that the contextual
  fraction is discontinuous is wrong within a scenario.
- **The Noether-type claim is weaker than it reads.** Baez's account puts
  the symmetry–conservation equivalence in an antisymmetric bracket, which a
  Markov kernel lacks.
- **The CbD 2.0 qualification holds, but only for binary observables.**
  The canonical-systems paper shows that the verdict depends on the
  representation.

## Points for the owner

- **Brandom was skimmed from the author's own posted course scans** of the
  whole book. The history note says so. Revert it to Deferred if that
  source is not acceptable.
- **"Frank, Goodman & Tenenbaum 2009" is ambiguous.** The paper registered
  is the word-learning paper. The informative-speaker precursor of rational
  speech acts is Frank, Goodman, Lai and Tenenbaum 2009 (CogSci), which is
  not held.
- **Gogioso and Pinzani's successor** (arXiv 2206.08911) is not held. If it
  is filed, the withdrawn paper becomes Superseded by it.
- **One reader sent the owner's email address to Unpaywall** in a single API
  query. It was not repeated, and the other readers were told not to send it.

## Five papers on the theory of trained networks

*2026-10-09 18:18:25 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: THEORY-180 THEORY-182 THEORY-022 — Proposed; cited as what this batch filed or bears on -->

The owner gave five arXiv papers to register, with no stated context. Each
was read on its own merits by a separate reader, from the arXiv PDF, and
each now has an Active LIT and a Read NOTE. All five fall on one theme:
what can be solved or measured about how networks train and what their
weights hold.

## What entered

- **Single-head attention in high dimensions** (Boncoraglio et al.,
  [LIT-857](../../record/literature.d/LIT-857.md)), with a Proposed THEORY ([THEORY-180](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-180.md)): weight decay on
  tied query–key weights is exactly a nuclear-norm penalty on their
  product. The spectral law that follows is derived, not proved; the paper
  calls its main results "Claims".
- **Closed-form dynamics of word2vec-like models** (Karkada, Simon, Bahri &
  DeWeese, [LIT-855](../../record/literature.d/LIT-855.md)), with a Proposed THEORY ([THEORY-182](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-182.md)): a
  rank-limited contrastive embedding learns the top eigenvectors of the
  co-occurrence deviation one at a time, not the best low-rank PMI. Proved
  for a proxy of word2vec, not word2vec.
- **Exact learning dynamics of in-context learning in linear transformers**
  (Mainali & Teixeira, [LIT-859](../../record/literature.d/LIT-859.md)). No THEORY: a Saxe-style solution whose
  fixed point was already known; its non-linear half rests on timing
  coincidences.
- **Towards understanding grokking** (Liu et al., [LIT-858](../../record/literature.d/LIT-858.md)), with a
  Proposed THEORY ([THEORY-181](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-181.md)) on when a training set fixes the
  generalising representation in the toy model.
- **Small singular values matter** (Staats, Thamm & Rosenow, [LIT-856](../../record/literature.d/LIT-856.md)).
  No THEORY. Its claim that information sits in the lower outliers of the
  spectrum is inferred from decile ablations that do not isolate them.

## The boundary

Four are not held in the anthology clone (commit d8b5ba5, possibly stale)
and carry `anthology-candidate`. The fifth, Staats et al., is held there as
[ANTH-LIT-517](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-517.md) with its reading [ANTH-NOTE-263](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/notes.d/NOTE-263.md), and is held here too under
[ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md). The second question here is how far a random-matrix null can
locate information in a learned matrix. The reading here disagrees with
[ANTH-NOTE-263](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/notes.d/NOTE-263.md) on one point (the Llama key and value exception), recorded in
its NOTE and not corrected there.

## Found along the way

- Three of the five changed title between arXiv versions; each LIT uses the
  current title and records the earlier one.
- Boncoraglio et al. cite Staats et al. as their empirical source for
  transformer weight spectra.
- Liu et al. is the earliest work in the record to find the circle in
  modular-addition embeddings, which [THEORY-022](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-022.md) is about. Adding it to that
  THEORY's sources is left to a revision of [THEORY-022](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-022.md).
- The vocabulary has no word for training dynamics, random-matrix theory or
  distributional semantics. `learning-theory` stands in loosely. No word was
  added.
- The owner ruled the same day that, when sources disagree on a date, the
  earlier one is taken ([ADR-002](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-002.md), version 2).

## Bearing on [QUESTION-025](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-025.md)

None answers it; their bearings are written into the question's new
section. The nearest thing to an answer was already in the record: Saxe et
al. 2019 ([LIT-862](../../record/literature.d/LIT-862.md)) gives tree-shaped linear directions for hierarchical
features in a linear network, one per branching rather than one per
attribute. The batch adds that hierarchy may be held by distances or by
containment rather than directions, that hyperbolic curvature alone is not
evidence of hierarchy, and that none of the geometric encodings gives a
lattice's meets and joins.

## The boundary

None is held in the anthology clone (commit d8b5ba5, possibly stale). The
machine-learning papers (Cagnetta, Sala, Ganea, Lin, Yang, Koch-Janusz &
Ringel) carry `anthology-candidate`; the network, neuroscience and
information-theory papers do not.

## Found along the way

- Several readers reported no word for hyperbolic or metric geometry, for
  statistical physics and the renormalization group, or for perception.
  `mathematics`, `network-science`, `natural-sciences` and `cognition`
  stand in. No word was added.
- The olfaction paper's date is its online date, 29 August 2018, not the
  issue's cover date of 3 August, which predates the article. The
  earlier-date rule settles real doubt about first appearance; a cover
  date before the article existed is not one.
- Works these papers build on that neither record holds: three follow-ups
  to the random hierarchy model (arXiv 2402.16991, 2404.10727,

## Floridi's line on artificial agency: six works filed, all read

*2026-10-10 05:46:20 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: THEORY-208 THEORY-071 THEORY-173 — Proposed; the account filed from the target's reading and its rivals, named as such -->
<!-- inactive-ok-file: QUESTION-009 — Deferred; set aside, and cited as the open question the batch bears on -->
<!-- inactive-ok-file: CLAIM-010 — Rejected; cited as the permissiveness objection the batch's criteria meet, not as standing -->
<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-534 — Unavailable, unread; named as a work the target cites that the record holds -->

The owner asked to file Floridi, "AI as Agency without Intelligence: On
Artificial Intelligence as a New Form of Artificial Agency and the Multiple
Realisability of Agency Thesis" (Philosophy & Technology 38:30, 2025), and
the line of work it builds on. Six works were filed. Three could be read
from lawful open copies and were. For the other three, the target among
them, no lawful full text could be reached, and they were registered unread
and Deferred, each with its access attempts recorded. The owner then
supplied the published version of the target, and it was read the same day
(see the last section). Four are read, and two remain unread.

## What entered

Read, each with a NOTE (the target was read later the same day, from a copy
the owner supplied; see the last section):

- **Floridi 2023, "AI as Agency Without Intelligence: on ChatGPT, Large
  Language Models, and Other Generative Models"** ([LIT-896](../../record/literature.d/LIT-896.md),
  doi:10.1007/s13347-023-00621-y), read in full from the publisher's
  open-access PDF ([NOTE-697](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-697.md)). It is the first statement of the slogan,
  and an editorial rather than an argument: no criteria for agency are given.
- **Floridi & Sanders 2004, "On the Morality of Artificial Agents"**
  ([LIT-898](../../record/literature.d/LIT-898.md), doi:10.1023/B:MIND.0000035461.63578.9d), read from the
  University of Hertfordshire preprint, in full, from page images, because
  the PDF has no text layer ([NOTE-701](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-701.md)). It is where the line
  starts: agenthood as interactivity, autonomy and adaptability at a stated
  level of abstraction, and moral agency split from responsibility.
- **Floridi 2008, "The Method of Levels of Abstraction"** ([LIT-900](../../record/literature.d/LIT-900.md),
  doi:10.1007/s11023-008-9113-7), read from the author's preprint in the
  University of Hertfordshire repository, in full ([NOTE-700](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-700.md)). It is a
  method set out in definitions, not a result: observables, levels and
  gradients of abstraction, with an epistemological levelism in place of an
  ontological one. Its one formal claim, that disjoint and nested gradients
  convert into each other, fails under its own definition of nesting. It
  never analyses agency.

- **Floridi 2025, the target** ([LIT-897](../../record/literature.d/LIT-897.md),
  doi:10.1007/s13347-025-00858-9). It was first registered unread, because
  no open copy could be reached. It was then read in full from the
  published version the owner supplied ([NOTE-702](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-702.md)), and it is now
  Active. It names the Multiple Realisability of Agency thesis and sets it
  against the Artificial Realisability of Intelligence. It is a taxonomy of
  kinds of agency, not an argument for that thesis. The thesis is assumed
  (p. 2). The three criteria of 2004 come back, loosened. AI's lack of
  intelligence is asserted, and no level of abstraction is stated.

Registered unread, Deferred, seeded from the abstract:

- **Floridi 2013, "Distributed Morality in an Information Society"**
  ([LIT-901](../../record/literature.d/LIT-901.md), doi:10.1007/s11948-012-9413-4). Its own abstract was not
  seen; the entry is seeded from search-result descriptions of it.
- **Floridi 2016, "Faultless responsibility"** ([LIT-899](../../record/literature.d/LIT-899.md),
  doi:10.1098/rsta.2016.0112), seeded from the published abstract, which
  Crossref carries.

Each identifier and publication date was checked against Crossref on
2026-10-10.

The relations, as filed: F2025 `extends` F2023; F2013 `extends` FS2004;
F2016 `extends` F2013. The two on unread works rest on the abstracts and
the Crossref reference lists (F2013 cites FS2004 and F2008; F2016 cites
F2013, FS2004 and F2008), and a reading should confirm them. The relations
among the read works are set by their readings. The reading of F2025
confirms its `extends` to F2023 and adds one to FS2004, whose three criteria
it takes. It writes none to F2008, whose method it names but does not use.
F2025 cites all five others.

## How deeply

Three read and three not when the batch was filed, and four read and two
not by the end of the day. [ADR-001](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-001.md) leaves the depth of each filing to the
curation log, and this is the statement for this batch. The owner has said
that in this record registering a work means reading it (the curation entry
of 2026-10-09, 00:41). The three unread works are an exception forced by
access, not chosen: each was looked for on 2026-10-10 and none could be
reached lawfully.

- **F2025.** OpenAlex lists it as green open access, but the open copy is
  the submitted version on PhilArchive (philpapers.org/archive/FLOAAA-5.pdf),
  which returned a Cloudflare challenge (403) and refused headless Chromium.
  SSRN 5135645 returned 403, and "Content Blocked" in a browser. The
  Springer version of record is not open access. ResearchGate was not tried,
  since it refuses automated access. The owner later supplied the published
  version, and it has been read.
- **F2013.** PhilArchive (philpapers.org/archive/FLODMI.pdf) returned a
  Cloudflare 403. The Hertfordshire record (uhra.herts.ac.uk/id/eprint/20632)
  has no file. Springer is not open access, and PubMed 23197312 has no free
  text.
- **F2016.** PhilArchive (philpapers.org/archive/FLOFRO.pdf) returned a
  Cloudflare 403. The Royal Society PDF returned a Cloudflare challenge and
  refused a browser too. PubMed 28336791 has no free text.

F2013 and F2016 each say in their status notes that they stay Deferred
until read, not on merit. Reading either would move it to Active with a
NOTE. A reader with a browser session past PhilArchive's challenge could
reach both submitted versions.

## The boundary

None of the six is held in the Anthology of the SOTA. A grep of a clone of
its record/ (commit d8b5ba5, 2026-10-09, possibly stale) for "Floridi" and
for each DOI found nothing. They are philosophy of agency and ethics, which
no anthology topic holds and none of which carries an instruction for
machine-learning practice, so they belong here and
[ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md) does not apply. None carries
`anthology-candidate`. They are tagged `agency` first.

## Found along the way

- **Where the line meets the record.** The batch bears on the record's
  distributed-agency line ([CLAIM-030](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-030.md), [CLAIM-045](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-045.md)) and on [QUESTION-009](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-009.md), "When
  does a pattern of coordination constitute an additional agent?". Floridi
  2013 and 2016 allocate moral standing across a network of human,
  artificial and hybrid agents. Floridi 2025's agency without mental states
  could say what the network's nodes are, but the paper does not make that
  connection. It cites distributed morality in one sentence (p. 6). It
  names three collective kinds of agency (ant colonies, corporations,
  Agentic AI) without a criterion for when a group is one, so
  [QUESTION-009](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-009.md) stays open. It is compatible with [CLAIM-030](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-030.md) and gives no
  evidence for it. On [ADR-024](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-024.md), Floridi 2025 keeps agency apart from
  intelligence and personhood, as that decision does. But the human kind
  of agency in its taxonomy absorbs identity, narrative self-understanding
  and a sense of self (pp. 14–15).
- **Permissiveness again.** The criteria of Floridi & Sanders 2004 meet the
  objection the record holds as [CLAIM-010](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-010.md), that on such an account every
  control system is an agent; the reading of that paper finds the objection
  answered by assertion. Floridi 2025 does not do better. It accepts the
  objection's conclusion: interactivity alone makes a river a natural agent
  (p. 9), and a thermostat is an artefactual agent (pp. 4, 13). It restricts
  no level of abstraction. It sorts agency into kinds, and the kinds are
  told apart by origin, mechanism and goal source, not by the three
  criteria. Floridi & Sanders' "for most entities there is no LoA at which
  they can be considered an agent" is not repeated.
- **Already held, cited by the target.** Frankfurt 1971 ([LIT-692](../../record/literature.d/LIT-692.md), read),
  cited only for the moral dimension of human agency (p. 15); Prigogine &
  Stengers 1984 ([LIT-534](../../record/literature.d/LIT-534.md), unread).
  Floridi's levels of abstraction were already used here, for structural
  realism ([LIT-152](../../record/literature.d/LIT-152.md)) and personal identity ([LIT-136](../../record/literature.d/LIT-136.md)).
- **Cited by the target, not held, not registered.** List 2021 on group
  agency and AI (doi:10.1007/s13347-021-00454-7), Dung 2024 on understanding
  artificial agency (doi:10.1093/pq/pqae010), Popa 2021
  (doi:10.1007/s13347-021-00483-2), van Lier 2023
  (doi:10.1007/s11229-023-04083-9), Himma 2009
  (doi:10.1007/s10676-008-9167-5), Bandura 2006 (the record holds only
  Bandura 1977, [LIT-545](../../record/literature.d/LIT-545.md)), Pearl & Mackenzie 2018 (the record holds Pearl's
  *Causality*, [LIT-894](../../record/literature.d/LIT-894.md)), Floridi & Chiriatti 2020 on GPT-3, Floridi &
  Nobre 2024, and Floridi's *The Ethics of Artificial Intelligence* (2023).
  List 2021 and Dung 2024 would be the first to file if the agency line
  wants rivals to Floridi's account.
- **Distributed knowledge, then common knowledge.** Floridi 2013's abstract
  borrows distributed knowledge from epistemic logic; Floridi 2016's borrows
  common knowledge. Both LITs ask a reading to say why.

## 2026-10-10: the target read

After this entry was written, the owner supplied the published version of
record of Floridi 2025 (Springer PDF, 27 pp., an Editor Letter). It was read
in full the same day ([NOTE-702](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-702.md)), with the text extracted by
`pdftotext -layout`. The PDF is not in the repository. The paper's own
outline replaced the reconstructed abstract, and the LIT is now Active.
It was retagged `agency`, `cognition`, `social-ontology`,
`society-and-governance`. It `extends` F2023 and FS2004, and it `rivals`
the organisational account of minimal agency ([LIT-566](../../record/literature.d/LIT-566.md)) and the account
of large models as social technologies ([LIT-848](../../record/literature.d/LIT-848.md)). The headline is that
it gives a taxonomy, not an argument. The thesis named in the title is
assumed. Of the four supports it announces, only the literature is used,
as a survey. Floridi & Sanders' criteria return, loosened, and they
separate only natural agency from the rest. AI's lack of intelligence is
asserted. No level of abstraction is specified. Against what the 2004 and
2023 readings found missing, it supplies criteria, though graded ones that
do not sort the kinds. It sets no limit on choosing a level of
abstraction beyond keeping one stable and ranking levels by purpose, and
it does not keep to that itself. It answers the permissiveness objection
by accepting it. Following the record's practice for comparable accounts
of agency ([THEORY-071](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-071.md), [THEORY-173](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-173.md)), the account is filed Proposed as
[THEORY-208](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-208.md), with those two as rivals.

## 2026-10-10, later: the two Deferred works read

The owner then supplied the published versions of the other two, and both
were read in full.

- **Floridi 2013** ([LIT-901](../../record/literature.d/LIT-901.md), [NOTE-698](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-698.md)), Deferred to Active. It
  defines distributed morality and introduces infraethics, the framework of
  moral enablers such as trust, privacy and transparency. Its analogy with
  distributed knowledge is looser than it claims: every example sums
  contributions of one kind past a threshold left unspecified, and there is
  no aggregation rule for actions. Its supra-agents are stipulated, and no
  Floridi & Sanders criterion is applied to them. Responsibility is left to
  the 2016 paper. `extends` [LIT-898](../../record/literature.d/LIT-898.md) is confirmed. No THEORY was filed.
- **Floridi 2016** ([LIT-899](../../record/literature.d/LIT-899.md), [NOTE-699](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-699.md)), Deferred to Active. It
  allocates responsibility for distributed moral actions by default,
  overridably and in full, to every causally accountable node. The reading
  finds that its "responsibility" is Floridi & Sanders 2004's
  accountability, used as a corrective signal to agents that learn. It also
  finds that back-propagation, the model it borrows, assigns credit in
  proportion to contribution, not equally, and that its own case of the
  Dutch boats is settled by control, not causation. It `extends` [LIT-901](../../record/literature.d/LIT-901.md)
  and [LIT-898](../../record/literature.d/LIT-898.md). Following the record's practice for French and Pettit
  ([THEORY-131](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-131.md), [THEORY-139](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-139.md)), the account is filed Proposed as
  [THEORY-207](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-207.md).

All six works in the batch are now read.

with the dancing couple ([CASE-046](../../record/cases.d/CASE-046.md)) as the paradigm case. Two adopted
terms were discussed from general knowledge: Kelso's coordinative structure
and Koestler's holon. These are the works behind them.

## What entered

Read, with a NOTE:

- **Simon (1962), "The Architecture of Complexity"** ([LIT-905](../../record/literature.d/LIT-905.md),
  [NOTE-704](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-704.md)). Read in full from the JSTOR PDF on a University of
  Washington course page. The record has read from a JSTOR PDF on a course
  page before (McAdams 2019). It is the source of Koestler's holon
  (through the watchmaker parable), and it has two findings the session
  can use: near decomposability as a boundary criterion, and the claim
  that higher levels of an organization have slower dynamics and rarer
  interactions, which is the all-hands case's cadence.

Registered unread, Deferred:

  doi:10.1037/0096-1523.10.6.812). The jaw-perturbation studies, the

  doi:10.1016/s0166-4115(08)61936-6). Coordinative structures as

- **Turvey (1977)** ([LIT-904](../../record/literature.d/LIT-904.md), the 2017 Routledge reprint of the
  volume, doi:10.4324/9781315467931). The usual source for the term.

  *Correction (2026-10-14, [NOTE-826](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-826.md)):* Turvey did not introduce the
  term. He says it is "borrowed from Easton (1972a) but used here with
  greater latitude" ([LIT-904](../../record/literature.d/LIT-904.md), p. 8). The chapter is where it was widened
  from reflexes to functional combinations of them and made the unit of

- **Bernstein (1967)** ([LIT-907](../../record/literature.d/LIT-907.md)). The degrees-of-freedom problem. The

- **Koestler (1967)** ([LIT-908](../../record/literature.d/LIT-908.md)). The holon. Controlled lending only.

## Boundary

None is held in the anthology. A grep of its record for Bernstein,
Koestler, holon, Simon's title and "coordinative structure" found nothing
relevant. None carries an instruction for machine-learning practice.

## Depth

One of six read. The next reading that would move a claim is Kelso et al.
(1984). If the record adopts reciprocal compensation as a membership test,
the test should be quoted from the paper, not from memory. Of the takeaways

## Mathematics of Meaning registered as MOM; five entries dual-filed for system boundaries

*2026-10-11 02:58:12 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: CLAIM-161 — Proposed or new; the entries this curation records -->

The owner asked: "register MoM as a remote and then dual file anything we
need from there on nucleation directly". [ADR-037](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md) records the decision. This
entry records what was filed, why, and how each was checked.

## The question it serves

What makes a combined form one system, and where its boundary lies. The
cases are the dancing couple ([CASE-046](../../record/cases.d/CASE-046.md), the owner's [CLAIM-175](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-175.md)),
the firm at its all-hands ([CASE-050](../../record/cases.d/CASE-050.md)) and the person across time. A
survey of Mathematics of Meaning, at commit d987e2a, found the five
entries below. It also found the record's own verdict on the wider question:
[MOM-CLM-170](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-170.md) records that the corpus's list of five boundary criteria
"terminates in a shrug". The gap criterion is that record's answer.

## What was dual-filed, and how it was checked

All five are CLAIMs in `distributed-agency`, each naming its MOM code:

- **[MOM-CLM-160](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-160.md) → [CLAIM-154](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md)** (Active). The Occam-priced reification
  threshold. Re-run: exact Bayes factor against the rule in the conjugate
  case, agreement to 9e-16 in eight settings.
- **[MOM-CLM-144](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-144.md) → [CLAIM-164](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-164.md)** (Active). The gap picks the object.
  Davis–Kahan, plus a re-run of MOM's stability table at 150 resamples. The
  pattern was reproduced; the exact angles vary with the draw.
- **[MOM-CLM-165](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-165.md) → [CLAIM-153](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-153.md)** (Active, abelian case). Unity as a
  monodromy over at least three contexts. Re-run: gradient descent against
  the closed form in all eight settings, and the two-context case always
  zero.
- **[MOM-CLM-153](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-153.md) → [CLAIM-161](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-161.md)** (Proposed, though Active in MOM). Selfhood
  as γ conserved under the system's own dynamics. A sound repair, but γ is
  unspecified and nothing was measured.
- **[MOM-POS-001](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/positions.d/POS-001.md) → [CLAIM-152](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md)** (Active). Sufficiency-based
  individuation is target-relative. True by definition, and the standing
  caution on the other four.

The scripts are not kept in the record. They re-implement each check from
the claim's own statement and are described in each entry's history.

Works already held in both records, cross-referenced under [ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md):

- Simon (1962) is [MOM-LIT-018](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-018.md) and [LIT-905](../../record/literature.d/LIT-905.md).
- Bruineberg et al. (2022) is [MOM-LIT-023](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-023.md) and [LIT-603](../../record/literature.d/LIT-603.md).

## Not filed

- **Everything else in the survey.** That includes the admissibility-groupoid
  drafts (whose central claim MOM itself retired as [MOM-CLM-142](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-142.md)), the
  predictive-closure functional in MOM's LLM-generated Attic, and the
  notebook criterion in a captured ChatGPT reply. None is graded in MOM's
  record, so none has a footing to carry over. If a question here needs one,
  it should be graded in MOM first.

## Fired before trusting

A citation of a MOM code that does not exist, [MOM-CLM-999](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-999.md), was planted in a
draft of this entry and the pipeline was run. **The lint did not catch it.**
MOM codes resolve by the code-only filename convention, which builds a URL
without checking that the file exists, and `luria repair` linked the bad
code like a good one. `luria remotes --check` reported every MOM document as
"unverifiable: repo not public": the repository is private, so anonymous
requests 404. It reports the same for ANTH from this environment. The only
check that worked was against a local clone: all eight MOM codes cited in
this record exist at MOM commit d987e2a, checked by script. The planted
line was removed. Until the remote is pinned, a bad MOM code is caught only
by checking against a clone. [ADR-037](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md) says so.

*2026-10-11 05:31:56 · curation · record*

The owner offered their microbiome as an example of drive from a lower
level ("my microbiome can impact things like my affect and level of hunger").
The record held the holobiont line for corals and several interoception
theories, but no human gut–brain literature. Two open-access reviews were

  doi:10.1021/ar00052a005). Grounds [CLAIM-181](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md). Once a more stable form
  has appeared, seeds of it can make the old form unobtainable. This is

  doi:10.1515/zpch-1897-2233). Not attached. A possible reading of the

  Growth"** ([LIT-924](../../record/literature.d/LIT-924.md), doi:10.2113/0540057). Grounds [CLAIM-176](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-176.md):

- **Vekilov 2010, "The two-step mechanism of nucleation of crystals in
  solution"** ([LIT-926](../../record/literature.d/LIT-926.md), doi:10.1039/c0nr00628a). Not attached. A

Shape and instability:

- **Witten & Sander 1981, diffusion-limited aggregation** ([LIT-925](../../record/literature.d/LIT-925.md),
  doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.47.1400). Grounds [CLAIM-186](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-186.md): tips catch
  what arrives next.

Order parameters:

The assistant also suggested Kashchiev's *Nucleation* (2000), Mullins &

Four of the seven ground claims while unread. They are held for what the

- **Vekilov 2010, "Nucleation"** ([LIT-919](../../record/literature.d/LIT-919.md), doi:10.1021/cg1011633,

The owner then asked for readings. Each of the eight was looked for in a
lawful open copy. Unpaywall and Europe PMC found one for Vekilov's
"Nucleation" (PMC2995260, an NIHPA author manuscript). Ostwald's volume is

- **Ostwald 1897** ([NOTE-709](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-709.md)), read in full in German from the OCR

  stable; a metastable intermediate waits for a seed unless it is labile;
  and the paper records no exceptions but explains them away. The word
  "Stufenregel" does not appear. The use the LIT was filed for, a stage
  reading of the thesis sequence, does not hold up. The seed experiments

  missed.

Both readings complicate [CLAIM-176](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-176.md): neither physical threshold is a

separate agent from the full text, then checked by quoting its key
passages against the source before filing.

## Stability theory for the nucleating-argument line: generalized stability theory and May, four works filed, none read

*2026-10-11 21:43:07 · curation · record*

The owner asked how the record covers stability theory: generalized,
variational, dynamic and thermodynamic. A survey of titles, keywords and
summaries found:

- **Ecological and resilience stability:** good and mostly read (Holling,
  [LIT-741](../../record/literature.d/LIT-741.md); Scheffer; [THEORY-132](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-132.md), [THEORY-136](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-136.md)).
- **Viability:** held (Aubin's notes, [LIT-714](../../record/literature.d/LIT-714.md), read; the monograph,
  [LIT-738](../../record/literature.d/LIT-738.md), unread; [THEORY-134](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-134.md)).
- **Variational principles:** held as two debates read critically, the free
  energy principle and maximum or minimum entropy production.
- **Thermodynamic stability:** held but largely unread. The Brussels books,
  Glansdorff & Prigogine ([LIT-537](../../record/literature.d/LIT-537.md)) and Nicolis & Prigogine ([LIT-524](../../record/literature.d/LIT-524.md)), are
  Deferred.
- **Generalized stability theory**, in Farrell and Ioannou's sense: nothing.
  The foundations of dynamical stability were thin too.

The owner asked for four works to fill the gaps that matter most to the
line, and for a reading of [THEORY-134](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-134.md) against the persistence claim.

## What entered

- **Farrell & Ioannou 1996, "Generalized Stability Theory", Parts I and
  II** ([LIT-931](../../record/literature.d/LIT-931.md), [LIT-929](../../record/literature.d/LIT-929.md)). The founding statement of the
  non-modal view, for autonomous and then time-dependent operators. Part I
  is free from the publisher.
- **Trefethen, Trefethen, Reddy & Driscoll 1993, "Hydrodynamic Stability
  Without Eigenvalues"** ([LIT-932](../../record/literature.d/LIT-932.md)). The short, widely read case: shear
  flows judged stable by their eigenvalues turn turbulent through transient
  amplification.
- **May 1972, "Will a Large Complex System be Stable?"** ([LIT-930](../../record/literature.d/LIT-930.md)). A
  size threshold for the stability of large random systems.

All four were checked against Crossref and are Deferred and unread. The
anthology holds none of them.

## What they bear on

- **Growth rate ([CLAIM-186](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-186.md)).** The GST works are grounds, and a note draws
  the consequence. An argument that settles in the end can still show a
  burst of drift after a disturbance, and directed dependencies are a
  standard source of non-normality.
- **Capture ([CLAIM-179](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-179.md)).** May is a ground, and a note adds a possible size
  limit on settling, beyond unused anchors.
- **Persistence ([CLAIM-185](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md)).** [THEORY-134](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-134.md) was added as a ground, with a
  note. Persistence is relative to a constraint set fixed independently of
  the dynamics, and for an argument the record's grammar is that set. A
  matching note on [CLAIM-181](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md) records that the counter and the persistence
  claim meet there.

## Gaps noted and not filled

- Lyapunov's 1892 memoir, structural stability (Andronov–Pontryagin,
  Smale), Thom's catastrophe theory, and a standard dynamics text
  (Strogatz; Guckenheimer & Holmes).
- Classical extremum principles.
- Gibbs's stability conditions, Callen's text, and Keizer & Fox's critique
  of the Glansdorff–Prigogine criterion. The record holds Landauer's
  objection ([LIT-532](../../record/literature.d/LIT-532.md)) but not that one.

## How the list was made

1. **The snapshot.** It holds 8,032 entries. 4,467 have a title and
   abstract. Most of the rest are placeholder titles from blocked pages.
   1,904 of those were recovered through the DOI or arXiv id in their URL,
   using Crossref and arXiv. 755 ScienceDirect links carry no DOI and were
   left out.
2. **Matching against the records.** Entries already held here (131) or in
   the anthology (45) were matched by identifier and title.
3. **Ranking.** Each remaining entry (title and abstract, first 160 words)
   was embedded with a local open model, BAAI bge-small-en-v1.5, and so was
   each Open or Deferred question (title and its "The question" section).
   The question set covered main and the two open PRs. For each of 71
   questions, the 15 nearest entries were kept: 504 in all.

   matched, from the abstract, and were told to be strict. 72 were judged
   useful to a question as posed (69 distinct works). 177 were judged
   anthology material only and 243 not useful.
5. **Drafting.** Four more agents confirmed each work's citation against
   arXiv, Crossref or bioRxiv and checked the anthology. The feed's metadata
   was wrong or incomplete for about a third of the works: missing
   co-authors, OpenReview links standing in for arXiv versions, and acceptance
   dates given as publication dates. The entries use the confirmed metadata.

**What the readings corrected in the filings of a few hours earlier.**

- **Kamenica & Gentzkow do not give [QUESTION-071](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-071.md) an invisible influence.**
  The filing said nothing in the persuaded receiver's present reasoning
  shows the steering, only its history. The paper says the receiver knows
  the signal and why it was chosen. The optimum also shows in her present
  beliefs. What the paper gives [QUESTION-071](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-071.md) is influence that is overt and
  still effective. The paper never cites Blackwell, and the filing's phrase
  "preferring a garbling of full information" was empty. Under the
  commitment assumption every signal is such a garbling.
- **Di Paolo is not [CLAIM-075](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-075.md)'s rival.** The filing called his paper the
  route from viability to norms that [CLAIM-075](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-075.md) must face. He argues that
  viability alone yields no norm the system can use, which is [CLAIM-075](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-075.md)'s
  own point made more strongly. His norms are for the system only. So Enoch's
  objection to constitutivism ([LIT-117](../../record/literature.d/LIT-117.md)) does not apply as the filing
  implied. His adaptivity is closer to an operative regime than to
  [CLAIM-025](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-025.md)'s transformation capacity.
- **Gallego & Orús does not bear on [QUESTION-026](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-026.md) or [CLAIM-098](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-098.md).** It computes
  syntactic probability only, with meaning set aside. Its many-to-one step
  stays inside one sentence. It keeps the word "renormalization" without
  rescaling, fixed points or flow. Its reader recommends setting it Rejected
  here, with the anthology's holding ([ANTH-LIT-695](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-695.md)) as the reason. That is
  for the owner to decide. The LIT stays Active, and its standing says why it
  barely bears.

**What the readings confirmed or sharpened.**

- **Fiat/bona fide crosses produced/imposed ([CLAIM-194](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-194.md)).** The membrane is
  bona fide and produced, the beam bona fide and imposed. On Smith & Varzi's
  terms every combined form of separate bodies is fiat. So the distinction
  cannot pick between answers to [QUESTION-035](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-035.md). A fiat boundary is still not
  arbitrary: the material "enables" and "constrains" where it can be drawn.
- **Self-production has a definition but no test ([CLAIM-194](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-194.md)).** Weber &
  Varela define the boundary a system makes for itself. They give no test for
  it. They restrict autopoiesis to the cell, which makes the counter stronger
  than it states.
- **Lewis's "almost one" fits [CLAIM-164](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-164.md) only in part.** It fits perturbed
  copies of one gap-isolated subspace, where the gap gives the threshold
  Lewis leaves open. It does not fit vectors inside a degenerate cluster.
  For those, his supervaluation suggests "indeterminate reference" rather
  than [CLAIM-164](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-164.md)'s "names nothing".

**Follow-ups the readers suggested and did not make.** Each touches an entry
outside this batch, so each is left to a later contribution:

- [QUESTION-071](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-071.md): name the overt-but-effective case.
- [QUESTION-070](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-070.md): note that a harm criterion needs a baseline.
- [CLAIM-075](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-075.md): say which kind of "conditional" judgement it means.
- [CLAIM-164](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-164.md): soften "names nothing", or defend it.
- [CLAIM-157](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-157.md): say how the duration clause handles a block that fades.
- [CLAIM-194](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-194.md): note that autopoiesis admits no combined form.
- File Lin & Tegmark (arXiv:1606.06737), which Gallego & Orús restates less
  rigorously.

## The intention-based line of illocution filed: Grice (1957, 1975), Strawson (1964), Bach and Harnish (1979)

*2026-10-13 18:44:12*

The owner asked how well the record covers conversational implicature and
Grice. The answer was that it covers both only through rational speech acts.
[LIT-816](../../record/literature.d/LIT-816.md), [LIT-821](../../record/literature.d/LIT-821.md) and [LIT-809](../../record/literature.d/LIT-809.md) are read, and [THEORY-172](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md) rests on them. No work
by Grice, by the neo-Griceans or by relevance theorists is held. [CLAIM-221](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-221.md)
already names the gap: its objection to [CLAIM-151](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) appeals to the
intention-based account of illocution of Grice, Strawson and Bach and
Harnish. The record holds none of them, so the defeat condition of
[CLAIM-151](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) cannot fire. [QUESTION-073](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-073.md) asks for the same works. The owner
asked for them to be filed.

## What is filed

The four works [CLAIM-221](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-221.md) and [QUESTION-073](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-073.md) name:

- Grice, "Meaning" (1957), *The Philosophical Review*;
- Grice, "Logic and Conversation" (1975), in Cole and Morgan (eds.),
  *Syntax and Semantics 3*;
- Strawson, "Intention and Convention in Speech Acts" (1964), *The
  Philosophical Review*;
- Bach and Harnish, *Linguistic Communication and Speech Acts* (1979),
  MIT Press.

`pragmatics` is the primary tag for each ([ADR-034](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-034.md)). A grep of the
anthology's record/ (clone of 2026-10-13, commit d1573d2) for "Grice",
"Strawson", "Harnish", "Logic and Conversation" and "implicature" found
nothing, so these entries are for this record only.

Each entry says whether a lawful full text was reachable and, if it was,
how deeply it was read.

**What the readings corrected.**

- **Litherland and Mørch.** "Instruction" in their title means Reddit's own
  rules, and the planners' designs fall under "emergence". The case, the
  equal-budget claim and the identifiability question had read it the
  other way. All three are corrected, and the paper now answers
  [QUESTION-084](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-084.md) in part.
- **Hawkes processes.** The branching ratio is a control parameter, and
  outside the linear excitatory case only a sufficient bound. It is not
  the order parameter that the question, both workbench entries and the
  Hawkes LIT said it supplies to [CLAIM-163](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md). Corrected where it was said.
- **Equal budgets.** Use of r/place's equal cooldown was itself heavy-tailed
  (Wu and Silva), so coordination is one source of unequal influence, not
  the only one. [CLAIM-272](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-272.md) now says so.
- **Lahiri.** The filing called it the closest case of constitutive
  influence. Its top level of autonomy is mostly not constitutive
  influence, and none of its vignettes shows an agent changing a control on
  itself.
- **Segura.** The filing's summary, "assay sets conservative for candidate
  models", is not in the SSRN abstract, which describes a topos-theoretic
  formalization. The summary and [QUESTION-086](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-086.md) now mark it unconfirmed.
- **Bickhard against [THEORY-072](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md).** Bickhard holds that a candle flame's
  self-maintaining processes are functional for it. Mossio, Saborido and
  Moreno ([LIT-570](../../record/literature.d/LIT-570.md)), whom [THEORY-072](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md) relies on, deny that. It is a
  disagreement about function and does not touch [THEORY-072](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md)'s title.
- **Adams et al. and Wu and Silva.** Adams et al. model no participants, so
  they do not estimate reach as the exchange expected. Wu and Silva
  clustered artworks for 2017 only.
- **Hoel et al.** The macro advantage depends on imposing a uniform
  intervention distribution at each level separately. "Causally
  privileged" overstated it.

A reader sent the owner's email address to the Unpaywall API, which
requires one, while looking for Segura's copy. It should not have been
sent. The owner has been told.

## Triage of the 167 Deferred works: what to read next, and where a copy can be had

*2026-10-14 01:23:03*

The owner asked for the Deferred readings to be triaged, and for a list of
those that are both likely to be valuable to the research agenda and likely
to be readable. Since [ADR-041](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-041.md), `Deferred` means that no failed search for a
copy is recorded. The 183 `Unavailable` works were left out. No status was
changed and nothing was read. This entry is a queue, not a reading.

## How it was scored

**Value** came from three signals, read together:

- the entry's own "Priority for a deeper reading" line, where it has one (46
  of 167 do: 16 high, 19 medium, 11 low);
- whether a THEORY, QUESTION, CLAIM or CASE cites the work, or the work's
  status note says which question it was registered for;
- how much the record has worked on that question, counted by mentions in
  `claims.d`, `arguments.d` and `workbench.d` on 2026-10-14. The most worked
  were [QUESTION-005](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-005.md) (83), [QUESTION-027](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-027.md) (37), [QUESTION-029](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-029.md) (36), [QUESTION-002](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-002.md)
  (33), [QUESTION-021](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-021.md) (31), [QUESTION-031](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-031.md) (30), [QUESTION-073](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-073.md) and [QUESTION-009](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-009.md)
  (27 each), and [QUESTION-054](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-054.md) (20). Works registered for a question that is
  itself `Deferred` ([QUESTION-008](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-008.md), [QUESTION-059](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-059.md), [QUESTION-061](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-061.md)) were ranked
  down.

**Availability** was checked as follows. An `arxiv:` source counts as open
(77 works). For the 73 works with a DOI, OpenAlex was asked for an
open-access location: 48 had none (`closed`) and 25 had one. For 25 of the
works with an OpenAlex location, this client then fetched it once. Most
returned the full text. MDPI, the AMS, the Royal Society, ACM and the American
Meteorological Society returned 403, and bioRxiv returned 429. The 17 `url:` works were
judged by their host. SEP, eScholarship, NASA NTRS and PMC are open. A
publisher's catalogue page or an Open Library listing is not open.

## Random projections: seven works registered unread, and a question tying the record's three uses together

*2026-10-14 21:06:29 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-1158 — Unavailable; the one work this entry registers that could not be read -->

The owner asked how the record stands on random projections. A search of
`record/` found three uses and no reading of the theory behind them. The
uses were random Fourier features ([LIT-679](../../record/literature.d/LIT-679.md), [THEORY-106](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-106.md)), the
compressed-sensing bound in Toy Models of Superposition ([NOTE-278](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-278.md)), and
the thresholded random projections of sparse distributed memory and the
mushroom body ([NOTE-242](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-242.md), [NOTE-670](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-670.md)). The search covered random projection,
Johnson–Lindenstrauss, the restricted isometry property, sketching,
locality-sensitive hashing, Achlioptas and fly hashing. No LIT, THEORY,
QUESTION or CLAIM had any of them as its subject. The owner asked for the
anchor works to be filed and for a question to tie the threads together.

## What entered

All seven were registered Deferred and unread. Metadata was checked against
Crossref, and against arXiv where there is an arXiv id.

- **Johnson & Lindenstrauss (1984)** ([LIT-1153](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1153.md), doi:10.1090/conm/026/737400).
  The lemma itself.
- **Dasgupta & Gupta (2003)** ([LIT-1157](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1157.md), doi:10.1002/rsa.10073). The
  elementary proof most later work quotes.
- **Achlioptas (2003)** ([LIT-1159](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1159.md), doi:10.1016/S0022-0000(03)00025-4).
  Shows that signed, zero-mean matrices with entries ±1, or √3·{+1, 0, −1}
  with two thirds zeros, are enough. Filed as the ensemble the fly and SDM
  use; the reading showed it is not (corrected after the reading).
- **Larsen & Nelson (2017)** ([LIT-1154](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1154.md), arXiv:1609.02094). Shows the
  bound is tight, so ε⁻² log n is a threshold.
- **Baraniuk, Davenport, DeVore & Wakin (2008)** ([LIT-1156](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1156.md),
  doi:10.1007/s00365-007-9003-x). Derives RIP from JL concentration. Filed
  as the bridge to the superposition bound; the reading showed it bridges
  sufficiency only (corrected after the reading).
- **Donoho & Tanner (2009)** ([LIT-1160](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1160.md), arXiv:0906.2530). The phase
  transition that [NOTE-278](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-278.md) asks about.
- **Dasgupta, Stevens & Navlakha (2017)** ([LIT-1158](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1158.md),
  doi:10.1126/science.aam9868). The fly olfactory circuit read as
  locality-sensitive hashing.

The question is [QUESTION-120](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-120.md), on the `formal-apparatus` line, because
it asks about a general result that other lines borrow.

## Boundary

None of the seven is held in the anthology. A grep of its `record/` (clone
at d1573d2) for the titles, identifiers, Johnson–Lindenstrauss, random
projection, restricted isometry, Achlioptas and mushroom body found the lemma
used only inside Linformer ([ANTH-LIT-529](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-529.md)) and random projections only inside
TracIn ([ANTH-LIT-400](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-400.md)). Six of the works are mathematics, and the seventh is
a neural circuit evaluated as a retrieval algorithm. No anthology topic
holds any of them, so none carries `anthology-candidate`.

Rahimi and Recht's random features paper is held in neither record and was
not filed. It is ML practice and belongs to the anthology.

## Depth

None of the seven was read, and every key takeaway is the result as it is
standardly stated. The reading that would move the question first is
Baraniuk et al. If its proof is as short as its title says, the
superposition bound in [NOTE-278](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-278.md) can be rewritten in the record's own terms.

## Reading, the same day

The owner then asked for the seven to be read. Six were read in full, each
from a lawful copy named in its LIT's history: [NOTE-930](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-930.md) (a course-hosted
scan of the published article), [NOTE-932](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-932.md) and [NOTE-931](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-931.md) (author-posted
copies), [NOTE-926](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-926.md) (a course-hosted 2002 journal draft, not the JCSS
text, whose Elsevier copy returned 403), and [NOTE-925](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-925.md) and [NOTE-933](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-933.md)
(arXiv). The fly paper is `Unavailable`. Its bioRxiv preprint is open but
returned 429 to this client throughout, so a browser fetch would clear it.

The readings corrected the filing in several places, and each LIT's
history says where. The ones that matter for the question are these. The
fly's matrix is not an Achlioptas ensemble. Baraniuk et al. explain
sufficiency of k log(N/k), not necessity. Donoho–Tanner universality is
asymptotic. The JL lower bound does not bound superposition capacity.
[QUESTION-120](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-120.md) is at version 2 with these corrections.

Griffiths as a memorize-or-look-up trade does not hold, and the entries
that repeated it are corrected.

## The LEGO parable ported from Mathematics of Meaning: what was kept, what was rebuilt, what was left

*2026-10-15 03:31:56 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: CLAIM-037 — Proposed; open claims cited as open, nothing here rests on their being settled -->
<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-1081 — Unavailable; held without a reading, cited as such -->

The owner asked: "I think there are some (albeit half baked, maybe
quackish but at the very least directionally correct) ideas built around
LEGO case studies that would be useful for us to port to (or modify for)
the nucleation record: see `Main Project/Geometric Epistemology/The Lego
Parable`". Mathematics of Meaning was read at commit d987e2a. Every MOM
code cited below was checked against that clone, since [ADR-037](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md) says a bad
MOM code is caught no other way.

  0, 1, 3–5, 7, 8c and 9, the Overview and Outline, Part II's Preface and
  Appendices, and all of Part III, including the attic and misc folders
  and the Smoothies note.
- **MOM's own grading of it.** [MOM-CLM-135](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-135.md), [MOM-CLM-136](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-136.md), [MOM-CLM-137](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-137.md),
  [MOM-CLM-138](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-138.md), [MOM-CLM-139](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-139.md), [MOM-ARG-047](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/arguments.d/ARG-047.md), [MOM-CLM-099](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-099.md) and [MOM-CLM-166](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-166.md).
  **MOM's intake is not a segment-by-segment review.** Its intake records
  mark all 53 monograph files "reviewed", and every segment of every file
  "produced" the same four entries ([MOM-ARG-047](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/arguments.d/ARG-047.md), [MOM-CLM-137](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-137.md), [MOM-CLM-138](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-138.md),
  [MOM-CLM-139](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-139.md)). So topical overlap with MOM is not evidence that MOM
  graded a passage. The second pass found three things MOM's record does
  not touch: the blow-up argument ([CLAIM-305](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-305.md)), the castle eigenmode ([CASE-097](../../record/cases.d/CASE-097.md)) and
  the smoothie note, which MOM's record never mentions ([CLAIM-309](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-309.md)).
- **The owner's own parable.** `homelab/own-words.md`, 2026-07-02, told
  alongside the EMT case this record already holds ([CASE-085](../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md)).

## What was filed

First pass:

- **[CASE-094](../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md)**, the owner's LEGO parable, a stipulated thought experiment. It
  is the second time [CASE-085](../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md)'s pattern has turned up, so it gets a code.
- **[CLAIM-307](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-307.md)** (Active), from [MOM-CLM-166](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-166.md). Retrieval and evidence are
  different criteria for a category, and they move oppositely with copy
  count. It complements [CLAIM-154](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md), the detection criterion dual-filed from
  [MOM-CLM-160](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-160.md) on 2026-10-11. MOM's table was re-run and reproduced, and a
  simulation of linear search agreed with m/(c+1) to within about 1%. One
  correction: that the criteria disagree on every row holds for MOM's
  deadline, not in general.
- **[CASE-095](../../record/cases.d/CASE-095.md)** (fictional construction) and **[CLAIM-310](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md)**. This is the directionally
  correct part of the monograph's contextuality, modified. As
  descriptions, sortings of bricks always share a joint refinement
  ([MOM-CLM-137](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-137.md)) and their events stay Boolean ([MOM-ARG-047](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/arguments.d/ARG-047.md)), so the
  monograph's central example is the non-contextual case of [CLAIM-037](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-037.md) and
  [CLAIM-131](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-131.md). As arrangements under a bin budget, they really compete. The
  monograph's "Sheafification as Descriptive Compromise" survives as the
  choice between the meet and the join of two partitions.
- **[QUESTION-114](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-114.md)**, refining [QUESTION-095](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-095.md): is sorting amortized search, and is
  database index selection the cost model [QUESTION-095](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-095.md) lacks?
- **[QUESTION-113](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-113.md)**: evidence, retrieval and persistence across refinement as three
  criteria for naming a category.

Second pass, after reading the rest:

- **[CLAIM-305](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-305.md)** (Active). Blow-up adds no observation. The monograph's Part I
  says resolution of singularities "restores identifiability", adds "new
  observables" and makes Fisher information non-degenerate ("Definitions
  and Theorems", Theorem 3.2), and maps this onto splitting a LEGO bin.
  The pulled-back model gives one distribution over the whole exceptional
  divisor. In x ~ N(ab, 1) the Fisher matrix is zero all along it,
  checked numerically. Splitting a bin is refining the observation, a
  Blackwell matter. [MOM-CLM-135](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-135.md) graded the definitions correct, and
  [MOM-CLM-099](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-099.md) the three senses of the word. Neither reached this step.
- **[CASE-097](../../record/cases.d/CASE-097.md)** (construction). Appendix H's castle topic persists by
  construction but as no eigenmode: the nearest eigenvector changes rank
  and turns about 51°, computed. It illustrates [CLAIM-148](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-148.md) and narrows
  [QUESTION-113](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-113.md), whose persistence criterion has to be stated for factors.
- **[CASE-096](../../record/cases.d/CASE-096.md)** and **[CLAIM-309](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-309.md)** (Active). The owner's smoothie line, and the
  finding that the note's signal-detection reading reverses its rising
  half. Discriminability from milk only falls as milk is added; the line
  is a preference over the ratio. This is the same kind of reversal
  [MOM-CLM-166](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-166.md) found in the LEGO parable's formal reading.
- **[CLAIM-306](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)** (Active). "If I can't find it, it isn't there" acts on
  an unfinished search as negation as failure acts on a finished one. It
  was first filed as "negation as failure under a deadline", with Reiter
  1978 and Clark 1978 registered unread. The owner asked for both to be
  read (Reiter from his own 1977 workshop report, [NOTE-899](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-899.md); Clark from
  the author's posted scan, [NOTE-894](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-894.md)), and both corrected it. The
  closed-world assumption (the database is complete) and finite failure
  (the search finished) are separate assumptions, and a search cut off by
  a deadline meets neither, so the rule is stronger than both. It is safe
  when the full search finishes in time, given by
  P(present | not found) = π(1 − h)/(π(1 − h) + 1 − π). In [CASE-085](../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md) the drug
  was known to be stocked, which is where Reiter shows the closed-world
  assumption inconsistent, so there the rule was a decision to stop, not an
  inference.
- **[QUESTION-114](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-114.md) extended** with a survey of the database literature for the
  owner ("work at the intersection of database theory and information
  retrieval"). It covers physical design and index selection, Yao's
  "Should tables be sorted?", database cracking, move-to-front and
  rent-or-buy. All citations were Crossref-checked; none is registered
  yet. The survey found no single cost model covering bugs, filing and
  bins.
- **[QUESTION-113](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-113.md) extended** with the owner's objections in the source: a criterion
  for naming must not be trivial, and must apply to objects as well as
  descriptors.

## The two visual-search works

Read at the owner's request.

- **Treisman and Gelade 1980** ([LIT-1082](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1082.md)): Read, [NOTE-897](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-897.md), from a
  Princeton course copy. It corrected the first pass. The paper puts
  serial search down to conjunctions of features, not similarity. It
  argues against similarity as the cause, and similarity on one dimension
  made search slow but not item by item. [CLAIM-310](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md) part 3 was restated:
  sorting on one attribute turns a conjunction search into a feature
  search within each bin. [CLAIM-310](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md) moved to Active on that narrower form.
  [CASE-095](../../record/cases.d/CASE-095.md), [CASE-094](../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md) and [CLAIM-307](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-307.md) were corrected to match.
- **Duncan and Humphreys 1989** ([LIT-1081](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1081.md)): Unavailable. The one course copy
  now returns 404, the Internet Archive's capture could not be reached,
  and OpenAlex reports it closed. Its abstract, checked by script against
  the MRC CBU bibliography page, states the similarity account. The
  record holds the disagreement with one side read.

## Four works on database physical design, and [ADR-044](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-044.md)

At the owner's request ("register and read those, and draft the ADR"):
Finkelstein, Schkolnick and Tiberio 1988 ([LIT-1084](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1084.md)), Yao 1981
([LIT-1097](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1097.md)), Idreos, Kersten and Manegold 2007 ([LIT-1090](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1090.md)) and
Sleator and Tarjan 1985 ([LIT-1093](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1093.md)). All four were Read, from a
University of Crete course copy, a University of Maryland course copy
(compared with Yao's own Stanford report), the CIDR proceedings and
Sleator's CMU page. ACM's open copies refused every request.

Three of the survey's descriptions were corrected by the readings.
Finkelstein's model is steady-state and has no one-time build cost. Yao
shows sorted order optimal only in an extreme regime, and counts lookup
only. Sleator and Tarjan compare move-to-front with the best dynamic
offline rule, not with an arrangement. Their Theorem 3, that rearranging
ahead of need never beats moving the found item, is the finding that most
changes [QUESTION-114](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-114.md). It supports [CASE-094](../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md)'s practice and puts
"sorting is amortized search" in question. [QUESTION-114](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-114.md) records all
four and stays Open: none gives the joint cost model, and the
precomputed-answer case (the cockpit's bugs) is in none of them.

These works had no topic of their own and were first tagged
`information-retrieval`, the nearest term. The owner: "don't hesitate to
extend the vocabulary as needed". [ADR-045](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-045.md) adds `databases` (Databases and
data structures) and retags them. Harinarayan, Rajaraman and Ullman 1996
([LIT-1094](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1094.md)), the survey's pointer for precomputed answers, was registered
and read at the owner's request for the case the four leave out.

[ADR-044](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-044.md) proposes a `corroborates` relation between claims, after a
`supports` filed in the first pass wrote a false `rests_on` onto [CLAIM-296](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-296.md).
The owner accepted it ("accept [ADR-044](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-044.md) and apply it"). The relation is
declared in `luria.yaml` and applied first to [CLAIM-310](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md), which
corroborates [CLAIM-296](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-296.md).

## Three more on the sorting question

At the owner's request. Comer 1978 ([LIT-1086](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1086.md)) is Unavailable: ACM
refused every request, and a Purdue report version sits behind a Cloudflare
challenge. A secondary account says it proves the hardness of choosing
attributes that distinguish every pair of records, not workload-driven
index selection, so the record's first description of it is marked
unverified. Piatetsky-Shapiro 1983 ([LIT-1089](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1089.md), read from SIGMOD's open
archive) proves the workload-based result by reduction from set cover and
is now cited for it. Karlin, Manasse, Rudolph and Sleator 1988
([LIT-1096](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1096.md)) was read from the publisher's scan on an MIT course page.
That is a course copy like the Princeton and Drexel ones used earlier, not
an author's posting. It gives rent-or-buy without the name, and the record
cites it as the first competitive analysis of that argument, not as the
source of the name.

Chaudhuri and Narasayya 1997 ([LIT-1083](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1083.md)) followed, read from the VLDB
Endowment's proceedings PDF, which refuses requests without a browser
User-Agent. It prices fewer terms than Finkelstein et al.: no build cost,
no storage.

Bruno and Chaudhuri 2007 ([LIT-1095](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1095.md)) and Athanassoulis et al. 2016
([LIT-1085](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1085.md)) were read last. Bruno and Chaudhuri are the closest to the
question's joint model, with a guarantee narrower than the survey said: one
index, no storage limit, and an unstated small-step condition, which a
simulation for the reading found. The RUM conjecture is vocabulary, not a
model.

The owner asked for "Harinarayan's follow-up on view maintenance". Stanford's
warehousing publication list shows Harinarayan wrote none. Gupta 1997
([LIT-1091](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1091.md)), by Harinarayan's co-author, adds maintenance cost to view selection and
was read in its place, from Gupta's own preprint. It adds upkeep only for AND
graphs and assumes no updates for the data cube itself. Gupta and Mumick
1999 ([LIT-1092](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1092.md)), read at the owner's request from the authors'
camera-ready, budget maintenance time instead. They show upkeep is not
additive and bound a greedy only for OR view graphs. Staleness stays
unpriced, so the question stays open. Their 2005 TKDE paper
([LIT-1080](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1080.md)), read from Gupta's own manuscript, turned out to be the
journal version of both ICDT papers, not of the 1999 one alone as filed; it
proves two of the three theorems and adds nothing the question needs.

## THEORYs for the readings

The owner noticed that this contribution and PR [#148](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/148) registered dozens of
readings and filed no THEORY. That was an oversight in how the readings
were filed, not a rule: each reading's bearing went into its question's
prose, and the paper's own finding was never stated as an account. Two
claims grounded works the record had read as bare LITs, which [ADR-032](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)
calls the weakest footing ([CLAIM-306](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md) on Clark and Reiter, [CLAIM-302](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-302.md)
on Goldreich), and [CLAIM-298](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-298.md) grounded an unread one.

Thirty-one THEORYs were drafted from the NOTEs, sixteen Active and fifteen
Proposed: eleven for this contribution's readings and twenty for PR [#148](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/148)'s.
Each states the finding with its conditions and says what it does not
show. Proposed is used where the record holds one unreplicated study, a
review's report of studies not read at source, an argued rather than
measured saving, or a conjecture. The anchoring account ([THEORY-335](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-335.md))
stays Proposed rather than Rejected: its lexical-decision test failed to
replicate, but the same task missed direct priming, so the test, not the
account, is what failed. The feature-integration THEORY ([THEORY-358](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-358.md))
states the search slopes, not the paper's mechanism, which Duncan and
Humphreys contest and the record could not read.

Claims now ground the accounts instead of the works: [CLAIM-306](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)
([THEORY-341](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-341.md)), [CLAIM-310](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md) ([THEORY-358](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-358.md)), [CLAIM-298](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-298.md)
([THEORY-335](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-335.md)), [CLAIM-302](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-302.md) and [CLAIM-304](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-304.md) ([THEORY-357](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-357.md),
[THEORY-352](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-352.md)), [CLAIM-294](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-294.md) ([THEORY-347](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-347.md), [THEORY-353](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-353.md)) and
[CLAIM-296](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-296.md) ([THEORY-351](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-351.md), [THEORY-346](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-346.md)). The rent-or-buy account
([THEORY-348](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-348.md)) bears against [CLAIM-303](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s clause that recurrence is
evidence of reuse and not the criterion: in the worst case, recurrence
weighted by the cost of rebuilding is the criterion, within a factor of 2.
At the owner's request it is filed as an objection, [CLAIM-308](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md), a
counter left Proposed: it narrows the clause where reuse cannot be
forecast, and does not reach staleness.

Drafting found errors in the readings, corrected in the same contribution:
two Active LITs ([LIT-1066](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1066.md), [LIT-1067](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1067.md)) whose bodies still said "Not read";
[LIT-1064](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1064.md) naming [LIT-1078](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1078.md) as the lexical-decision test, which is Mussweiler
and Strack 2000a; [LIT-1062](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1062.md) calling a trial-voiding error cost a doubling;
[LIT-1071](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1071.md) still calling Howes et al. a memorize-or-look-up trade;
[QUESTION-103](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-103.md) crediting Geisler with the efficiency formula; stale
"Deferred" acknowledgements for two Unavailable works; and two passages
on [QUESTION-114](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-114.md)'s database readings overtaken by later ones.

## Not ported, and why

- **The Epistemic Geometry Theorem** (Part II chapter 9), its extensions
  in Part III and Appendix G, and Part I's Theorem 4.3. [MOM-CLM-139](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-139.md)
  rejects the theorem. Its commutativity condition holds for every pair
  of sortings ([MOM-CLM-137](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-137.md)), condition 2 is about the site, not the
  presheaf, and the Rademacher, VC, rank and "archetype" clauses added
  later are not conditions of the same kind.
- **The topos chapter, the Čech cocycle definition, meta-contexts, stacks
  and the "compatibilist subsheaf".** These are standard definitions with
  no instance that is not empty in this framework. The cocycle definition
  is garbled, and the subsheaf theorem takes as hypothesis the vanishing obstruction that, by [MOM-CLM-139](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-139.md), does not even imply gluing.
  [CLAIM-153](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-153.md) holds the record's worked monodromy case.
- **SDT as non-neutral measurement** (Part I chapter 2) and **Part I
  chapters 0, 1 and 3.** These are surveys. Chapter 3's "event as an
  equivalence class of indistinguishable outcomes" confuses
  distinguishable in distribution with decidable from one observation:
  with any noise the relation is the identity, yet no single observation
  decides an event. The record's [THEORY-031](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-031.md) and [QUESTION-103](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-103.md) already hold
  the graded version.
- **State–observable duality** (Part I chapter 5). A real Galois
  connection between sets of observables and the partitions they induce,
  stated loosely. [CLAIM-264](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-264.md) and [CLAIM-142](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-142.md) hold what the record needs.
- **Nominal compatibilism, archetypes and PRH** (Part III). [MOM-CLM-138](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-138.md)
  rejects the position. The observation it kept is in [QUESTION-113](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-113.md).
- **LEGO sets as LDA documents, and hierarchical probability** (Part III,
  attic). Sound analogies for mixture models, with no claim of their own
  to test.
- **Two collectors with different collections** (Part I chapter 10). Its
  contextuality claim is [MOM-CLM-137](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-137.md)'s defect again. What it gestures at,
  that a builder's bins are fitted to their own collection, follows from
  [CLAIM-307](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-307.md): bins depend on copy counts and use.
