## Database theory and semantic search: 23 works read for the sorting question, the cost of reuse and revision

*2026-10-15 10:11:36 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-1101 LIT-1108 — Unavailable; held without a reading, cited as such -->

The owner asked whether "there are any results at the intersection of
database theory and semantic search that might be useful to the
nucleation record", and on the answer, to "register and read them all",
then to add HNSW. Twenty-three works were registered; twenty-one were read
and two are Unavailable, Cho and Garcia-Molina 2003 ([LIT-1101](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1101.md): the
author's copy timed out on every try) and Fagin 1996 ([LIT-1108](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1108.md): the
open copies returned 403). Neither the anthology nor this record held any
of them.

**What was asked of them, and what came back.**

- **Staleness priced** ([QUESTION-114](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-114.md)). Cho and Garcia-Molina 2000 prices
  it as freshness or age under a refresh budget; Olston, Loo and Widom
  2001 trade it against upkeep in one objective. The work named as the
  nearest joint model, Labrinidis and Roussopoulos 2003, is not one: its
  staleness is a threshold. The question stays Open.
- **The cost of recognizing reuse** ([CLAIM-303](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md), [CLAIM-308](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md)). Certifying
  that stored views answer a new query exactly is NP-complete for
  conjunctive queries; partial reuse is cheap. This is a concrete source
  of the drifting per-use cost [CLAIM-308](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md) already excludes. At the owner's
  request it was filed as an objection to [CLAIM-308](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md), [CLAIM-314](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-314.md), a
  counter left Proposed: it undermines [CLAIM-308](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md)'s fixed per-use price,
  not its arithmetic.
- **Organizing for similarity** ([QUESTION-114](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-114.md), [CLAIM-310](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md)). An exact
  space-time curve for hashing, cell-probe floors, the dimensions past
  which partitioning stops paying, and graph indexes whose guarantees hold
  only for a slow build. Fagin, Lotem and Naor reproduce Treisman's
  feature-versus-conjunction contrast in access costs.
- **Revision** ([QUESTION-105](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-105.md)). Derivation counts, delete-and-rederive,
  witness bases and provenance polynomials answer it for changes to base
  facts; none covers defeat or proves minimality.

**Readers' corrections to the registrations.** The "Why this is here"
written at registration, from memory, overstated several works; every
one was rewritten from its reading. The larger ones: Chandra and Merlin state
equivalence, not containment; Beyer et al. bear on [CLAIM-310](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md), not
[CLAIM-309](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-309.md), and their condition is sufficient only; the "about 10
dimensions" of Weber et al. is a measured crossover, not their analysis;
Indyk and Xu prove nothing about HNSW, and show its bad cases only by
experiment; the lower bounds of Andoni et al. hold on random instances in
one model; HNSW's final version drops deletion; provenance semirings never
mention deletion; and Labrinidis and Roussopoulos 2003 constrain staleness
rather than trade it.

**Copies.** Several were read from versions other than the one

<a id="20261015190538"></a>

## ADR-043 accepted: a required warrant field on CLAIM, every claim classified, nineteen compounds flagged

*2026-10-15 19:05:38 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: CLAIM-298 CLAIM-199 CLAIM-314 CLAIM-315 — Proposed; claims cited as the pilot's cases, nothing here rests on their being settled -->

The owner asked for a PR that "approves and operationalizes" the proposed
warrant field ([ADR-043](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md)). It is now Active.

**What was done.** A closed vocabulary `claim-warrants` (demonstrated,
empirical, interpretive) and an optional `warrant` field on CLAIM in
`luria.yaml`; the CLAIM template documents it and sets it by default; the
map in CLAUDE.md names it beside status and role. The pilot the ADR asked
for was run on twenty-six claims: the thirteen of the 2026-10-14 exchange,
A9's three older ones, and the claims filed on 2026-10-15. The table and
its findings are in [ADR-043](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md).

**The split.** [CLAIM-298](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-298.md) was compound, as the proposal had already noticed.
Rather than supersede it, its empirical half was filed as [CLAIM-315](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-315.md),
scoped to the comparative-question paradigm, and [CLAIM-298](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-298.md) now rests on it
and is marked interpretive. Its title already stated the general claim, so
nothing in the argument that cites it moves.

**Two decisions the pilot made.** `unestablished` is dropped, since every
claim it would have marked was interpretive and Proposed. And a claim that
cites a theorem but concludes something further is interpretive, not
demonstrated ([CLAIM-199](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-199.md), [CLAIM-314](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-314.md)); that rule is in the ADR so the next
classifier does not have to rediscover it.

**Required, and the whole record classified.** The first version of the
PR left the field optional because about three hundred claims were
unclassified. The owner: "There's no point adding this if we don't use
it", and "'failing' is a forcing function to make you fill in the field.
this is a feature, not a bug." The field is now required on every CLAIM.
The other 289 claims were classified by eight readers in parallel, one
batch each, and applied: with the pilot, 87 demonstrated, 12 empirical and
216 interpretive. The readers disagreed over untested empirical
hypotheses; four were set to interpretive so that `empirical` means some
observation the record holds supports the claim. Nineteen claims were
flagged compound and given the warrant of their main conclusion; four are
already split in effect by a separate claim, and fifteen are listed in
[ADR-043](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md) for the owner. Two readers found their scratch files overwritten by
others working in the same directory; both re-read their claims from the
record, and every batch's output was checked to cover exactly its claims.

**Not built.** The lint for a demonstrated claim resting on an
undemonstrated one, because that pattern is legitimate when the premise is
stated as a condition.

*2026-10-15 21:06:46 · curation · record*

The owner asked whether the warrant splits had downstream effects on the
record's argument. A check of every relation into the changed claims found

owner's request.

split, so quotations stayed accurate, but some passages cited a claim for
content it no longer holds as its own. A reader went through every
citation of the split claims in live text and found fifteen that cite the
moved part; nine more were found in reading notes, a THEORY and LIT
entries. Where a passage quotes the original, the original's code stays and
the new home is added; where it only refers to the content, it now names

## Later works on dimension reduction and Lipschitz extension: four filed, three read

*2026-10-16 04:22:31 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-1161 — Unavailable; Bourgain, the one work this entry files that could not be read -->

The owner asked for the later works relevant to the random-projection
readings to be read and filed. Three were named by the readings
themselves. Bourgain (1985) and Linial, London and Rabinovich (1995) are
in [NOTE-930](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-930.md)'s Connections, flagged as unchecked. Alon and Klartag
(2017) is in [NOTE-925](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-925.md)'s report of later work. The assistant added a
fourth, Lee and Naor (2005), as the later work on Johnson and
Lindenstrauss's extension problem ([THEORY-392](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-392.md)). No reading names it,
and its LIT's history says so.

## What entered

- **Bourgain (1985)**, [LIT-1161](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1161.md), doi:10.1007/BF02776078. `Unavailable`:
  OpenAlex lists only the closed Springer copy, and web searches found no
  author-posted or course-hosted copy. Linial, London and Rabinovich state
  its theorem and reprove its distortion bound, and the record reads it
  through them.
- **Linial, London and Rabinovich (1995)**, [LIT-1155](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1155.md), read in
  [NOTE-928](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-928.md) from the authors' February 1995 manuscript on an MSU
  course page. Filed as [THEORY-394](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-394.md): O(log n) dimensions and O(log n)
  distortion for every n-point metric, with expanders needing Ω(log n).
- **Lee and Naor (2005)**, [LIT-1152](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1152.md), read in [NOTE-927](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-927.md) from a
  January 2004 preprint on James Lee's page. Filed as [THEORY-396](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-396.md),
  C log n/log log n for extension into any Banach space, and
  [THEORY-400](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-400.md), extension from padded random partitions.
- **Alon and Klartag (2017)**, [LIT-1151](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1151.md), read in [NOTE-929](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-929.md) from
  arXiv v4. Filed as [THEORY-399](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-399.md), the bit counts and the dimension
  lower bound for every ε ≥ 2/√n, and [THEORY-393](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-393.md), the bipartite JL
  lemma.

## What the readings changed

- Problem 4 of Johnson and Lindenstrauss is answered in the negative, by
  the record's inference from Linial, London and Rabinovich. The
  sharpness of their √(log n) extension bound stays open, as Lee and Naor
  say ([THEORY-392](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-392.md), version 2).
- Larsen and Nelson's report of Alon and Klartag needed qualifying: the
  bound is additive, for ε ≥ 2/√n, and only its lower half is proved
  ([THEORY-395](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-395.md), version 2).
- [NOTE-679](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-679.md) relays a miscitation from Sala et al. The paper credits Linial,
  London and Rabinovich with a Euclidean lower bound for trees that they
  do not contain. [NOTE-679](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-679.md) is annotated.
- [QUESTION-120](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-120.md) goes to version 4: Alon and Klartag's proof makes its
  proposed shape literal, a log of a family's size.

## Boundary

None of the four is held in the anthology. A grep of its `record/` for
the authors' names and identifiers found nothing. All four are
mathematics. Linial, London and Rabinovich also carry `operations-research`
for multicommodity flow, and Alon and Klartag carry `information-theory`
for their bit counts. None carries an instruction for machine-learning
practice.

*2026-10-16 07:14:04 · curation · record*

The owner asked how THEORYs are distributed against LITs and NOTEs, and
then asked for the low-coverage topics to be audited, lowest first. The
owner's working hypothesis is that a work read closely enough to carry a
NOTE will usually support at least one THEORY. The owner expects that old
readings hold accounts that were never filed, and that filing them would
strengthen the record's arguments.

## The count that chose the topic

On 2026-10-16 the record held 1,161 LITs, 933 NOTEs and 400 THEORYs. 894
LITs carry a NOTE; 505 of those are a THEORY's `source`, and 389 are not.
By primary tag, moral-psychology had 18 LITs and no THEORY. Fourteen of
the 18 had a `Read` NOTE. The other four are `Unavailable`. Counted over
all tags, moral-psychology had three THEORYs, all on responsibility, and
none drew on these fourteen.

## What entered

Twelve THEORYs, four `Active` and eight `Proposed`. Codes are the
temporary ones `luria new` assigned.

- **Two rival accounts.** Morality-as-cooperation ([THEORY-468](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-468.md)) from
  [LIT-503](../../record/literature.d/LIT-503.md), [LIT-047](../../record/literature.d/LIT-047.md) and [LIT-496](../../record/literature.d/LIT-496.md). Moral Foundations Theory ([THEORY-539](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-539.md))
  from [LIT-499](../../record/literature.d/LIT-499.md), [LIT-502](../../record/literature.d/LIT-502.md) and [LIT-500](../../record/literature.d/LIT-500.md). Each is filed with the half of it the
  evidence does not reach. For MAC that is the prediction that
  non-cooperative behaviour is morally neutral ([LIT-503](../../record/literature.d/LIT-503.md), p. 40). For MFT
  it is Sanctity's pathogen origin.
- **Four findings, `Active`.** The 961-of-962 ethnographic result, with
  its detectability caveat ([THEORY-653](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-653.md)). The MAC-Q's seven Relevance
  factors in three countries ([THEORY-505](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-505.md)). The liberal–conservative
  foundation profile ([THEORY-435](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-435.md)). Purity moralized in MAC's own
  questionnaire data ([THEORY-632](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-632.md)).
- **Six more accounts, `Proposed`.** The MFQ-2's six factors
  ([THEORY-613](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-613.md), extending MFT). Puritanical morality as cooperation,
  from [LIT-101](../../record/literature.d/LIT-101.md) ([THEORY-494](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-494.md)). Fairness by partner choice, from [LIT-508](../../record/literature.d/LIT-508.md)
  ([THEORY-457](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-457.md)). Relationship regulation, from [LIT-507](../../record/literature.d/LIT-507.md)
  ([THEORY-626](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-626.md)). The social intuitionist model, from [LIT-511](../../record/literature.d/LIT-511.md)
  ([THEORY-558](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-558.md)), which MFT presupposes. Obligation from joint
  commitment, from [LIT-125](../../record/literature.d/LIT-125.md) ([THEORY-495](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-495.md)).
- **`rivals` edges.** MAC against MFT and against partner choice. MFT
  against the puritanical, relationship-regulation and MAC accounts.

## What did not enter, and why

- **Moral Molecules ([LIT-509](../../record/literature.d/LIT-509.md), [NOTE-399](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-399.md)).** Its reading says it "should
  not be cited as evidence that morality is combinatorial". Its 21 cells
  were each filled by searching for a confirming instance, with no
  protocol, and the paper says the theory does not predict which molecules
  exist. There is no finding to state. It is named in the MAC account's
  "does not say".
- **The 256-society dictionary study ([LIT-512](../../record/literature.d/LIT-512.md), [NOTE-406](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-406.md)).** It cannot
  detect valence. Its agreement with the sixty-society hand codes is κ
  .08–.25. It is in the Connections of [THEORY-653](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-653.md) as a rough
  replication of presence, not of valence. It is not a source, because
  that THEORY does not rest on it.
- **The Turkish validation ([LIT-513](../../record/literature.d/LIT-513.md)).** It entered as the second source
  of the MAC-Q THEORY, not as a THEORY of its own. Its prosociality and
  scarcity results are nulls or near-nulls and are reported there.

So twelve of fourteen readings became sources. That fits the owner's
hypothesis for this topic. Two caveats apply. Several readings were
already written with a THEORY in view ([NOTE-034](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-034.md)'s "Any THEORY document
citing it…"). And the two that entered nothing are the programme's
weakest papers, which their readings had already judged.

## Choices made

- **Status.** A finding was made `Active` when the record believes it as
  stated: as a description of self-report, or of a coded corpus, with the
  caveats in its title or "does not say". An account went `Proposed`
  when its readings mark it untested or argued rather than shown. No
  account here is `Active`.
- **No `answers` edge.** [QUESTION-007](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-007.md) asks what grounds normativity
  between agents at one level. Tomasello's account describes how the
  sense of obligation between peers arises. Its author concedes that it
  cannot say what anyone ought to do. It is named in the THEORY's
  Connections and not linked as an answer.
- **Error carried forward.** The hawk–dove attribution to Maynard Smith
  and Price, which [NOTE-034](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-034.md) and [NOTE-408](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-408.md) correct, is repeated in the MAC
  THEORY as a correction rather than as the paper's lineage.

<a id="20261016073804"></a>

## Social ontology, game theory, religion, design rationale: nine THEORYs from eleven readings

*2026-10-16 07:38:04 · curation · record*

Part of the THEORY backfill the owner asked for on 2026-10-16: for each
LIT with a `Read` NOTE that no THEORY cites as `source`, decide whether the
reading supports an account, and file the ones it does. This group held
eleven such LITs: eight in social-ontology, one each in game-theory,
religion and design-rationale. Every NOTE was `Read`; none was a skim.

## What entered

Nine THEORYs, one `Active` and eight `Proposed`. Codes are the temporary
ones `luria new` assigned.

- **Groups.** Ritchie 2013 ([THEORY-549](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-549.md); sources [LIT-479](../../record/literature.d/LIT-479.md), [LIT-486](../../record/literature.d/LIT-486.md)): a
  structured group is not its members, since coincident groups of one kind
  are two; plurality, fusion, aggregate and set theories cannot allow it.
  Ritchie 2018 ([THEORY-575](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-575.md); [LIT-486](../../record/literature.d/LIT-486.md), [LIT-479](../../record/literature.d/LIT-479.md)): organized groups are
  structured wholes, feature groups are social kinds. It `extends` the
  first.
- **Social kinds.** Haslanger ([THEORY-667](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-667.md); [LIT-480](../../record/literature.d/LIT-480.md)): gender and race as
  hierarchical social positions, filed with its ameliorative status in the
  title and its descriptive claim as what `promote_when` can test.
- **Institutions, as rivals.** Searle's status functions ([THEORY-625](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-625.md);
  [LIT-482](../../record/literature.d/LIT-482.md)) against Hindriks & Guala's rules in equilibrium
  ([THEORY-414](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-414.md); [LIT-481](../../record/literature.d/LIT-481.md)). They disagree about what a constitutive rule
  adds and whether institutions need one, and neither has settled it, so
  the edge is `rivals`, not `corrects`.
- **The social fact.** Durkheim ([THEORY-648](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-648.md); [LIT-484](../../record/literature.d/LIT-484.md)): exteriority and
  constraint, general because collective.
- **Grounding and anchoring.** Epstein ([THEORY-487](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-487.md); [LIT-487](../../record/literature.d/LIT-487.md)), from a
  survey and the author's précis, filed as `Proposed` because the
  distinction's sharpness is disputed and the survey gives the dissents a
  sentence each.
- **Non-redundant group attitudes.** List & Pettit's replies
  ([THEORY-536](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-536.md); [LIT-730](../../record/literature.d/LIT-730.md)), with `answers: [QUESTION-009]` as a partial
  answer of one kind.
- **Bayesian persuasion.** Kamenica & Gentzkow ([THEORY-404](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-404.md); [LIT-1021](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1021.md)),
  `Active`: proved results, stated with their conditions (common prior,
  commitment, one ideal receiver, sender-preferred tie-breaking).

## What did not enter, and why

- **De Cruz, Religion and Science ([LIT-194](../../record/literature.d/LIT-194.md), [NOTE-107](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-107.md)).** A survey with no
  thesis of its own. Its characterisations of scholarly consensus are the
  author's, with no systematic evidence (C2, C5); its one argued point,
  that Barbour's categories are neither exhaustive nor exclusive, is an
  informal argument from one counterexample that offers no replacement.
  Its reading says there is no THEORY here to support or contradict.
- **Kunz & Rittel, IBIS ([LIT-758](../../record/literature.d/LIT-758.md), [NOTE-811](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-811.md)).** A seven-page design
  specification. Its three general claims are asserted (all `weak` in the
  NOTE), and its reading already declined to file a THEORY. It names Rittel
  and Webber's wicked problems as the place to file C1 from, if read.

So nine of eleven readings became sources, and every social-ontology
reading did. That fits the owner's hypothesis here, with a caveat: only
one of the nine is `Active`. Most of these works are definitions,
frameworks or conceptual analyses that their readings mark as argued by
example, so the accounts they support are proposals. The two that entered
nothing are a survey and a specification.

## Choices made

- **Status.** Only the proved result is `Active`. Each social-ontology
  account went `Proposed`, and each `promote_when` names an argument or
  case of a kind the source did not supply, and says why more of the
  source's own kind of example cannot settle it.
- **Haslanger as a claim.** The paper is stipulative by design. The title
  states the account with its condition ("defined as a feminist and
  antiracist theory needs them"), and `promote_when` points at the
  descriptive claim the paper ties its definitions to, since the
  ameliorative half cannot be settled by evidence.
- **`answers` edges.** One only: [THEORY-536](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-536.md) on [QUESTION-009](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-009.md). Searle's
  account was not linked to [QUESTION-007](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-007.md): the desire-independence that would
  make it a grounding of normativity is asserted and disputed by its rival.
  Bayesian persuasion was not linked to [QUESTION-070](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-070.md) or [QUESTION-071](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-071.md): the
  paper does not call it manipulation, and its case is visible influence on
  belief, not invisible influence on a will. Both are in Connections.
- **No sources added to existing THEORYs.** [LIT-730](../../record/literature.d/LIT-730.md) bears on [THEORY-127](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-127.md) and
  [THEORY-139](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-139.md), as its reading says, and Ritchie and Epstein are used in
  [THEORY-043](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md)'s body; none is load-bearing for those accounts, and this task
  edits no existing THEORY.
- **Codes from parallel work not cited.** The moral-psychology batch's
  Tomasello account (joint commitment and obligation) is the nearest
  THEORY to Searle and Durkheim, but it is not on this branch; [LIT-125](../../record/literature.d/LIT-125.md) is
  cited instead.

## Errors found while reading

- **[LIT-194](../../record/literature.d/LIT-194.md)'s body is stale.** It still says "Seeded from the abstract and a
  skim, not a reading", that the work "was filed `Deferred`, unread", and
  gives a priority for a deeper reading, though [NOTE-107](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-107.md) is a full reading
  and the status is `Active`.
- **[NOTE-107](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-107.md)'s Bearing says the vocabulary "cannot yet say 'religion'"**;
  the `religion` topic now exists and is the LIT's primary tag.
- **[ADR-032](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)'s `inactive-ok-file` directive** names [LIT-758](../../record/literature.d/LIT-758.md) as "Deferred … unread";
  it was read on 2026-10-14 and is `Active`.
- **[NOTE-394](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-394.md) and [NOTE-391](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-391.md) say no THEORY cites or needs their works.** True
  when written; now each is a THEORY's source.

## Linguistics, pragmatics, philosophy of language and myth: ten THEORYs from eleven readings

*2026-10-16 07:38:34 · curation · record*

Part of the THEORY backfill the owner asked for on 2026-10-16. The working
hypothesis is that a work read closely enough to carry a NOTE will usually
support at least one THEORY. This entry covers four topic groups:
linguistics, pragmatics, philosophy-of-language and myth-and-folklore. Each
group had LITs with a `Read` or `Skimmed` NOTE that no THEORY cites as
`source`, seventeen in all.

## What entered

Ten THEORYs, one `Active` and nine `Proposed`. Codes are the temporary ones
`luria new` assigned.

- **Linguistics, the anti-lexicalist trio.**
  - [THEORY-477](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-477.md), `Active`: none of ten wordhood criteria is necessary
    and sufficient for the orthographic word across languages, and the
    test batteries choose criteria opportunistically. From Haspelmath 2011
    ([LIT-063](../../record/literature.d/LIT-063.md)). Its NOTE named C1 and C4 as the defensible content, and the
    title keeps to them. "Morphosyntax is one domain" is left in the body
    as the hedged consequence.
  - [THEORY-643](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-643.md), `Proposed`: the restrictions credited to a word
    component are restrictions on X0 against XP and on affix selection.
    From Bruening 2018 ([LIT-071](../../record/literature.d/LIT-071.md)), with Müller's reply named as the
    opposing reading, as its NOTE asked.
  - [THEORY-588](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-588.md), `Proposed`: lemma-based production models fail
    algorithmically, not only representationally. From Krauska and Lau
    2023 ([LIT-031](../../record/literature.d/LIT-031.md)). It `presupposes` [THEORY-643](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-643.md).
- **Pragmatics and the intention-based line.**
  - [THEORY-444](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-444.md), `Proposed`: Grice's analysis of speaker meaning
    ([LIT-1042](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1042.md)).
  - [THEORY-511](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-511.md), `Proposed`: Strawson's account of illocutionary force
    ([LIT-1043](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1043.md), with [LIT-1042](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1042.md)). It `extends` the Grice THEORY and `answers`
    [QUESTION-073](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-073.md) in part.
  - [THEORY-693](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-693.md), `Proposed`: Du Bois's stance triangle, with the
    too/either marking as its one stated prediction ([LIT-779](../../record/literature.d/LIT-779.md)).
  - [THEORY-472](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-472.md), `Proposed`: the informative speaker and the size
    principle, with learners' and speakers' results ([LIT-824](../../record/literature.d/LIT-824.md)).
- **Philosophy of language.**
  - [THEORY-518](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-518.md), `Proposed`: differential stability of distributional
    meaning ([LIT-208](../../record/literature.d/LIT-208.md)).
  - [THEORY-665](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-665.md), `Proposed`, resting on a skim: Brandom's deontic
    scorekeeping model of assertion ([LIT-794](../../record/literature.d/LIT-794.md)).
- **Myth and folklore.**
  - [THEORY-432](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-432.md), `Proposed`: in Lévi-Straussian myth analysis the
    transformation group is cut by the analyst. From Descola 2016
    ([LIT-822](../../record/literature.d/LIT-822.md)), with Santucci, Doja and Capocchi 2020 ([LIT-807](../../record/literature.d/LIT-807.md)) as the
    second source for its concession that the software takes the table of
    oppositions as input.

## What did not enter, and why

- **Language Design as Information Renormalization ([LIT-1023](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1023.md), [NOTE-718](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-718.md)).**
  Its reading ends "No THEORY should be produced from this reading". The
  power law restates Lin and Tegmark less rigorously with an asserted
  averaging step, nothing is tested on data, and the architecture claim is
  ML practice, which is the anthology's ([ANTH-LIT-695](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-695.md)).
- **Semantic Unification ([LIT-841](../../record/literature.d/LIT-841.md), [NOTE-644](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-644.md)).** Its one structural point is
  Proposition 1, a fact about the construction, not a finding about
  language. The NOTE says so and also warns against citing it for
  contextuality in [THEORY-012](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md)'s sense.
- **Logic and Conversation ([LIT-1041](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1041.md), [NOTE-734](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-734.md)).** Unavailable, and only
  pp. 45–47 read. The pages state the Cooperative Principle and the maxims
  but not the account of implicature, so there is no account to file.
- **Marabini on Brandom ([LIT-106](../../record/literature.d/LIT-106.md), [NOTE-179](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-179.md)).** Unavailable, and a seeded
  skim that says it is "not enough to state its assumptions or results
  exactly".
- **Doja, Capocchi and Santucci 2021 ([LIT-804](../../record/literature.d/LIT-804.md), [NOTE-609](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-609.md)).** Software and a
  map display, with no claim about myth tested. It summarises [LIT-807](../../record/literature.d/LIT-807.md)'s
  engine faithfully, so it is named in [THEORY-432](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-432.md)'s Connections and
  is not a source.
- **Morphology of the Folktale ([LIT-830](../../record/literature.d/LIT-830.md), [NOTE-642](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-642.md)).** A skim of the English
  translation of [LIT-828](../../record/literature.d/LIT-828.md). [THEORY-167](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-167.md) already holds the content from the
  Russian reading, and the NOTE judged its translation observation too
  thin for a THEORY.

So eleven of seventeen readings became sources. Two of the six that did
not are Unavailable partial skims. Two are software or programme papers
whose readings judged them to carry no finding. One is a translation whose
original already sources a THEORY. One ([LIT-1023](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1023.md)) has its substance in the
anthology. That fits the owner's hypothesis for these topics, with one
caveat: four of the eleven ([LIT-779](../../record/literature.d/LIT-779.md), [LIT-822](../../record/literature.d/LIT-822.md), [LIT-807](../../record/literature.d/LIT-807.md), [LIT-031](../../record/literature.d/LIT-031.md)) carry
NOTEs or LIT notes that said no THEORY should be filed. In each case the
THEORY filed here avoids the part the reading rejected:

- Du Bois's NOTE offered the too/either rule as a candidate. It is filed
  inside the triangle account as that account's one prediction.
- Krauska and Lau's NOTE ruled out the unimplemented model as a source.
  The THEORY rests on the critique (C1–C5) and lists the model under
  "does not say".
- Descola's and Santucci's notes said each reports no finding about myth.
  Together they support a claim about the method, which is what is filed.
- Brandom's NOTE said "No THEORY is filed from a skim". The brief for this
  backfill allows a `Proposed` THEORY on a skim if it says so, and
  [THEORY-665](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-665.md) says so in its summary, Source and `promote_when`.

## Choices made

- **One `Active`.** Haspelmath's criterion-by-criterion result is a
  counterexample argument the record believes as stated, with the
  orthographic target named in "does not say". Every other account is
  argued from chosen examples, a skim, or a parameter-free fit that cannot
  separate it from a simpler rival.
- **`answers`.** Only [QUESTION-073](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-073.md), from Strawson. The question names the
  intention-based line as its rival, and Strawson's scheme makes the
  prediction the question needs: no non-institutional case with the overt
  intention fixed and the act changed. Grice individuates no act types, so
  his THEORY carries no edge. Du Bois offers stance categories but no
  reliability test, so [QUESTION-076](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-076.md) gets no edge.
- **No `rivals`.** Brandom's normative account of content and Grice's
  intention-based account run in opposite orders of explanation. As each
  is stated here they do not exclude each other, so the contrast is in
  prose in both.
- **No edge to [THEORY-172](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md).** The informative-speaker THEORY is the
  precursor of the rational-speech-act account. A relation would belong on
  [THEORY-172](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md), which this task does not edit.

## Existing documents and errors noted

- **[THEORY-172](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md)** does not cite [LIT-824](../../record/literature.d/LIT-824.md). [LIT-824](../../record/literature.d/LIT-824.md)'s own Standing says its
  Experiment 1 "adds to the evidence for [THEORY-172](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md)", so the owner may want
  [LIT-824](../../record/literature.d/LIT-824.md) added to that THEORY's `source`, or an `extends` edge from
  [THEORY-172](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md) to [THEORY-472](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-472.md).
- **[THEORY-167](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-167.md)** could name [LIT-830](../../record/literature.d/LIT-830.md) as the English text, but the account
  does not rest on it.
- **[LIT-1043](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1043.md)'s NOTE** records that Strawson cites Grice's "Meaning" as
  volume LXVII; the volume is LXVI. That is Strawson's slip, and the NOTE
  already corrects it.
- **[NOTE-029](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-029.md)** carries an `inactive-ok-file` directive calling [LIT-031](../../record/literature.d/LIT-031.md)
  "Deferred"; [LIT-031](../../record/literature.d/LIT-031.md) is now Proposed. [NOTE-158](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-158.md) carries the same kind of
  stale directive for [LIT-208](../../record/literature.d/LIT-208.md), with its lapse clause written twice. Both
  still hold because both LITs are inactive. They are left alone, since
  this task edits no NOTE.
- **[LIT-779](../../record/literature.d/LIT-779.md)** names [LIT-780](../../record/literature.d/LIT-780.md) as "Deferred", while [LIT-1043](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1043.md) and the
  [QUESTION-073](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-073.md) directives name it "Unavailable". [LIT-780](../../record/literature.d/LIT-780.md) is Unavailable.
- **`luria repair`** also upgraded an old code spelling in the curation
  entry of 2026-10-15 (194615), `CLAIM-tmp3bdbx` to `CLAIM-315`. That
  change is not this contribution's, and it was reverted here to keep the
  diff to its own files. [QUESTION-073](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-073.md)'s new `answered_by` entry is the converse
  that `luria link --fix` writes for the Strawson THEORY's `answers`.

## Thermodynamics: eight THEORYs from ten readings

*2026-10-16 07:38:35 · curation · record*

Part of the THEORY backfill the owner asked for on 2026-10-16 (see the
moral-psychology entry of the same day). The thermodynamics topic held ten
LITs with a `Read` NOTE and no THEORY citing any of them. All ten were
filed on 2026-10-02 in one batch on dissipative structures, maximum entropy
production and the fluctuation theorems. Every NOTE was read in full, with
its LIT. No paper was fetched; each THEORY rests on the record's reading.

## What entered

Eight THEORYs, three `Active` and five `Proposed`. Codes are the temporary
ones `luria new` assigned.

- **Three findings, `Active`.**
  - The fluctuation theorems ([THEORY-431](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-431.md)), from Crooks ([LIT-522](../../record/literature.d/LIT-522.md)),
    Jarzynski ([LIT-517](../../record/literature.d/LIT-517.md)) and Seifert's review ([LIT-523](../../record/literature.d/LIT-523.md)). Exact given
    their premises, and filed with what they do not say: no proof of the
    second law, no selection principle for steady states, no practical
    reach beyond fluctuations of order k_BT.
  - England's macrostate bound ([THEORY-679](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-679.md)), from [LIT-515](../../record/literature.d/LIT-515.md). The
    general bound is a re-derived coarse-grained second law. The title
    carries the condition the replication numbers need, since their
    reverse probability is argued, not proved.
  - The critique of Dewar's derivation of maximum entropy production
    ([THEORY-676](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-676.md)), from Grinstein and Linsker ([LIT-525](../../record/literature.d/LIT-525.md)) and Dewar
    ([LIT-521](../../record/literature.d/LIT-521.md)). Its point about Dewar 2005 is held on the Comment's
    account and its spin chain, because that letter could not be read.
- **Five accounts, `Proposed`.**
  - Maximum entropy production ([THEORY-671](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-671.md)), from Kleidon ([LIT-519](../../record/literature.d/LIT-519.md))
    and Dewar ([LIT-521](../../record/literature.d/LIT-521.md)).
  - Life and planetary MEP, Kleidon's thermodynamic Gaia
    ([THEORY-517](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-517.md)), from [LIT-519](../../record/literature.d/LIT-519.md). It `presupposes` the MEP account.
  - Dissipative adaptation ([THEORY-412](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-412.md)), from Perunov, Marsland and
    England ([LIT-518](../../record/literature.d/LIT-518.md)) with [LIT-515](../../record/literature.d/LIT-515.md). It `presupposes` the fluctuation
    theorems and England's bound.
  - Gradient dissipation ([THEORY-532](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-532.md)), from Schneider and Kay
    ([LIT-533](../../record/literature.d/LIT-533.md)).
  - Life forced into existence by geochemistry ([THEORY-492](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-492.md)), from
    Morowitz and Smith ([LIT-528](../../record/literature.d/LIT-528.md)).

So all ten readings became sources. That fits the owner's hypothesis, with
a caveat on how it was met: five of the eight are `Proposed`, and three of
them come from readings whose NOTEs say "No new THEORY is indicated".

## What did not enter, and why

No LIT went without a THEORY. Two candidates were considered and folded
into others:

- **Kleidon's contrast with Prigogine** (minimum entropy production
  describes relaxation; MEP selects among steady states). It is in the
  title of the MEP account, not a THEORY of its own, because the review
  argues it by example and states neither principle's conditions.
- **Seifert's other results** (the Sagawa–Ueda feedback bound, efficiency
  at maximum power). The review is a source for the fluctuation-theorem
  finding only. The feedback bound bears on [THEORY-030](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-030.md)'s subject and is
  named there by the review's NOTE; filing it would need the primary
  papers, which the record does not hold.

## Choices made

- **Departing from three NOTEs.** [NOTE-416](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-416.md), [NOTE-415](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-415.md) and [NOTE-425](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-425.md) each
  end with "No new THEORY is indicated", meaning the claims are too weak
  to source a THEORY the record believes. Dissipative adaptation, gradient
  dissipation and the geochemical origin of life are each a definite
  account that the literature cites and that other THEORYs need to name.
  So they were filed as `Proposed`, each saying in its Source section that
  its NOTE judged it too weak, and each with a `promote_when` that names
  what would settle it and what cannot.
- **No `rivals` edges.** Schneider and Kay, and Morowitz and Smith, reject
  maximum entropy production, and Perunov et al. say maximizing mean
  dissipation is not predicted to be likely. None of the three argues the
  rejection in a way that makes the accounts unable both to be right:
  Schneider and Kay's restated law is compatible with a maximum among
  steady states. Each THEORY says so in Connections. Nor is any of them
  declared a rival of [THEORY-072](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md): the life-as-dissipation accounts frame
  the line between organism and dissipative structure as one of degree,
  but their claims are about tendencies and channels, not about that line.
- **`presupposes`, not `extends`.** Dissipative adaptation takes the Crooks
  relation and England's macrostate form as premises for a claim about
  something else. Planetary Gaia takes MEP as a premise, explicitly ("under
  the presumption that MEP is justified sufficiently well").
- **No `answers` edge.** [QUESTION-085](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-085.md), on whether an r/place artwork is
  self-maintaining, is the only question near this topic. None of these
  accounts answers it. The gradient-dissipation THEORY names it.
- **Corrections carried forward.** Each THEORY follows its NOTE's
  corrections: England's inverted logarithm and rounded RNA figure;
  Kleidon's three entropy-budget figures printed in W for mW; Schneider and
  Kay's inconsistent Table 2 entry; Seifert's §7.2 bound read with T.

## Existing THEORYs that might cite these readings

None should have had one of them as `source`. [THEORY-026](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md) and [THEORY-030](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-030.md)
each name several of these readings in their NOTEs as background, and the
NOTEs say explicitly that they are not sources. [NOTE-420](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-420.md) recommends that
[THEORY-026](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md) name Seifert ([LIT-523](../../record/literature.d/LIT-523.md)) in its Connections for the
protocol-level nonnegativity of its dissipation; that edit is left for a
separate change.

## Errors found in the record

None new. The NOTEs' own Corrections sections already record the errors in
the papers.

## Philosophy of science, part 2 of 2: eleven THEORYs from ten of fourteen readings

*2026-10-16 07:49:25 · curation · record*

The second half of the philosophy-of-science group in the THEORY backfill
the owner asked for on 2026-10-16. Fourteen LITs, each with a `Read` or
`Skimmed` NOTE and cited as no THEORY's `source`, were audited against
their readings. Nothing was fetched; every THEORY rests on the record's
NOTE, and its numbers and page references are the NOTE's.

## What entered

Eleven THEORYs, two `Active` and nine `Proposed`, from ten readings. The
codes are the temporary ones `luria new` assigned.

- **Two findings, `Active`.**
  - [THEORY-569](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-569.md), from [LIT-165](../../record/literature.d/LIT-165.md) (Hartmann & Trpin, [NOTE-168](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-168.md)): the
    set-valued CohOG+ measure of explanatory power satisfies TLI for
    single hypotheses, fails OLI, and in one chain and one collider ranks
    the richer explanans set higher over a stated range of priors. A
    theorem, a counterexample and two existence examples, all three
    numerical claims recomputed by the reader.
  - [THEORY-469](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-469.md), from [LIT-169](../../record/literature.d/LIT-169.md) (Trappes, [NOTE-155](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-155.md)): because
    persistence and selection are logically independent, NCT's
    evolutionary niche and the realized population ecological niche differ
    in extension. The non-identity is the finding; the three kinds of case
    that populate the gap are weaker and are said to be.
- **Nine accounts, `Proposed`.**
  - [THEORY-594](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-594.md), French on unitary inequivalence and OSR ([LIT-170](../../record/literature.d/LIT-170.md),
    [NOTE-162](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-162.md)).
  - [THEORY-491](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-491.md), Worrall on randomisation ([LIT-175](../../record/literature.d/LIT-175.md), [NOTE-126](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-126.md)).
  - [THEORY-418](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-418.md), Griesemer & Shavit's 3Cs ([LIT-188](../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md), [NOTE-173](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)). The
    LIT is itself `Proposed`, and the THEORY says the sketch has no
    operational criteria.
  - [THEORY-637](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-637.md), Leonelli on openness as sharing ([LIT-189](../../record/literature.d/LIT-189.md), [NOTE-098](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-098.md)).
  - [THEORY-690](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-690.md) and [THEORY-459](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-459.md), two accounts from De Haro &
    Butterfield ([LIT-199](../../record/literature.d/LIT-199.md), [NOTE-178](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-178.md)): dualities yield no genuine
    underdetermination and do not favour structural realism; and exact
    duality is incompatible with ontological emergence between the duals.
  - [THEORY-673](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-673.md), Luque on the Price equation as a generalization-sketch
    ([LIT-205](../../record/literature.d/LIT-205.md), [NOTE-101](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-101.md)).
  - [THEORY-451](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-451.md), Cartwright on singular causal claims and rigour
    ([LIT-213](../../record/literature.d/LIT-213.md), [NOTE-161](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-161.md)).
  - [THEORY-610](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-610.md), Worrall's 1989 structural realism ([LIT-315](../../record/literature.d/LIT-315.md),
    [NOTE-297](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-297.md)).

## What did not enter, and why

- **Wigner, Symmetry and Conservation Laws ([LIT-180](../../record/literature.d/LIT-180.md), [NOTE-147](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-147.md)).** The LIT
  is `Unavailable`, and the NOTE is a skim that says it is "not enough to
  state its assumptions or results exactly". A THEORY on it would have
  nothing to promote it against but the skim.
- **O'Malley & Parke, Philosophy of Microbiology ([LIT-210](../../record/literature.d/LIT-210.md), [NOTE-159](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-159.md)).** An
  SEP survey whose positions are reported and attributed. Its reading calls
  it "an orientation, not an argument for a thesis". Its own commitments
  (the contingency of zoocentrism, the deflation of microbiome-and-self
  claims) are graded weak or are disambiguations, not accounts. Its report
  that eukaryogenesis may not have been a transition in individuality is
  named in the Connections of [THEORY-418](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-418.md).
- **Piaget, Structuralism ([LIT-837](../../record/literature.d/LIT-837.md), [NOTE-618](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-618.md)).** A skim of 17 pages, one
  in four, of chs. I–IV. The NOTE files no THEORY and says why: the pages
  seen are definitional, and a quarter of four chapters cannot ground a
  claim about what is true.
- **Floridi, The Method of Levels of Abstraction ([LIT-900](../../record/literature.d/LIT-900.md), [NOTE-700](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-700.md)).** A
  method stated in definitions, not a result. Its one formal claim fails
  under its own definitions, and its guard against relativism ranks levels
  only within a fixed purpose. The NOTE files no THEORY, and [NOTE-099](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-099.md) filed
  none for the ISR paper that uses the same machinery.

So ten of fourteen readings became sources: ten of the twelve `Read`
NOTEs, and neither of the two skims. Of the two `Read` readings that
entered nothing, one is a survey and one a method. The owner's hypothesis
held for readings that argue a thesis, and not for surveys, methods or
skims. Nine of the eleven THEORYs are `Proposed`, because most of these
works argue rather than test.

## Choices made

- **Two THEORYs from one book.** De Haro & Butterfield's underdetermination
  and structural-realism verdict, and their emergence result, rest on
  different parts of the book and could fail separately, so each has its
  own document.
- **No `rivals`, `extends` or `presupposes`.** Worrall 2007 and Cartwright
  both deflate the evidence hierarchy, from different sides, and can both
  be right. French and De Haro & Butterfield concern different phenomena
  (inequivalent representations of one theory; dualities between models).
  Worrall 1989 is the epistemic position the ontic accounts start from, not
  a premise they take. These are stated in prose.
- **No `answers`.** Griesemer & Shavit's entrenchment-plus-closure
  criterion is a candidate for [QUESTION-035](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-035.md), but that question asks for a
  criterion that returns a verdict that can be wrong, and the sketch has no
  measurement; three readings of 2026-10-14 bearing on it were likewise not
  linked. Its closure is a mark of individuality, not agency, so it does
  not answer [QUESTION-093](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-093.md) either. Both are named in its Connections.
- **No existing THEORY duplicated these.** None of the record's 391
  THEORYs cites any of the fourteen LITs. [THEORY-034](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-034.md) and [THEORY-038](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-038.md) cover
  structural realism from Chakravartty's dilemma and category theory and do
  not state Worrall's, French's or De Haro & Butterfield's accounts.

## Errors found in the record, left for their owners

- **[LIT-175](../../record/literature.d/LIT-175.md)'s "Key takeaways"** still carries the seed's error that none of
  the standard arguments for randomisation, selection bias included,

  "cast-iron". The LIT's `summary` is right; its takeaway bullet is not.

- **[NOTE-161](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-161.md)** (Cartwright) says Worrall ([LIT-175](../../record/literature.d/LIT-175.md)) and Reiss ([LIT-118](../../record/literature.d/LIT-118.md)) are

- **[NOTE-173](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)** carries a directive for [LIT-188](../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md) that calls it `Deferred`

## Metaphysics and mereology: 13 THEORYs from 12 readings

*2026-10-16 07:50:27 · curation · record*

Part of the THEORY backfill the owner asked for, which audits read works
that no THEORY cites as `source`. This group was every such LIT with
`metaphysics` or `mereology` as its primary tag: eight and four, all
`Active`, each with one `Read` NOTE. The owner's hypothesis is that most
read works support at least one THEORY.

## What entered

Thirteen THEORYs, one `Active` and twelve `Proposed`. Codes are the
temporary ones `luria new` assigned. Each has a single source, the reading
it comes from.

- **Active.** [THEORY-493](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-493.md), from Varzi's SEP entry ([LIT-124](../../record/literature.d/LIT-124.md)): from core
  mereology, GEM is reached by exactly three pairings of decomposition and
  unrestricted-sum principles, and Simons's Supplementation + Sum3 is not
  one. It is a published result with a countermodel, reported by the entry
  with citations; the record has not checked the proofs, and the document
  says so.
- **Proposed, metaphysics.** Lewis on the problem of the many ([LIT-1015](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1015.md),
  [THEORY-452](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-452.md)). Holik et al. on quasi-sets for a non-individual
  property ontology ([LIT-107](../../record/literature.d/LIT-107.md), [THEORY-535](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-535.md)). Vetter's possibility
  conception of dispositions ([LIT-109](../../record/literature.d/LIT-109.md), [THEORY-670](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-670.md)). Hazelwood's
  dilemma for reciprocal causation ([LIT-156](../../record/literature.d/LIT-156.md), [THEORY-612](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-612.md)). Poltorak on
  wave-function realism and causal closure ([LIT-164](../../record/literature.d/LIT-164.md), [THEORY-485](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-485.md)).
  Watson's epistemic and ontological theses for unsupervised learning
  ([LIT-187](../../record/literature.d/LIT-187.md), [THEORY-556](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-556.md)). Schwitzgebel's Universal Bizarreness and
  Dubiety ([LIT-216](../../record/literature.d/LIT-216.md), [THEORY-506](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-506.md)). Esfeld and Lam's moderate structural
  realism ([LIT-895](../../record/literature.d/LIT-895.md), [THEORY-453](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-453.md)).
- **Proposed, mereology.** Smith and Varzi on fiat and bona fide boundaries
  ([LIT-1024](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1024.md), [THEORY-622](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-622.md)). Varzi's verdict that no mereological
  principle is merely meaning-fixing ([LIT-124](../../record/literature.d/LIT-124.md), [THEORY-589](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-589.md)). Register's
  depth of the moral body ([LIT-138](../../record/literature.d/LIT-138.md), [THEORY-540](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-540.md)). Levin's nested,
  goal-defined selves ([LIT-439](../../record/literature.d/LIT-439.md), [THEORY-583](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-583.md)).
- **`answers` edges.** [THEORY-583](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-583.md) partly answers [QUESTION-009](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-009.md): a pattern
  of coordination is an additional agent when shared information lets the
  parts pursue a goal none of them can sense. [THEORY-612](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-612.md) constrains
  [QUESTION-033](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-033.md): a level and the parts composing it at the same time are not
  independently fixable, so cannot be one another's causes.
  [THEORY-556](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-556.md) constrains [QUESTION-028](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-028.md): an algorithm's finding a category
  is evidence about it, and not what makes it a kind.

## What did not enter, and why

Nothing. All twelve readings became sources, which fits the owner's
hypothesis here. Three caveats apply.

- Most of the twelve are philosophical arguments, and their THEORYs are
  `Proposed` accounts whose `promote_when` names a kind of argument or
  construction, not an experiment. The data behind them are thin: Vetter's
  hand-coded corpus count, and Levin's cited experiments, which show that
  coupling changes outcomes, not that it changes a self.
- Three readings said "No THEORY" in their Bearing ([NOTE-125](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-125.md), [NOTE-137](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-137.md),
  [NOTE-112](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-112.md)). Each meant that no existing THEORY was supported. Each work
  states a definite thesis with its conditions, so each was filed.
- Varzi's entry gave two documents, one formal and one philosophical,
  because the result about axiom systems holds whatever "part" means and
  should not be cited as support for the verdict.

## Choices made

- **No relation edges to existing THEORYs.** `rivals`, `presupposes` and
  `extends` would have had `luria link --fix` write converses into
  documents this batch was told to leave alone. The candidates are named in
  each Connections instead: Levin against [THEORY-071](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-071.md) (minimal agency), which
  denies that a homeostat's individuality is agency; Hazelwood presupposing
  Woodward's interventions ([THEORY-138](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-138.md)); and Esfeld and Lam against the
  census in [THEORY-034](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-034.md).
- **No `answers` edge to [QUESTION-035](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-035.md)** from Lewis or from Smith and Varzi.
  Both classify or count the question's candidates, and neither supplies a
  criterion. The same for Schwitzgebel and [QUESTION-046](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-046.md).
- **Tags.** Vetter's THEORY adds `linguistics`, which [NOTE-125](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-125.md) called
  defensible because the positive case is built on '-able' semantics and a
  corpus count. Levin's leads with `mereology`, as his LIT does.

## Errors and gaps found in the record

- **[THEORY-034](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-034.md)'s title is out of date.** It says only Floridi's view, among
  the record's readings, keeps relata while denying them every intrinsic
  identity-fixing feature. Its own dated note says Esfeld and Lam
  ([LIT-895](../../record/literature.d/LIT-895.md)) are a second, which meets the first refutation condition of its
  `promote_when`. [LIT-895](../../record/literature.d/LIT-895.md) is argued from in its body but is not in its
  `source`.
- **[THEORY-043](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md) leans on Levin** ([LIT-439](../../record/literature.d/LIT-439.md)) as the composition-side statement
  for agency but does not cite it as `source`.
- **[LIT-124](../../record/literature.d/LIT-124.md)'s key takeaway still calls the partial-order core
  "uncontroversial".** [NOTE-163](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-163.md) recommends dropping that word, because the
  entry says the opposite.
- **[NOTE-163](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-163.md)'s Bearing says no THEORY cites mereology.** That is no longer
  true ([THEORY-017](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md), [THEORY-043](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md), [THEORY-232](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-232.md), and now this batch).
- **`luria repair` upgraded an old code spelling** in
  record/curation.d/2026/10/15/194615.md, a temporary code for what is now
  [CLAIM-315](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-315.md).
  The change was reverted here because that file is outside this batch;
  lint still reports it.

## Philosophy of science, part 1 of 2: 14 THEORYs from 13 readings

*2026-10-16 07:50:36 · curation · record*

The THEORY backfill continues with philosophy of science, split in two by
LIT. This half held fifteen LITs, each with a `Read` NOTE and none a
THEORY's `source`. Codes below are the temporary ones `luria new` assigned.

## What entered

Fourteen THEORYs, four `Active` and ten `Proposed`, from thirteen
readings.

- **Active, four.** The impossibility of strictly irreversible approach to
  equilibrium from isolated Hamiltonian dynamics, and how each surveyed
  account pays for it ([THEORY-463](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-463.md), [LIT-114](../../record/literature.d/LIT-114.md)). Belot's problem of time in
  spatially compact general relativity ([THEORY-441](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-441.md), [LIT-122](../../record/literature.d/LIT-122.md)). Inductive
  risk at the internal stages of the dioxin studies ([THEORY-639](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-639.md),
  [LIT-139](../../record/literature.d/LIT-139.md)). That clustering is not made superior by the absence of labels
  ([THEORY-550](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-550.md), [LIT-162](../../record/literature.d/LIT-162.md)).
- **Proposed, ten.** Health and disease not definable by justice alone
  ([THEORY-600](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-600.md), [LIT-098](../../record/literature.d/LIT-098.md)). Niche construction unrolled into an acyclic
  organism–environment sequence ([THEORY-446](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-446.md), [LIT-110](../../record/literature.d/LIT-110.md)). The common core
  does not break duality underdetermination without a metaphysical
  principle ([THEORY-687](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-687.md), [LIT-113](../../record/literature.d/LIT-113.md)). Warrant as elimination of
  alternatives ([THEORY-537](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-537.md), [LIT-118](../../record/literature.d/LIT-118.md)). The Fractured Understanding
  Hypothesis ([THEORY-438](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-438.md), [LIT-131](../../record/literature.d/LIT-131.md)). Values required, and only
  indirectly, where consequences of error are foreseeable ([THEORY-442](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-442.md),
  [LIT-139](../../record/literature.d/LIT-139.md)). Brain–computer interface evidence fits mind–brain identity, not
  autonomous mental causation ([THEORY-410](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-410.md), [LIT-147](../../record/literature.d/LIT-147.md)). Genes as
  reproducees, and material overlap required of reproducers only
  ([THEORY-465](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-465.md), [LIT-157](../../record/literature.d/LIT-157.md)). Lloyd's four roles in "unit of selection"
  ([THEORY-413](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-413.md), [LIT-160](../../record/literature.d/LIT-160.md)). Replication cannot say which effect exists
  where the effect is unformed ([THEORY-572](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-572.md), [LIT-161](../../record/literature.d/LIT-161.md)).
- **Relations.** [THEORY-442](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-442.md) `presupposes` [THEORY-639](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-639.md).
  [THEORY-410](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-410.md) `presupposes` [THEORY-133](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-133.md) (List and Menzies) and
  `answers` [QUESTION-033](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-033.md), as a constraint: many-to-one realisation shows
  some coarse variable drives, not that the named higher level does.
  `luria link --fix` wrote the converses into [THEORY-133](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-133.md) and [QUESTION-033](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-033.md).
  No `rivals` were declared. Lloyd and Bourrat disagree about "Darwinian
  individual", but Bourrat's term concerns the reproducer role alone, so
  the two accounts can both be right.

## What did not enter, and why

- **Mallory, stochastic measuring devices ([LIT-140](../../record/literature.d/LIT-140.md), [NOTE-090](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-090.md)).** The
  headline is an analogy, and the author concedes the agentive analogy it
  opposes "can't be refuted" (p. 15). Its reading calls it "an alternative
  image, not a demonstration". Its sharper points, strong against weak
  model content and seed-dependence as a failure of instrument regularity,
  belong to the ML literature it cites, as the reading says. There was no
  claim that could come out wrong.
- **Angius et al., transformer success ([LIT-153](../../record/literature.d/LIT-153.md), [NOTE-106](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-106.md)).** A survey that
  assimilates published studies to Cummins, mechanistic and simulative
  explanation, with no new analysis and no counter-cases. Its reading says
  it should not be a source; its one firm caution (ICL "mechanism" papers
  often give mathematical equivalences) is better sourced from the primary
  papers.

So thirteen of fifteen readings became sources, which fits the owner's
hypothesis. Two caveats. Two of the thirteen readings said outright that
the work "supports no THEORY document directly" ([NOTE-152](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-152.md), [NOTE-103](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-103.md)), and
the SEP-style surveys ([LIT-114](../../record/literature.d/LIT-114.md), [LIT-160](../../record/literature.d/LIT-160.md)) needed the most narrowing to
yield a claim that could be wrong. For [LIT-113](../../record/literature.d/LIT-113.md) the account filed is the
survey's central conditional verdict, which its reading rates moderate.
And [LIT-139](../../record/literature.d/LIT-139.md) gave two THEORYs, because its descriptive finding is well
supported and its normative claim rests on a premise it leaves unargued.

## Choices made

- **Status.** `Active` for a proved result ([LIT-122](../../record/literature.d/LIT-122.md)'s vanishing
  Hamiltonian, [LIT-114](../../record/literature.d/LIT-114.md)'s constancy of fine-grained Gibbs entropy and
  recurrence), or a finding described with its scope ([LIT-139](../../record/literature.d/LIT-139.md)'s dioxin
  cases, [LIT-162](../../record/literature.d/LIT-162.md)'s counterexamples). `Proposed` for every account its
  reading calls argued, illustrated or untested. For the philosophical
  accounts `promote_when` names the kind of case analysis or survey that
  would bear on them, and says that more illustrations cannot.
- **Corrections followed.** Each THEORY follows its NOTE's corrections of
  the seeded skims: Veit makes no concession on p. 17; in Bourrat control
  comes "for free" in scaffolded collectives and autonomy is what evolves;
  Freeborn's Othello verdict breaks his own bridge-principle condition.
- **Back-references.** `luria link --fix` added `presupposed_by` to
  [THEORY-133](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-133.md) and `answered_by` to [QUESTION-033](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-033.md). Those are the only edits to
  files this batch did not create.

## Errors found in the record

- `luria repair` wanted to upgrade a stale code in
  record/curation.d/2026/10/15/194615.md: it still cites the temporary
  code of what is now [CLAIM-315](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-315.md). Left for the owner's branch, since that
  file is outside this batch.
- No errors were found in the fifteen NOTEs beyond those they already
  correct. Existing THEORYs that cite these LITs in prose ([THEORY-030](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-030.md) for
  [LIT-114](../../record/literature.d/LIT-114.md); [THEORY-048](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-048.md), [THEORY-053](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-053.md), [THEORY-057](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-057.md), [THEORY-058](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-058.md) and [THEORY-133](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-133.md) for
  [LIT-147](../../record/literature.d/LIT-147.md)) cite them as caveats, not as evidence, so none should have
  listed them as `source`.

## Self, personhood and individuation, in the THEORY backfill: fourteen THEORYs from sixteen readings

*2026-10-16 07:54:49 · curation · record*

The THEORY backfill continues by topic group (moral psychology was first,
071404). This group took the sixteen LITs tagged `self`, `personhood` or
`individuation` that had a `Read` NOTE and no THEORY citing them as
`source`. [ADR-024](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-024.md) keeps agent, individual, self and person apart, and the
tags follow it: persistence and what matters went to `personhood`, what a
self is to `self`, and counting organisms and their parts to
`individuation`.

## What entered

Fourteen THEORYs, one `Active` and thirteen `Proposed`. The codes are the
temporary ones `luria new` assigned.

- **Persons over time.**
  - Parfit's division argument ([THEORY-447](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-447.md)), from [LIT-447](../../record/literature.d/LIT-447.md) with Olson's
    survey ([LIT-454](../../record/literature.d/LIT-454.md)).
  - Lewis's stage reply ([THEORY-476](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-476.md)), from [LIT-446](../../record/literature.d/LIT-446.md).
  - Williams's first-person series ([THEORY-531](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-531.md)), from [LIT-462](../../record/literature.d/LIT-462.md).
  - The psychological-continuity criterion ([THEORY-546](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-546.md)), from Locke
    ([LIT-464](../../record/literature.d/LIT-464.md)), with the repairs as [LIT-454](../../record/literature.d/LIT-454.md) and [LIT-447](../../record/literature.d/LIT-447.md) give them.
  - Floridi's level-of-abstraction deflation ([THEORY-650](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-650.md)), from [LIT-136](../../record/literature.d/LIT-136.md).
  - Dufner's map of identity and ethics ([THEORY-464](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-464.md)), from [LIT-130](../../record/literature.d/LIT-130.md).
  - Olson's seven questions of personal identity ([THEORY-417](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-417.md)), from
    [LIT-454](../../record/literature.d/LIT-454.md). This is the one `Active` THEORY: a conceptual map the record
    holds as stated.
- **Selves.**
  - Hume's bundle and the fiction of identity ([THEORY-681](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-681.md)), from
    [LIT-451](../../record/literature.d/LIT-451.md).
  - Dennett's centre of narrative gravity ([THEORY-691](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-691.md)), from [LIT-442](../../record/literature.d/LIT-442.md).
  - Strawson against narrativity ([THEORY-684](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-684.md)), from [LIT-452](../../record/literature.d/LIT-452.md).
  - Gallagher's ownership and agency in the minimal self
    ([THEORY-458](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-458.md)), from [LIT-453](../../record/literature.d/LIT-453.md).
  - The context-fixed referent of a chat agent's "I" ([THEORY-490](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-490.md)), from
    Shanahan 2025 ([LIT-466](../../record/literature.d/LIT-466.md)) with the role-play paper ([LIT-460](../../record/literature.d/LIT-460.md)).
- **Individuation.**
  - Meincke's critique of parthood under substance ontology and her count
    between one and two ([THEORY-448](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-448.md)), from [LIT-142](../../record/literature.d/LIT-142.md).
  - Wilson and Barker's separation of Darwinian from physiological
    individuality ([THEORY-443](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-443.md)), from [LIT-168](../../record/literature.d/LIT-168.md).
- **Relations.**
  - `rivals`: Parfit against Lewis, and Parfit against Williams.
  - `presupposes`: Dufner on Parfit.
  - `answers`: [QUESTION-043](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-043.md) from the continuity criterion and from Strawson;
    [QUESTION-035](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-035.md) from Meincke and from Wilson and Barker. Each constrains
    its question rather than answering it, and each Connections section
    says how.

## What did not enter, and why

- **Dennett, "Where Am I?" ([LIT-405](../../record/literature.d/LIT-405.md), [NOTE-338](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-338.md)).** Its reading calls it
  intuition pumps with no thesis defended to the end. The official answer,
  that a person is where his point of view is, is "tentative, offered with
  stated doubts". The duplicate is stipulated, and the ending, two persons
  once the brains drift apart, is "illustrated", the punch line and not an
  argument. There is no finding to state. Its cases (Yorick, Hamlet,
  Hubert) would serve better as a CASE, if the record's own argument needs
  them a second time.

So fifteen of sixteen readings became sources, which fits the owner's
hypothesis for this group. The caveats: thirteen of the fourteen are
`Proposed`. Most are philosophical accounts whose `promote_when` names a
kind of argument that would settle them; for Gallagher, Strawson and
Shanahan it names a kind of study. One NOTE said no THEORY was indicated:
[NOTE-370](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-370.md), for the role-play paper, unless joined with a reading that
answers its question. That paper entered only as the second source of
Shanahan's 2025 account, which is the pairing [NOTE-370](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-370.md) names.

## Choices made

- **Surveys.** The three SEP entries were read as surveys, and the account
  filed from each is the reading's own synthesis or the entry's own
  argument, not a position it reports. For Olson that is the map of
  questions, not his animalism. The too-many-thinkers objection is set out
  in the continuity criterion's "does not say", since the animalist book
  ([LIT-448](../../record/literature.d/LIT-448.md)) is unread.
- **No relations to existing THEORYs.** This filing touches no existing
  THEORY. Where an existing one is a rival or a neighbour, the body says so
  in prose: [THEORY-060](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-060.md) against Strawson, [THEORY-322](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-322.md) beside Gallagher, and
  [THEORY-064](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-064.md) beside Hume.
- **Back-references.** `luria link --fix` wrote `answered_by` into
  [QUESTION-035](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-035.md) and [QUESTION-043](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-043.md), and `presupposed_by` into the Parfit THEORY.
- **A dropped rivalry.** Dennett and Strawson were not made `rivals`.
  Strawson's grid credits Dennett with falsifying revision, which [NOTE-364](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-364.md)
  and [NOTE-383](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-383.md) both doubt, and the two disagree about how widely people
  narrate, not about the same claim.

## Errors found in the record
