## natural-sciences: 10 THEORYs from 17 readings

*2026-10-16 08:02:46 · curation · record*

Part of the THEORY backfill audit. The natural-sciences topic group held
seventeen LITs with a `Read` or `Skimmed` NOTE and no THEORY citing them as
`source`. Each was re-read from its NOTE and LIT to decide whether the
reading supports one or more THEORY documents. The owner's hypothesis is
that a work read closely enough to carry a NOTE usually supports at least
one THEORY.

Ten of the seventeen became a THEORY's source. The seven that did not are
the group's reviews, a dated forecast, an unrefereed single-study preprint,
and two crystallization papers whose readings route their content to the
record's own CLAIMs instead. So the hypothesis held for ten of seventeen
here, weaker than for the moral-psychology batch, and the misses are
explained by what kind of work each is, not by shallow reading.

## What entered

Ten THEORYs: six `Active`, four `Proposed`.

- **The cooperation lineage (six).** Filed from the works
  morality-as-cooperation cites as its biological sources, read as biology,
  not as morality. Hamilton Part I ([THEORY-408](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-408.md), Active, [LIT-497](../../record/literature.d/LIT-497.md)):
  inclusive fitness and the −k > 1/r threshold. Hamilton Part II
  ([THEORY-655](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-655.md), Proposed, [LIT-506](../../record/literature.d/LIT-506.md), extends Part I): the two
  principles and the haplodiploidy hypothesis, "unrigorous" and anecdotally
  tested. Maynard Smith & Price ([THEORY-466](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-466.md), Active, [LIT-505](../../record/literature.d/LIT-505.md)):
  the ESS and limited war, with the correction that Retaliator only ties
  Mouse and that there is no Hawk-Dove game here. Trivers ([THEORY-663](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-663.md),
  Proposed, [LIT-510](../../record/literature.d/LIT-510.md)): reciprocal altruism and the moral emotions that
  regulate it. Axelrod & Hamilton ([THEORY-672](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-672.md), Active, [LIT-498](../../record/literature.d/LIT-498.md)):
  TIT FOR TAT's stability condition on w, with the neutral-stability
  caveat. Nowak ([THEORY-567](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-567.md), Active, [LIT-501](../../record/literature.d/LIT-501.md), extends the Hamilton
  and Axelrod accounts): the five b/c-threshold mechanisms, altruism only.
- **Four more.** The Eulalia impact shower ([THEORY-499](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-499.md), Proposed,
  [LIT-009](../../record/literature.d/LIT-009.md)): a plausibility model, most-favourable solution only,
  cluster date inherited from Copernicus. The individualized niche
  ([THEORY-473](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-473.md), Active, [LIT-127](../../record/literature.d/LIT-127.md)): a framework its own authors call
  metaphorical, whose central quantity has no individual-level estimate.
  REST2 convergence ([THEORY-562](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-562.md), Proposed, [LIT-076](../../record/literature.d/LIT-076.md)): swap
  acceptance measures ladder mixing, not sampling. The Belousov-Zhabotinsky
  oscillation ([THEORY-508](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-508.md), Active, [LIT-531](../../record/literature.d/LIT-531.md)): the relaxation-cycle
  mechanism, with the closed-versus-open distinction that matters for using
  BZ as a dissipative structure.

The six `Active` are Hamilton Part I (a result proved under stated
assumptions), Axelrod & Hamilton (a described model whose stability
condition the record believes, with the neutral-stability caveat kept in
the title), Nowak (the compact map of mechanisms), Maynard Smith & Price
(the ESS and limited-war result), the BZ mechanism, and the niche framework
as a description of its own structure. The four `Proposed` are the Eulalia
model (a plausibility argument its authors do not call proof), Hamilton
Part II (the author's own "unrigorous"), Trivers (functional reasoning
fitted to 1960s findings), and REST2 (argued, with a passing example and no
failed-run counterexample).

## What did not enter, and why

- **Concussion review ([LIT-029](../../record/literature.d/LIT-029.md), [NOTE-858](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-858.md)).** A narrative review whose
  claims are other studies', and whose one conclusion is a dated statement
  of ignorance: as of 2017 the long-term risk of repetitive concussion was
  unmeasured by any design able to measure it. No account to state.
- **Rigorous RG ([LIT-039](../../record/literature.d/LIT-039.md), [NOTE-821](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-821.md)).** A Comment that reports others'
  results. The one result fit to file, 4D φ⁴ triviality, belongs to
  Aizenman and Duminil-Copin's paper, which the record does not hold.
- **The Strongest El Niño ([LIT-059](../../record/literature.d/LIT-059.md), [NOTE-031](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-031.md)).** A dated, unverified
  forecast in a blog post. Nothing in the record rests on it, and the event
  it forecasts is now checkable against observation instead.
- **Gut microbiota and appetite ([LIT-903](../../record/literature.d/LIT-903.md), [NOTE-706](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-706.md)).** A narrative
  review, mostly rodent and in vitro by its authors' own statement. Its
  content is already held as `grounds` for the owner's [CLAIM-166](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-166.md), not as a
  standalone finding about the world.
- **A. baumannii oxidative-stress preprint ([LIT-852](../../record/literature.d/LIT-852.md), [NOTE-656](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-656.md)).** A
  single unrefereed bioRxiv preprint whose central claim is assembled from
  reporters, correlative detection and simulation rather than observed end
  to end. The reading explicitly declines a THEORY: the claim is exactly the
  kind [THEORY-136](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-136.md) counsels holding at arm's length.
- **Vekilov, Nucleation ([LIT-919](../../record/literature.d/LIT-919.md), [NOTE-708](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-708.md)) and Ostwald, rule of
  stages ([LIT-920](../../record/literature.d/LIT-920.md), [NOTE-709](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-709.md)).** Both readings state in terms that
  no THEORY should be filed from them, and both route their physical content
  to the record's own CLAIMs about argument nucleation ([CLAIM-176](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-176.md),
  [CLAIM-181](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md), [CLAIM-185](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md), [CLAIM-186](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-186.md)) as evidence via their `supports`
  edges. Vekilov's two-step mechanism rests on one protein and a fitted
  model; Ostwald's rule is "a frequently applicable rule", not a law, on a
  handful of cases. The [NOTE-709](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-709.md) verdict names [LIT-920](../../record/literature.d/LIT-920.md) as the primary source
  if the record later states a rule-of-stages THEORY; this audit does not.

## Choices made

- **Status.** `Active` only where the record believes the account as
  stated: a proved result, a described model with its scope, or a
  mechanism supported by a confirming test. `Proposed` where the reading
  marks the account argued, untested, one-system or (for the Eulalia model)
  a plausibility argument. Each Proposed THEORY names a kind of result that
  would settle it and says what cannot.
- **Topic tags.** The group's primary tag `natural-sciences` leads every
  THEORY, with the secondary tags the readings carry (`mathematics`,
  `game-theory`, `complex-systems`, `ecology`, `philosophy-of-biology`,
  `probabilistic-modeling`, `emotion-and-affect`, `moral-psychology`).
  Following [ADR-018](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-018.md), the cooperation sources read as biology are not
  tagged `moral-psychology` except Trivers, whose human section is itself an
  account of moral emotion.
- **No `answers` edges.** None of the ten answers a QUESTION of the
  record's own closely enough to warrant the link; the overlaps are
  topical, not answering.
- **Relations between the new THEORYs.** `extends` edges where one account
  builds on another's mechanism: Hamilton Part II and Nowak extend Hamilton
  Part I, and Nowak extends Axelrod & Hamilton. No `rivals` edges: these
  accounts of cooperation are complementary, not competing.

## Errors found in the record

- **The Hawk-Dove attribution.** Morality-as-cooperation ([LIT-503](../../record/literature.d/LIT-503.md)) and
  [NOTE-034](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-034.md) credit hawk-dove contests to Maynard Smith & Price (1973).
  That paper ([LIT-505](../../record/literature.d/LIT-505.md), [NOTE-404](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-404.md)) has no Hawk-Dove game; its
  strategies are Mouse, Hawk, Bully, Retaliator and Prober-Retaliator, and
  "dove" does not occur. This is already recorded as a correction in
  [NOTE-404](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-404.md) and is carried into [THEORY-466](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-466.md); noted here for the
  benefit of the morality-as-cooperation account ([THEORY-468](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-468.md)), which
  repeats the lineage.
- **`luria repair` edited a file outside this batch.** It upgraded a stale
  placeholder code (`CLAIM-tmp3bdbx` → `CLAIM-315`) in
  `record/curation.d/2026/10/15/194615.md`, another batch's curation entry.
  That change was reverted here to avoid touching other agents' files in
  parallel worktrees; the repair can be rerun on the main branch.

## Society and governance: eleven THEORYs from eleven readings

*2026-10-16 18:01:55 · curation · record*

The THEORY backfill reached society-and-governance. Twenty LITs with that
primary tag had a `Read` NOTE and were no THEORY's `source`. Each NOTE was
read in full with its LIT, and existing THEORYs (including the first
round's `THEORY-tmp…` codes), QUESTIONs and CLAIMs were searched for the
same accounts.

## What entered

Eleven THEORYs, one `Active` and ten `Proposed`, from eleven readings.
Codes are the temporary ones `luria new` assigned.

- **One finding, `Active`.** The EEAS's 2024 FIMI sample: of 2,055
  channels recurring across incidents, 76.5% are not attributed to a state
  ([THEORY-659](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-659.md), from [LIT-084](../../record/literature.d/LIT-084.md)). The title carries the two limits the
  reading found: the sample is the EEAS's own and not representative, and
  the 76.5% is a share of a filtered graph, which the report's conclusions
  restate as a share of all channels.
- **Ten accounts, `Proposed`.**
  - The Google remedies opinion's account of scale as the fruit of
    exclusive distribution, remedied by sharing raw data rather than by
    divestiture ([THEORY-480](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-480.md), [LIT-006](../../record/literature.d/LIT-006.md)).
  - Doctorow's four constraints on platform decay ([THEORY-470](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-470.md),
    [LIT-033](../../record/literature.d/LIT-033.md)), filed as `extends` [THEORY-150](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-150.md), the 2023 enshittification
    cycle, because the talk adds a cause the essay lacks.
  - Competitive authoritarianism as relayed by Drezner from Levitsky and
    Way ([THEORY-440](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-440.md), [LIT-022](../../record/literature.d/LIT-022.md)). It rests on a relay, and says so.
  - Clark's reading of Russian "hybrid war" as a category defined by
    objective ([THEORY-488](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-488.md), [LIT-023](../../record/literature.d/LIT-023.md)), and Fridman's account of the
    narrative of a Western information war as politicised by many actors
    rather than directed ([THEORY-551](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-551.md), [LIT-088](../../record/literature.d/LIT-088.md) with [LIT-023](../../record/literature.d/LIT-023.md) second).
  - DISINFOX's mapping of DISARM incidents into standard STIX
    ([THEORY-651](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-651.md), [LIT-083](../../record/literature.d/LIT-083.md)). The demonstration is strong, but the LIT is
    a `Proposed` preprint, so the account is `Proposed` and carries an
    `inactive-ok-file` directive.
  - Algorithmic nudging needs mechanism-level oversight ([THEORY-627](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-627.md),
    [LIT-179](../../record/literature.d/LIT-179.md)).
  - Gelman's incentive account of visible falsehood ([THEORY-423](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-423.md),
    [LIT-014](../../record/literature.d/LIT-014.md)), Thompson's dispositional account of who goes Nazi
    ([THEORY-483](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-483.md), [LIT-055](../../record/literature.d/LIT-055.md)), and Moynihan's account of selective
    shutdowns as a transfer of the power of the purse ([THEORY-533](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-533.md),
    [LIT-061](../../record/literature.d/LIT-061.md)). All three are argued from chosen cases or vignettes, and
    each `promote_when` names the measurement that could settle it.

## What did not enter, and why

- **Primary legal and governmental records that decide or find nothing
  general.** The Minnesota show-cause transcript ([LIT-012](../../record/literature.d/LIT-012.md)), whose reading
  says citing it for a holding would be an error; the Broadview grand-jury
  transcript ([LIT-065](../../record/literature.d/LIT-065.md)); the Kerr County commissioners' transcript
  ([LIT-078](../../record/literature.d/LIT-078.md)). Each is a record of what was said, with no finding to state.
- **Doctrine.** Joint Publication 3-12 ([LIT-015](../../record/literature.d/LIT-015.md)) is definitional, "doctrine
  by stipulation" in its reading, with the operative authorities classified.
- **Commentary on single legal events.** Law Dork on the D.V.D. order
  ([LIT-052](../../record/literature.d/LIT-052.md)) and Vance on DOJ's reversal ([LIT-092](../../record/literature.d/LIT-092.md)). Their claims are
  readings of one order or filing, or predictions.
- **A district-court order under appeal.** The Rhode Island subpoena order
  ([LIT-024](../../record/literature.d/LIT-024.md)). Its holdings are contested in the First Circuit, one of the
  decisions it followed has been reversed, and its reading says not to cite
  it as settled. Its remedy point, that segregating a protected subgroup
  discloses membership, is a familiar de-identification fact stated as a
  legal finding, not a result of the order.
- **A weak result.** The Mothership post ([LIT-060](../../record/literature.d/LIT-060.md)). Its headline 1.6% is
  not reproducible from the published code, and the numerator is likely
  truncated. The LIT is `Proposed` with a `promote_when` that already names
  the run that would settle it; a THEORY would restate a number the record
  doubts.
- **A vendor's claim relayed by trade press.** The NEWSCASTER report
  ([LIT-072](../../record/literature.d/LIT-072.md)): one source, circumstantial attribution, no measure of effect.

So eleven of twenty readings became sources, and [LIT-023](../../record/literature.d/LIT-023.md) serves two. The
owner's hypothesis held for the argued and analytic works (eleven of
twelve, the exception being the irreproducible Mothership post). It did
not hold for the eight primary records, doctrine and single-event
commentary, which make up this topic's other half.

## Choices made

- **Proposed over Active.** Only the EEAS finding is `Active`, as a
  description of a coded sample with its limits in the title. Every account
  here is argued from chosen cases, relayed, or (DISINFOX) rests on a
  `Proposed` preprint.
- **No `answers` edges.** [QUESTION-070](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-070.md) names [LIT-179](../../record/literature.d/LIT-179.md)'s RL agent and
  [LIT-084](../../record/literature.d/LIT-084.md)'s tiered network as its two cases of manipulation with no
  intending member. The nudging and EEAS THEORYs describe those cases and
  name the question in Connections; neither says what manipulation is, so
  neither answers it. [QUESTION-119](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-119.md) is named from the Fridman account as a
  case, not an answer.
- **No `rivals` edges.** Clark and Fridman agree on the narrative and on
  its not being merely cynical, and differ in corpus. They are neighbours,
  not rivals; the Fridman account cites Clark as a second source.
- **No source added to [THEORY-150](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-150.md).** It already names [LIT-033](../../record/literature.d/LIT-033.md) in prose as a
  restatement. The talk's new causal claim is filed separately so that it
  can fail without taking the cycle with it.

## Errors found in the record

- [LIT-088](../../record/literature.d/LIT-088.md)'s seeded section still says the held *Russian Hybrid Warfare*
  "appears to be Fridman's own book". [NOTE-070](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-070.md) corrects this: [LIT-023](../../record/literature.d/LIT-023.md) is
  Clark's ISW report, and Fridman's book is not held. The passage is
  labelled as what the seeding asked, so it was left.
- The source errors already caught in the NOTEs are carried into the
  THEORYs as corrections, not repeated: Doctorow's "DC Circuit" and his
  account of the DMA as an "Act"; the EEAS conclusions' restatement of the
  76.5%; Fridman's doctrine-to-law ordering.

## Mathematics: eighteen THEORYs from twenty-one readings

*2026-10-16 18:03:37 · curation · record*

The THEORY backfill reached the mathematics group: twenty-one LITs with a
`Read` or `Skimmed` NOTE and no THEORY citing them as `source`. Each NOTE was
read in full, with its LIT. The papers were not fetched; every THEORY rests
on the record's reading. The caller's ruling for this group was that a
proved result, stated with its conditions, can be `Active`.

## What entered

Eighteen THEORYs, fifteen `Active` and three `Proposed`. Codes are the
temporary ones `luria new` assigned.

- **Operator theory and analysis, `Active`.** Spectral sets: the spectrum
  controls ‖f(A)‖ only for diagonalisable A, the numerical range always,
  with K ∈ [2, 11.08] ([THEORY-530](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-530.md), [LIT-011](../../record/literature.d/LIT-011.md)). The Mizohata–Takeuchi
  counterexample with log R loss ([THEORY-685](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-685.md), [LIT-030](../../record/literature.d/LIT-030.md)). Oseledets and
  Karlsson–Ledrappier ([THEORY-407](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-407.md), [LIT-093](../../record/literature.d/LIT-093.md)). Riesz representation,
  with Riesz 1907 as the existence-only priority note ([THEORY-629](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-629.md),
  [LIT-243](../../record/literature.d/LIT-243.md) and [LIT-326](../../record/literature.d/LIT-326.md)). Walsh's system and its Fourier-like convergence
  ([THEORY-620](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-620.md), [LIT-300](../../record/literature.d/LIT-300.md)).
- **Algebra and duality, `Active`.** Wedderburn's structure theorem
  ([THEORY-652](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-652.md), [LIT-309](../../record/literature.d/LIT-309.md)). Gelfand–Naimark ([THEORY-592](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-592.md), [LIT-313](../../record/literature.d/LIT-313.md)).
  Pontryagin duality in its compact/discrete form ([THEORY-645](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-645.md),
  [LIT-333](../../record/literature.d/LIT-333.md)). Eckart–Young ([THEORY-503](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-503.md), [LIT-330](../../record/literature.d/LIT-330.md)). Zaslavsky's region
  count ([THEORY-430](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-430.md), [LIT-355](../../record/literature.d/LIT-355.md)).
- **Type theory, `Active`.** The Segal condition and the dependent Yoneda
  lemma in simplicial type theory, with its sketched semantics in the title
  ([THEORY-544](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-544.md), [LIT-032](../../record/literature.d/LIT-032.md)). Conservativity of two-level type theory over
  HoTT ([THEORY-642](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-642.md), [LIT-095](../../record/literature.d/LIT-095.md)).
- **Games, control and compositionality, `Active`.** Debreu's existence
  theorem for generalized games ([THEORY-437](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-437.md), [LIT-067](../../record/literature.d/LIT-067.md)). LQR's
  return-difference margins and their loss under an observer
  ([THEORY-654](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-654.md), [LIT-051](../../record/literature.d/LIT-051.md)). Backprop as a functor ([THEORY-519](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-519.md),
  [LIT-827](../../record/literature.d/LIT-827.md)).
- **`Proposed`.** Spectral networks and Family Floer theory, from an
  unrefereed preprint whose analytic core the reader could not check
  ([THEORY-486](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-486.md), [LIT-017](../../record/literature.d/LIT-017.md)). Generative effects and left adjoints, from a
  `Skimmed` NOTE ([THEORY-686](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-686.md), [LIT-803](../../record/literature.d/LIT-803.md)). Diffusion maps, from a
  `Skimmed` NOTE whose equations were not seen ([THEORY-565](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-565.md), [LIT-981](../../record/literature.d/LIT-981.md)),
  with `answers: QUESTION-052` for the symmetric half only.

## What did not enter, and why

- **[LIT-064](../../record/literature.d/LIT-064.md) (Chu & Raginsky, [NOTE-046](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-046.md)).** Moved to the anthology as
  [ANTH-LIT-726](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-726.md) at the owner's request, with the reading. A THEORY here
  would hold one reading in two places.
- **[LIT-237](../../record/literature.d/LIT-237.md) (bra–ket notation, [NOTE-855](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-855.md)).** The NOTE files none: the
  article adds no claim, and its one substantive point, that the bracket is
  an inner product only where Riesz holds, is the Riesz theorem. That point
  is in [THEORY-629](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-629.md)'s "does not say", citing [NOTE-855](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-855.md).
- **[LIT-040](../../record/literature.d/LIT-040.md) (nLab, two-level type theory).** Superseded by [LIT-095](../../record/literature.d/LIT-095.md). Its NOTE
  read the paper, and the THEORY is sourced to [LIT-095](../../record/literature.d/LIT-095.md), not to the page.
  [LIT-095](../../record/literature.d/LIT-095.md) has no NOTE of its own; its reading is [NOTE-047](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-047.md).

So nineteen of twenty-one readings now carry a THEORY, counting [LIT-040](../../record/literature.d/LIT-040.md)
through [LIT-095](../../record/literature.d/LIT-095.md). That fits the owner's hypothesis for this group, with a
caveat: most of these are classical theorems, and five NOTEs had declined
a THEORY outright ([LIT-237](../../record/literature.d/LIT-237.md), [LIT-243](../../record/literature.d/LIT-243.md), [LIT-803](../../record/literature.d/LIT-803.md), [LIT-827](../../record/literature.d/LIT-827.md), [LIT-981](../../record/literature.d/LIT-981.md)), mostly on
the ground that a standard theorem need not be stated separately.
The filed THEORYs earn their place mainly in "What this does not say":
Eckart–Young gives no uniqueness of factors, Riesz 1907 states no
uniqueness, Walsh 1923 has no characters, Pontryagin 1934 has no general
LCA duality, Gelfand–Naimark has no categorical duality, and Stanley has no
topes. Those are the points the owner's prior-art map leans on.

## Choices made

- **Overriding four NOTEs' "No THEORY".** [NOTE-854](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-854.md) says the Riesz theorem
  is standard and should be cited to a textbook, and [NOTE-289](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-289.md) that a modern
  proof supersedes the 1907 note as a source. The THEORY
  states it with the conditions [LIT-243](../../record/literature.d/LIT-243.md) proves, and records that advice.
  [NOTE-625](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-625.md) declined a THEORY on Backprop as Functor because a claim about
  backpropagation is the anthology's side. The anthology does not hold the
  paper, and the THEORY states the compositional theorem, not an
  instruction; the reason is recorded in its "does not say". [NOTE-601](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-601.md) and
  [NOTE-784](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-784.md) are `Skimmed`, so their THEORYs are `Proposed` and say so.
- **One THEORY for two Riesz readings.** The 1907 note is the priority
  source and the REU paper the proof; neither alone carries the account.
- **[LIT-017](../../record/literature.d/LIT-017.md) stays `Proposed`, and so does its THEORY.** The statements are
  narrowed to what the proofs cover: exact Betti Lagrangians, finite
  creative networks. Theorem 5 is left out.
- **No new `rivals` or `extends`.** Riehl–Shulman and two-level type theory
  are alternative answers to one question, and both can be right; they name
  each other in Connections.
- **Outside facts flagged as outside.** The 1 + √2 Crouzeix–Palencia bound,
  Frobenius's theorem on real division algebras and Schmidt's 1907 priority
  for low-rank approximation are named as not verified in the record.

## Edits to existing documents

## What entered

Thirteen THEORYs, three `Active` and ten `Proposed`, from fifteen of the
eighteen readings. Codes are the temporary ones `luria new` assigned.

- **Three findings, `Active`.**

    ([THEORY-461](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-461.md)), from [LIT-207](../../record/literature.d/LIT-207.md).
- **`rivals` edges.** Turing and Dennett each rival Block's psychologism
  ([THEORY-092](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-092.md)), and Dennett rivals Searle. [THEORY-092](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-092.md) had said that if the
  record filed a behavioural criterion as a theory, it would correct it.
  `rivals` was chosen instead of `corrects` because all three are
  Proposed and the lookup machine is itself the point in dispute
  ([ADR-022](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-022.md)).

## What did not enter, and why

- **The world-models editorial ([LIT-195](../../record/literature.d/LIT-195.md), [NOTE-136](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-136.md)).** It argues nothing of
  its own. Its three senses of "world model" are posed conditionally, each
  anchored to one citation, and its verdicts are glosses on seventeen
  contributions the record has not read. A THEORY would rest on readings
  the record does not hold.
- **K-lines ([LIT-402](../../record/literature.d/LIT-402.md), [NOTE-352](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-352.md)).** The NOTE says "No THEORY in the record
  should rest on this memo". The reason is that it has no finding: the
  memo is half-built by its author's account, and nothing is simulated or
  measured. That bars a THEORY rather than only noting that none existed,
  so it was respected.
- **Jokes ([LIT-408](../../record/literature.d/LIT-408.md), [NOTE-361](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-361.md)).** The NOTE says "No THEORY in the record
  should cite it as support". It is an essay with no data and no program,
  and its unifying claim bends by its own Note 16. It was respected for
  the same reason.

So fifteen of eighteen readings became sources, which fits the owner's
hypothesis for this half of the topic. Two caveats apply. Three of the
fifteen NOTEs said "No new THEORY is indicated" or "No THEORY bears on
it" ([NOTE-355](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-355.md), [NOTE-349](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-349.md), [NOTE-331](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-331.md)). Each meant that no existing THEORY was
supported, or that nothing belonged in the anthology, not that the work
had no finding, so under the owner's ruling they did not bar a new one.
And several accounts are positions argued from thought experiments
(Turing, Searle, Dennett, Putnam, the extended mind). They are filed
because the record's other THEORYs already argue with them in prose, and
naming them lets those arguments become relations.

## Choices made

- **One THEORY for the extended mind, two sources.** Clark's 2005 reply
  restates and defends the 1998 argument and confirms in his own words
  that parity was not argued, so it went in as a second source rather than
  a THEORY of its own.
- **One THEORY for Aerts and Gabora I and II.** Part I's lattice is the
  proposal and Part II's model its realisation; the finding is about the
  pair.
- **What the Active findings claim.** Each is stated as what the published
  model or the reported statistics show, with the paper's stronger reading
  in "does not say".
- **Putnam on a skim.** It is Proposed under the owner's ruling for a
  well-established result discussed elsewhere. The record's full readings
  of Block, Chalmers and Schwitzgebel quote the same clause, and the
  THEORY says what it rests on.

  counterexample to Proposition 5), and the results that survive are proved
  in general by [LIT-788](../../record/literature.d/LIT-788.md), which is now a THEORY's source.
- **Sayed Ahmed's note ([LIT-956](../../record/literature.d/LIT-956.md), [NOTE-817](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-817.md)).** [NOTE-817](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-817.md) files no THEORY
  because what the paper asserts is either standard and better sourced
  elsewhere or stated without proof. That holds: Theorems 4.1 and 5.1–5.5
  have no proofs, and the one proved theorem (7.6) rests on the author's
  unheld preprints.

So 16 of 18 readings became sources. That fits the owner's hypothesis for
this group, with caveats. Several of the THEORYs are proved or computed
results stated with their scope (the lottery, Łoś, Shampoo, the averaging
counts), which the readings had already set out. Nine of the sixteen
NOTEs said there was no THEORY. For [NOTE-113](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-113.md), [NOTE-139](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-139.md), [NOTE-177](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-177.md), [NOTE-141](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-141.md),
[NOTE-015](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-015.md) and [NOTE-332](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-332.md) that meant no existing THEORY was supported; [NOTE-332](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-332.md)
sketched the one now filed. [NOTE-453](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-453.md) declined only a THEORY comparing IFS
with ACT, which is still not filed. [NOTE-456](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-456.md) meant that the source carries
no claim beyond its definition; its THEORY is Proposed and says so.
[NOTE-696](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-696.md) meant that the excerpts ground no claim about language; its
THEORY is about the operator only.

## Choices made

The THEORY backfill continued with the ethics and agency readings: twenty

## What entered

Seventeen THEORYs, three `Active` and fourteen `Proposed`. Codes are the

- Rule-consequentialism's reply to collapse, [THEORY-467](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-467.md) ([LIT-198](../../record/literature.d/LIT-198.md),

## What did not enter, and why

- **Browning & Veit, "The Desperate Search for Meaning in Life" ([LIT-116](../../record/literature.d/LIT-116.md),
  [NOTE-119](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-119.md)).** No THEORY. Its one thesis, that "without [otherness], the
  self cannot exist" (p. 9), is "stated, not argued", in a chapter with no
  references beyond two quotations. Its reading also finds a misdescription
  of Heidegger. A THEORY would state a claim that has no warrant in the
  work.
- **Floridi, "AI as Agency Without Intelligence" ([LIT-896](../../record/literature.d/LIT-896.md), [NOTE-697](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-697.md)).** No
  THEORY. The NOTE says an editorial "whose central claim is asserted
  cannot ground one", and that a THEORY should come from the 2025 paper.
  That THEORY now exists ([THEORY-208](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-208.md), from [LIT-897](../../record/literature.d/LIT-897.md)). It names this editorial
  in its Connections as the slogan's first statement. It does not argue

So eighteen of twenty readings became sources, sixteen as primary sources
and two as second sources ([LIT-146](../../record/literature.d/LIT-146.md), [LIT-286](../../record/literature.d/LIT-286.md)). That fits the owner's
hypothesis for this group, with two caveats. Four of the accounts are
reports of conceptual proposals whose evidence is their own coherence:
Hooker, Walsh, Floridi 2013 and Orseau et al. And Floridi 2013's NOTE had
said "no THEORY". Its reasons were the record's practice for that line,
and that the paper offers "a model and a coinage". The NOTE also named C1
and C7 as the support any later theory of moral thresholds would have. The

## Choices made

- **Status.** `Active` went to three accounts the record believes as
  stated. The first is a conceptual point the reading rates strong
  (precaution has no direction). The second is a description of
  experimental data with its limits in the title (Quillien). The third is
  an existence proof by construction (Brooks). Everything argued, assumed
  or conditional went `Proposed`. That includes Kenton et al., whose theorem
  is proved but whose definition of agency is a proposal.
- **Tags, minding [ADR-024](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-024.md).** Velleman went to `self-governance`,
  `personhood` and `self`, not `agency`, because his subject is
  identification and autonomy set against personal identity. Brooks went to
  `behavioral-integration` first. Floridi 2013 went to `ethics` and
  `society-and-governance`, not `agency`, because its "supra-agents" are
  agents by fiat and its claim is about the moral value of outcomes. The
  parasocial account took `narrative-unity`, for Lindemann's narrative,
  social-practice identity.
- **Edits to existing documents.**
  - [THEORY-207](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-207.md) gained `presupposes` (version 2).
  - [CLAIM-045](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-045.md)'s `grounds` now point at [THEORY-689](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-689.md) in place of [LIT-436](../../record/literature.d/LIT-436.md)

  - `luria link --fix` wrote the converses on [THEORY-173](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-173.md) and [QUESTION-032](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-032.md).
    It dropped [CLAIM-045](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-045.md) from [LIT-436](../../record/literature.d/LIT-436.md)'s `supports`.
- **No `answers` for [QUESTION-011](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-011.md) or [QUESTION-009](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-009.md).** Velleman's account
  constrains [QUESTION-011](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-011.md) only negatively: what makes a will-organization

## Errors found in the record

## What did not enter, and why

- **The nested HDP ([LIT-002](../../record/literature.d/LIT-002.md), [NOTE-023](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-023.md)).** A model construction and an
  inference algorithm. The only comparative finding, multiple paths
  beating a single path, rests on three corpora of at most 5,000
  abstracts, with Gibbs nCRP winning on one, one run per fold and the
  error bars undefined. At scale no nCRP baseline was run, and the flat
  baselines differ in capacity and initialisation. The printed global
  updates also contradict the derivation. Nothing could be stated as true
  that the reading supports.
- **Hierarchical Pitman–Yor topic models ([LIT-013](../../record/literature.d/LIT-013.md), [NOTE-008](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-008.md)).** A tutorial
  on an existing sampler. Its central result, the modular collapsed
  posterior, is cited from Chen et al. (2011), not proved here, and the
  TNTM results rest on one hashtag-queried corpus with undefined error
  bars. Its one clean data point (power-law discounts barely change
  perplexity) is a single ablation row.

So 23 of 25 readings became sources, which fits the owner's hypothesis
for these topics. The caveat is the same as in the first round: these
are mostly mathematical papers, whose theorems are findings by
construction. Of the eighteen, twelve rest on proofs, and the
empirical ones are scoped in their titles to the setting tested.

## Choices made

- **Declined THEORYs filed anyway.** Four NOTEs declined a THEORY, and two ([NOTE-589](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-589.md), [NOTE-591](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-591.md)) named a
  candidate without filing it. Both are now filed, [NOTE-589](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-589.md)'s
  interpretive half as a "does not say" line. For
  [LIT-577](../../record/literature.d/LIT-577.md) ("a construction plus illustrations") and [LIT-797](../../record/literature.d/LIT-797.md) ("the record
  would be stating the model's consequence") the THEORY is `Proposed`,
  with the condition in the title, and the summary says what the NOTE
  said. For [LIT-839](../../record/literature.d/LIT-839.md) (the anthology holds the metrics account) and [LIT-868](../../record/literature.d/LIT-868.md)
  (exact but narrow) the declined reason was not "no finding", so the
  proved result is filed `Active` and the summary says why. [LIT-836](../../record/literature.d/LIT-836.md)'s
  "No new THEORY" meant no existing one was changed.
- **Grouping.** The five cohomology readings became two THEORYs, split at
  the one result that changes the object (the iterated joint model).
  [THEORY-012](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md)'s "does not say" already carried this lineage in prose;
  it is now an account of its own, and [THEORY-012](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md)'s line stays. The two
  language studies share one THEORY, since each alone is a single
  unsecured or stipulated result.
- **No `rivals`.** The ICL account and the implicit-gradient account
  ([THEORY-169](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-169.md)) are at different levels and can both be true. The
  transitivity argument targets the random-variable reading, not the
  sheaf criterion of [THEORY-012](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md). The language THEORY bears on
  [THEORY-013](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-013.md) as evidence, not as an extension of its mechanism, so no
  `extends` was declared.
- **Not filed from [LIT-281](../../record/literature.d/LIT-281.md).** Chapters V–VII of the thesis (valuation
  algebras, AvN stabiliser groups, strong non-locality of three-qubit
  states) were not checked by the reading, and Chapter V is close to a
  restatement of the definitions.
- **Shannon's title.** It reports that Shannon rests entropy's
  justification on the coding theorems, rather than asserting it as the
  record's own view.

**ψ-ontology and readings of the wave function.**

- [THEORY-630](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-630.md), Proposed: protective measurement shows ψ ontic only if

  [THEORY-621](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-621.md), Proposed: Rovelli's relative facts, with no state of the

**Classical models and probabilistic theories.**

**The topos programme.**
- [THEORY-553](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-553.md), Active: quantity values are monotone spreads in a

## What did not enter, and why

- **[LIT-380](../../record/literature.d/LIT-380.md)** (Hamilton, Isham & Butterfield, KS III). It is Superseded by
  [LIT-382](../../record/literature.d/LIT-382.md), which proves the isomorphism this paper only asserts. It is
  named in [THEORY-619](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-619.md)'s Connections, not as a source.
- **[LIT-378](../../record/literature.d/LIT-378.md), [LIT-389](../../record/literature.d/LIT-389.md) and [LIT-200](../../record/literature.d/LIT-200.md)** entered as second or third sources, not
  as THEORYs of their own. [LIT-378](../../record/literature.d/LIT-378.md) is by its authors' account an amalgam of
  papers I–IV, and [NOTE-326](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-326.md) says no new THEORY is indicated. [LIT-389](../../record/literature.d/LIT-389.md) is a
  programmatic essay that proves nothing; it supports the base-category
  point. [LIT-200](../../record/literature.d/LIT-200.md) is a variant of the weak nomological reading.

So 21 of 22 readings became sources, and 18 of them primary sources. That
fits the owner's hypothesis strongly here. One caveat: several NOTEs said
"supports no THEORY document" ([NOTE-110](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-110.md), [NOTE-154](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-154.md), [NOTE-175](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-175.md)) or "the record
has no THEORY documents yet" ([NOTE-018](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-018.md), [NOTE-021](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-021.md), [NOTE-030](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-030.md), [NOTE-066](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-066.md),
[NOTE-080](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-080.md)). Those meant no existing THEORY. Most of the same NOTEs proposed a
THEORY in so many words, and five of the twenty follow those proposals
closely (from [NOTE-018](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-018.md), [NOTE-021](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-021.md), [NOTE-030](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-030.md), [NOTE-066](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-066.md) and [NOTE-080](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-080.md)).

## Choices made

- **Status.** A proved result, or a construction checked by the reading,
  went `Active` with its conditions in the title: PBR, steering, the
  fidelity and no-broadcasting theorems, the toy bit calculus, the
  interference model, the stochastic dictionary, the topos results. An
  interpretive account, or a result the paper asserts without proof, went
  `Proposed`: RQM, protective measurement, the nomological readings,
  Dorato, the open-systems ranking, Hance et al., the work notions and the
  composite failure.
- **Active from a review.** [THEORY-482](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-482.md) rests on a review that
  reproduces the derivation in full; the result is standard, as the owner's
  first-round ruling allows. [LIT-010](../../record/literature.d/LIT-010.md) itself advises citing the primary
  papers, which the record does not hold.
- **Relations.** `rivals` between Gao and Rovelli, who cannot both be right
  about ψ. `presupposes` from Hance et al. to PBR, from the composite result
  to the quantity-value result, and from [THEORY-037](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-037.md) to [THEORY-619](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-619.md).
  `extends` from the quantum Jarzynski equality to the classical fluctuation
  theorem. `corrects` from the sieve-semantics account to [THEORY-024](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-024.md), which
  was already Rejected and had no winner named.
- **`answers`.** Only [QUESTION-055](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-055.md), by [THEORY-516](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-516.md): a presheaf over
  contexts gets the Heyting pseudo-complement its base fixes. The
  interference model bears on [CLAIM-041](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-041.md)'s point that context effects do
  not establish nonclassicality, but [CLAIM-041](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-041.md) does not rely on it, so its
  `grounds` were left alone.

## Errors found in the record

- [NOTE-334](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-334.md)'s correction already records that [LIT-389](../../record/literature.d/LIT-389.md)'s remark on the (ℝ, ≤)
  presheaf is wrong; [THEORY-516](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-516.md) repeats it so the essay is not cited
  for it.
- The key takeaway in [LIT-081](../../record/literature.d/LIT-081.md)'s body still reads that Koecher–Vinberg plus
  Hanche-Olsen "force" C*-algebraic quantum theory. The summary is already
  corrected; the takeaway states it conditionally on strong self-duality,
  so it was left.
- No other errors were found beyond those the NOTEs already record.

## Cognition, part 2: twelve THEORYs from seventeen readings

*2026-10-16 18:16:53 · curation · record*

The second half of the cognition group in the THEORY backfill. Seventeen
LITs, each with a `Read` NOTE and no THEORY citing it as `source`. Codes
below are the temporary ones `luria new` assigned.

## What entered

Twelve THEORYs, three `Active` and nine `Proposed`. Fifteen of the
seventeen readings are now a THEORY's source.

- **The extended-mind dispute, as three rival accounts and one shared
  point.**
  - Chalmers's sensorimotor statement of the thesis, with consciousness
    held out by directness ([THEORY-512](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-512.md), Proposed; [LIT-415](../../record/literature.d/LIT-415.md), [LIT-421](../../record/literature.d/LIT-421.md)).
  - Adams and Aizawa's marks of the cognitive and contingent
    intracranialism ([THEORY-591](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-591.md), Proposed; [LIT-438](../../record/literature.d/LIT-438.md), [LIT-455](../../record/literature.d/LIT-455.md)).
  - Rupert's embedded cognition, argued from memory research
    ([THEORY-528](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-528.md), Proposed; [LIT-422](../../record/literature.d/LIT-422.md)).
  - The point all three accept, that coupling does not by itself make
    parthood ([THEORY-582](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-582.md), Active; [LIT-438](../../record/literature.d/LIT-438.md), [LIT-455](../../record/literature.d/LIT-455.md)). The first is a
    rival of the other two; the marks account presupposes the coupling
    point.
- **Philosophy of mind.** Belief ascription presupposes rationality, and
  the believer is an idealisation ([THEORY-596](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-596.md), Proposed; [LIT-440](../../record/literature.d/LIT-440.md),
  [LIT-456](../../record/literature.d/LIT-456.md)). Psychological states are not machine-table states
  ([THEORY-471](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-471.md), Active; [LIT-641](../../record/literature.d/LIT-641.md)).
- **AI and cognitive modelling.** Hand-built representations hide
  high-level perception, and no representation module can serve every
  task ([THEORY-541](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-541.md), Proposed; [LIT-414](../../record/literature.d/LIT-414.md), with Burns's review [LIT-457](../../record/literature.d/LIT-457.md)
  turning the charge on Copycat). Minsky's emotions as ways to think, a
  rival of [THEORY-045](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-045.md) on what feelings are ([THEORY-570](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-570.md), Proposed;
  [LIT-432](../../record/literature.d/LIT-432.md)). Monotonic logic and displaceable defaults
  ([THEORY-462](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-462.md), Proposed; [LIT-410](../../record/literature.d/LIT-410.md)).
- **Perception.** Block's border between seeing and thinking, from the
  précis only ([THEORY-454](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-454.md), Proposed; [LIT-649](../../record/literature.d/LIT-649.md)).
- **Language learning.** Joint inference of referential intentions and
  lexicon ([THEORY-542](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-542.md), Proposed; [LIT-815](../../record/literature.d/LIT-815.md)). Human function-learning
  chains converge on the favoured function, not shown to be the prior
  ([THEORY-489](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-489.md), Active; [LIT-820](../../record/literature.d/LIT-820.md)).

## What did not enter, and why

- **Pandemonium ([LIT-427](../../record/literature.d/LIT-427.md), [NOTE-360](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-360.md)).** A proposal written before the runs
  it promises. Its results are three sentences in the discussion, one of
  which reports that subdemon selection "did not do what we hoped". Its
  design argument for modularity is an assertion. It stays named in
  [THEORY-043](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md) as the decomposition's starting point.
- **Singh's exposition ([LIT-444](../../record/literature.d/LIT-444.md), [NOTE-339](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-339.md)).** Uncritical by design, with
  no implementation and no argument for the theory. Its one firm claim,
  that the Society of Mind has not been implemented, is historical and is
  better carried by the reading than by a THEORY.

So fifteen of seventeen readings became sources, which fits the owner's
hypothesis. Two caveats. Three of the twelve rest on works the readings
call proposals ([LIT-410](../../record/literature.d/LIT-410.md), [LIT-432](../../record/literature.d/LIT-432.md)) or a précis ([LIT-649](../../record/literature.d/LIT-649.md)), and each says so
and stays `Proposed`. And the two that entered nothing are the group's two
works with no claim of their own to test.

## Choices made

- **The coupling point is filed apart from the marks.** Adams and Aizawa's
  readings rate the logical point strong and the two marks assumed. One
  document would have had to be `Proposed` for the marks while the record
  believes the point. [CLAIM-172](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-172.md) and [CLAIM-173](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-173.md) now ground on the coupling
  THEORY instead of the bare [LIT-455](../../record/literature.d/LIT-455.md).
- **Two notes said no THEORY.** [NOTE-337](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-337.md) (frames) says the memo is "a
  source of hypotheses, not of support". [THEORY-462](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-462.md) takes only the
  half its reading calls correct, monotonicity, and marks the no-repair
  claim as the memo's assertion. [NOTE-611](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-611.md) (word learning) said no THEORY
  because the findings are specific to a small corpus and the record held
  nothing they correct. The second reason concerns existing THEORYs, so the
  account is filed `Proposed` with its scale in the title.
- **Active.** The coupling point, the case against machine-table states,
  and the human iterated-learning finding, each with its scope in the title.
  The machine-table account is a philosophical argument the reading rates
  strong against its stated target, and it leaves functionalism standing.
- **No `answers` edges.** [QUESTION-035](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-035.md) (when a combined form is one system)
  is where the coupling point bears, but [CLAIM-172](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-172.md) deliberately sidesteps
  parthood, so the THEORY constrains a route the record does not take.
  [QUESTION-046](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-046.md) (a criterion for group experience) is where Chalmers's
  directness criterion bears, and [THEORY-043](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md) already carries that
  application as the record's own.
- **Overlap with part 1.** Part 1 holds [LIT-097](../../record/literature.d/LIT-097.md) (the extended mind),
  [LIT-398](../../record/literature.d/LIT-398.md) (True Believers) and [LIT-402](../../record/literature.d/LIT-402.md) (K-lines). The accounts here were
  written not to state those works' theses. If part 1 files the 1998
  parity thesis, it is the account [THEORY-512](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-512.md) revises, and the three
  rivals edges here should be extended to it.

## Existing documents edited

## Consciousness, in the THEORY backfill: thirteen accounts from eighteen readings

*2026-10-16 18:17:40 · curation · record*

The THEORY backfill reached the consciousness readings: eighteen LITs with
a `Read` NOTE that no THEORY cited as `source`. Each NOTE was read in full
with its LIT, and existing THEORYs were checked for the same account
before anything was filed. Codes are the temporary ones `luria new`
assigned.

## What entered

Thirteen THEORYs, two `Active` and eleven `Proposed`.

- **Two findings, `Active`.**
  - [THEORY-597](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-597.md), from Lindahl et al. ([LIT-066](../../record/literature.d/LIT-066.md)): challenging
    meditation-related experiences span 59 categories in seven domains and
    occur in daily practice, at low dose and in the first days, not only
    on retreat. Filed as a description of a sample chosen for difficulty,
    with self-attributed causation.
  - [THEORY-498](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-498.md), from Kleiner & Ludwig ([LIT-143](../../record/literature.d/LIT-143.md)): satisfying a
    structure's axioms on experiential aspects does not make it a
    structure of experience. The negative half is proved by construction,
    which is why it is `Active`; the two positive cases are carried with
    their assumed premises.
- **The hard problem and its rival.** [THEORY-694](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-694.md) (Chalmers 1995,
  [LIT-406](../../record/literature.d/LIT-406.md), with Nagel, [LIT-096](../../record/literature.d/LIT-096.md)) and illusionism, [THEORY-633](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-633.md) (Frankish
  2016, [LIT-458](../../record/literature.d/LIT-458.md), with Dennett's "Facing Backwards", [LIT-397](../../record/literature.d/LIT-397.md), and Frankish
  2025, [LIT-103](../../record/literature.d/LIT-103.md)), filed as `rivals`.
- **Chalmers's other papers.** Organisational invariance ([THEORY-507](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-507.md),
  [LIT-392](../../record/literature.d/LIT-392.md) with [LIT-406](../../record/literature.d/LIT-406.md)), the combination problem ([THEORY-644](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-644.md), [LIT-395](../../record/literature.d/LIT-395.md)),
  the meta-problem challenge ([THEORY-577](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-577.md), [LIT-425](../../record/literature.d/LIT-425.md)) and the
  temporary-objections argument about language models ([THEORY-460](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-460.md),
  [LIT-411](../../record/literature.d/LIT-411.md)).
- **Dennett and his readers.** "Quining Qualia" ([THEORY-415](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-415.md), [LIT-433](../../record/literature.d/LIT-433.md))
  and Taylor's real-pattern reading ([THEORY-563](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-563.md), [LIT-461](../../record/literature.d/LIT-461.md)).
- **The rest.** IIT's ill-definedness and the proxy point ([THEORY-523](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-523.md),
  [LIT-185](../../record/literature.d/LIT-185.md)); Shanahan's candidature by encounter ([THEORY-606](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-606.md), [LIT-465](../../record/literature.d/LIT-465.md));
  pooled processing feelings as a contributor to cross-modal unity
  ([THEORY-573](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-573.md), [LIT-190](../../record/literature.d/LIT-190.md), itself a `Proposed` LIT).
- **`answers`.** Invariance answers [QUESTION-046](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-046.md) in part: it is a constraint
  on any criterion (a population isomorph is a subject), not a criterion.
  The meta-problem challenge answers [QUESTION-048](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-048.md) in part: a basis that
  does not explain the reports cannot be confirmed by them, and puzzled
  reports can be mimicked.

## What did not enter, and why

- **Schwitzgebel's reply to Kammerer ([LIT-459](../../record/literature.d/LIT-459.md), [NOTE-381](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-381.md)).** No new THEORY.
  [THEORY-043](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md) already states and argues from its three points (the
  condition-A gap, the Leo case, the simplicity dilemma) in its Kammerer
  and invariance bullets and in `promote_when`. The reply was added to
  that account's `source` instead.
- **Mashour & Alkire ([LIT-965](../../record/literature.d/LIT-965.md), [NOTE-797](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-797.md)).** No THEORY, as the NOTE decided.
  It is a perspective with no data; its one finding is second-hand from a
  study the record does not hold; its marker of returning consciousness
  is an access marker, which the authors concede. What it bears on is held
  by [THEORY-091](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-091.md), [THEORY-090](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-090.md), [THEORY-023](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-023.md) and [THEORY-100](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-100.md).

So seventeen of eighteen readings became sources, sixteen of them of new
accounts. That fits the owner's hypothesis for this topic, with three
caveats. Most of these readings are philosophical arguments, so most
accounts are `Proposed` and say what kind of result would move them;
several of those results do not yet exist anywhere. Two NOTEs said "No new
THEORY" ([NOTE-346](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-346.md), [NOTE-357](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-357.md)) because the record lacks the replies, not
because the works lack a claim; under the owner's ruling those were filed
`Proposed`, and [THEORY-415](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-415.md) says what its NOTE said. [NOTE-089](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-089.md) said Nagel
supports no theory "in the anthology's sense"; Nagel entered as the second
source of the hard-problem account rather than as an account of his own,
since a separate Nagel THEORY would have restated the same gap.

## Choices made

- **Rivals.** Only the hard problem and illusionism are declared rivals:
  they disagree about whether the further question has an answer to find.
  Shanahan's account denies [THEORY-023](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-023.md)'s presupposition rather than giving
  another answer to it, so it is named in Connections, not as a rival.
  Invariance and IIT cannot both be true for isomorphs, but the record has
  no THEORY stating IIT's exclusion as an account, so that conflict is
  stated in prose.
- **Frankish's commentary ([LIT-103](../../record/literature.d/LIT-103.md))** entered as a source of the illusionism
  account, for the bureau-de-change application, rather than as a THEORY
  of its own. Its charge against Veit is conditional, and [THEORY-101](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-101.md)
  already records Veit's concession.
- **Edits to existing documents.** [LIT-185](../../record/literature.d/LIT-185.md) v3, above. [THEORY-043](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md) v6 gains [LIT-459](../../record/literature.d/LIT-459.md) in its
  `source` and a Connections line naming the new accounts. [THEORY-023](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-023.md) v4
  gains [LIT-411](../../record/literature.d/LIT-411.md) in its `source`, as [NOTE-345](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-345.md) recommended, with a short section
  on what it adds and Connections lines for Shanahan and the meta-problem.
  Both claims are unchanged.

## Complex systems: thirteen THEORYs from fourteen of seventeen readings

*2026-10-16 18:21:38 · curation · record*

The THEORY backfill's complex-systems group: seventeen LITs with a `Read`
or `Skimmed` NOTE that no THEORY cited as `source`. Each NOTE was read in
full against its LIT, and the theory directory was searched for an
existing account first. Fourteen of the seventeen readings became sources
of a THEORY, and three did not. That fits the owner's hypothesis for this
group, with the caveat that two of the fourteen ([LIT-046](../../record/literature.d/LIT-046.md), [LIT-141](../../record/literature.d/LIT-141.md)) enter
as Proposed accounts their NOTEs had declined to file, under the ruling
that a NOTE's "no THEORY" for a survey or framework yields to a claim its
own reading supports.

## What entered

Thirteen THEORYs, seven `Active` and six `Proposed`. Codes are the
temporary ones `luria new` assigned.

- **Emergence and individuality.**
  - [THEORY-424](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-424.md) (Active; [LIT-005](../../record/literature.d/LIT-005.md)). Observational mutual-information
    individuality measures track association, not propagation; [NOTE-027](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-027.md)'s
    XOR system has Krakauer's conditional A at 1 bit where Bourrat's
    interventional Â is 0. It `answers` [QUESTION-115](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-115.md) in the constraining
    sense: temporal retention is not causal persistence.
  - [THEORY-607](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-607.md) (Proposed; [LIT-049](../../record/literature.d/LIT-049.md)). Bourrat's coarse-graining account:
    individuals in a transition are a summary description, quasi-ontological
    only by indispensability under finite resources. Filed with its
    degenerate criterion in "does not say", and `rivals` [THEORY-141](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-141.md)
    (Okasha: the level of selection changes in fact).
  - [THEORY-497](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-497.md) (Proposed; [LIT-025](../../record/literature.d/LIT-025.md)). The ΦID account: a supervenient
    feature can carry irreducible predictive information, and a system
    hosts one iff its dynamics carry synergy about their own future. The
    record holds the theorem only second-hand.
  - [THEORY-581](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-581.md) (Active; [LIT-027](../../record/literature.d/LIT-027.md)). Synergy bias can differ between two
    exactly consistent descriptions with equal mutual information; small,
    one redundancy function, and reversed for deterministic systems.
  - [THEORY-657](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-657.md) (Proposed; [LIT-141](../../record/literature.d/LIT-141.md)). With novelty as the definition,
    the other marks of emergence are separate questions: Kondo, liquid–gas,
    BKT and Butterfield's reductions as counterexamples.
- **Collectives.**
  - [THEORY-696](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-696.md) (Active; [LIT-035](../../record/literature.d/LIT-035.md)). Pooling under multiplicative noise
    raises each member's time-average growth from μ − σ²/2 to
    μ − σ²/(2N); a sufficient mechanism, not a solution of the cooperation
    puzzle.
  - [THEORY-608](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-608.md) (Active; [LIT-075](../../record/literature.d/LIT-075.md)). Ant groups improve with size on a
    piano-movers puzzle; human groups barred from speech do 32% worse than
    individuals. No inferential statistics; mechanisms untested.
  - [THEORY-402](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-402.md) (Proposed; [LIT-046](../../record/literature.d/LIT-046.md), [LIT-075](../../record/literature.d/LIT-075.md)). Collective intelligence
    as resources against coordination costs. [NOTE-055](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-055.md) judged the paper a
    vocabulary; it is filed with that verdict and a promote_when that asks
    for the resources to be measured.
- **Dynamics and pattern.**
  - [THEORY-634](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-634.md) (Active; [LIT-036](../../record/literature.d/LIT-036.md)). Cyclic non-reciprocal coupling gives
    a circulant spectrum and a parity dichotomy; the origin-of-life reading
    is in "does not say".
  - [THEORY-548](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-548.md) (Proposed; [LIT-057](../../record/literature.d/LIT-057.md)). Delay destabilises a random
    Lotka–Volterra community by a Hopf bifurcation; the diversity–stability
    sign depends on the measure, and the averaging null is untested.
  - [THEORY-692](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-692.md) (Active; [LIT-516](../../record/literature.d/LIT-516.md), [LIT-527](../../record/literature.d/LIT-527.md)). Minimum entropy production
    only in the strictly linear regime; far from equilibrium a sufficient
    stability condition and no selection principle. [LIT-527](../../record/literature.d/LIT-527.md) is a skim and
    is acknowledged as one.
  - [THEORY-543](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-543.md) (Active; [LIT-535](../../record/literature.d/LIT-535.md), [LIT-527](../../record/literature.d/LIT-527.md)). Turing's diffusive
    instability, with the unequal-diffusion corollary marked as [NOTE-427](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-427.md)'s
    derivation.
  - [THEORY-661](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-661.md) (Active; [LIT-905](../../record/literature.d/LIT-905.md)). Simon's near-decomposability: fast
    and independent inside blocks, slow and aggregate between them. The
    theorem is Simon & Ando's, cited and not held.

## What did not enter, and why

- **[LIT-021](../../record/literature.d/LIT-021.md) (Artime et al., [NOTE-007](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-007.md)).** An editorial with no result. Its
  one formal item sorts emergence by whether a pattern is "expected", which
  is never defined, and its status note says not to cite it for a
  definition.
- **[LIT-150](../../record/literature.d/LIT-150.md) (Rizi, [NOTE-153](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-153.md)).** A position statement. Its coarse-graining
  criterion has no distortion or predictive measure, so it cannot decide a
  case, and its LLM sentence is unsupported. [NOTE-153](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-153.md) says no THEORY
  follows; this audit agrees, and names it in [THEORY-657](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-657.md).
- **[LIT-933](../../record/literature.d/LIT-933.md) (Nowak et al., [NOTE-768](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-768.md)).** A programmatic heuristic with no
  model or prediction that could fail. Its one sharp contribution, a broad
  definition of synchronisation, is a definition. [NOTE-768](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-768.md) files no THEORY,
  and its bearing is already registered on [QUESTION-053](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-053.md) and [QUESTION-063](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-063.md).

## Choices made

- **Status.** A derivation within a stated model, a theorem the field
  holds, or a finding described with its scope went `Active`. An account
  the reading calls argued, a framework, a survey's conclusion, or a
  preprint result at one parameter setting went `Proposed`.
- **One rivalry.** Bourrat's descriptive account against Okasha's factual
  change of the level of selection ([THEORY-141](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-141.md)). The ΦID and
  effective-information accounts were not made rivals: their disagreement
  on [NOTE-010](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-010.md)'s two-bit permutation depends on the redundancy function.
  The dissipative-structure account was not made a rival of maximum
  entropy production ([THEORY-671](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-671.md)), since it says no selection
  principle is established, not that none holds.
- **Edits to existing documents.** [THEORY-222](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-222.md) (v2): its Connections said
  the record held no ΦID THEORY; it now names [THEORY-497](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-497.md). [CLAIM-157](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-157.md)
  (v4) and [CLAIM-331](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md) (v2): `grounds` gains [THEORY-661](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-661.md), the
  near-decomposability result both cite Simon for. `luria link --fix`
  wrote the converses on [THEORY-141](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-141.md) and [QUESTION-115](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-115.md).

## Errors found in the record

- [THEORY-222](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-222.md)'s "the record holds no THEORY stating the ΦID account" was
  true when filed and is now corrected.
- [QUESTION-115](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-115.md) and [CLAIM-331](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md) cite Proposed documents ([CLAIM-157](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-157.md),
  [CLAIM-327](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-327.md), [LIT-005](../../record/literature.d/LIT-005.md), [THEORY-222](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-222.md), [THEORY-257](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-257.md)) without an `inactive-ok`
  acknowledgement. These warnings predate this batch and were left.

## Representation learning, learning theory and loss landscapes: 20 THEORYs from 26 readings

*2026-10-16 18:23:53 · curation · record*

Part of the THEORY backfill of 2026-10-16. This group held 26 LITs with a
`Read` or `Skimmed` NOTE that no THEORY cited as `source`: eleven under
`representation-learning`, eight under `learning-theory` and seven under
`loss-landscapes`. Each NOTE and LIT was read in full; no paper was
fetched. Codes are the temporary ones `luria new` assigned.

## What entered

Twenty THEORYs, eleven `Active` and nine `Proposed`, drawing on 23 of
the 26 readings.

**Active (findings with their scope, or proved results).**

- [THEORY-698](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-698.md), from [LIT-267](../../record/literature.d/LIT-267.md): thresholded linear probes give a
  complete concept lattice for any incidence, so the Lattice
  Representation Hypothesis measured per-attribute agreement with GPT-4o
  annotations and no lattice law.
- [THEORY-640](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-640.md), from [LIT-302](../../record/literature.d/LIT-302.md): the Platonic hypothesis's measured
  convergence is local mutual-nearest-neighbour agreement, 0.16 of 1
  cross-modally, maximised over layer pairs, adopted after CKA showed a
  very weak trend.
- [THEORY-445](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-445.md), from [LIT-314](../../record/literature.d/LIT-314.md): group-equivariant networks are
  equivariant by construction through the regular representation, the
  group fixed in advance.
- [THEORY-504](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-504.md), from [LIT-611](../../record/literature.d/LIT-611.md): Gemma Scope's two fidelity measures
  disagree by site and in base-to-chat transfer.
- [THEORY-496](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-496.md), from [LIT-814](../../record/literature.d/LIT-814.md): label correctness contributes little to
  in-context gains; input distribution, label space and format carry them.
- [THEORY-683](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-683.md), from [LIT-833](../../record/literature.d/LIT-833.md): order of fixed few-shot examples moves
  accuracy from near chance to near the state of the art, idiosyncratically
  by model.
- [THEORY-420](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-420.md), from [LIT-856](../../record/literature.d/LIT-856.md): the smallest singular-value decile is
  never the cheapest to lose in rectangular transformer matrices, though
  it is in square ones.
- [THEORY-574](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-574.md), from [LIT-376](../../record/literature.d/LIT-376.md), [LIT-375](../../record/literature.d/LIT-375.md) and [LIT-374](../../record/literature.d/LIT-374.md): Li's structural width
  is a covering number under a locality constraint, metric not
  topological, and entails neither routing nor decoupled training.
- [THEORY-439](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-439.md), from [LIT-796](../../record/literature.d/LIT-796.md): the same demonstrations used as context
  and as a discarded weight update are not interchangeable.
- [THEORY-425](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-425.md), from [LIT-668](../../record/literature.d/LIT-668.md): a clean-trained connecting path keeps only
  what the clean data ask for, and can carry an adversarial-loss barrier.
- [THEORY-509](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-509.md), from [LIT-670](../../record/literature.d/LIT-670.md): generically, expert permutation and a
  common gate translation are all of an MoE gate's symmetry.

**Proposed (argued, thin, second-hand, or resting on an inference).**

- [THEORY-478](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-478.md), from [LIT-870](../../record/literature.d/LIT-870.md): hyperbolic diffusion distance is a
  thresholded snowflake of a latent tree metric, under cited and partly
  gapped heat-kernel bounds.
- [THEORY-421](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-421.md), from [LIT-871](../../record/literature.d/LIT-871.md): distance from the origin is only a partial

- [THEORY-566](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-566.md), from [LIT-879](../../record/literature.d/LIT-879.md): in Ganea et al.'s networks the curvature

- [THEORY-510](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-510.md), from [LIT-234](../../record/literature.d/LIT-234.md): class-dependent label preservation and
  per-class losses under a rising mean, with the count of losing classes
  not established.
- [THEORY-521](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-521.md), from [LIT-672](../../record/literature.d/LIT-672.md): discontinuous learning curves when the
  entropy of near-optimal hypotheses vanishes, held second-hand.
- [THEORY-481](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-481.md), from [LIT-859](../../record/literature.d/LIT-859.md): staged, spectrum-ordered learning of a
  linear-attention layer; `extends` [THEORY-186](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md).
- [THEORY-557](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-557.md), from [LIT-676](../../record/literature.d/LIT-676.md) and [LIT-660](../../record/literature.d/LIT-660.md): low-loss paths outside image
  classifiers; `extends` [THEORY-109](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-109.md).
- [THEORY-675](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-675.md), from [LIT-676](../../record/literature.d/LIT-676.md) and [LIT-666](../../record/literature.d/LIT-666.md): without a shared stable start
  the linear barrier depends on the data's structure.
- [THEORY-578](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-578.md), from [LIT-662](../../record/literature.d/LIT-662.md): a distribution-space geodesic can be a

`answers` edges: [QUESTION-025](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-025.md) (tmpzhrlj, tmpa223w), [QUESTION-039](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-039.md) (tmpf9wko,
tmpaeic7), [QUESTION-058](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-058.md) (tmp5lcx6), [QUESTION-069](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-069.md) (tmpjgtxb, tmpxxllh,
tmpltw3b, tmpe5k4b). Each constrains or partly answers its question, as
its Connections section says.

## What did not enter, and why

- **[LIT-978](../../record/literature.d/LIT-978.md) (Kothapalli's review of neural collapse, [NOTE-772](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-772.md), Skimmed).**
  A survey: every result in it is another paper's, unchecked here, and
  the LIT says no THEORY rests on it. [THEORY-083](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md) already carries the
  point the review would add, that collapse is derived only in models
  that remove the data.
- **[LIT-954](../../record/literature.d/LIT-954.md) (Gokhale's semantic landscape, [NOTE-807](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-807.md)).** A vocabulary, with
  no experiment and no proof. Its one derivation shows only that chosen
  assumptions can yield the observed exponents.
- **[LIT-677](../../record/literature.d/LIT-677.md) (Zhang & Blei on the ELBO landscape, [NOTE-522](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-522.md)).** The workshop
  paper reports none of the results it describes. It is named in
  [THEORY-557](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-557.md)'s "does not say" as a claim without evidence.

So 23 of 26 readings became sources, which fits the owner's hypothesis for
this group. Two caveats. Fifteen of the 23 NOTEs had declined or held back a THEORY,
for reasons that were judgements rather than "no finding": a measurement
"better cited from the LIT" ([LIT-833](../../record/literature.d/LIT-833.md)), an aggregate with exceptions
([LIT-814](../../record/literature.d/LIT-814.md)), evidence in one figure ([LIT-662](../../record/literature.d/LIT-662.md)), a result "about training
transformers" ([LIT-859](../../record/literature.d/LIT-859.md)), material the anthology already reads ([LIT-856](../../record/literature.d/LIT-856.md)).
Following the owner's ruling, those were filed, with the NOTE's reason
stated in the THEORY where it bears on status. And the three that entered
nothing are a survey, a vocabulary and a paper without results.

## Choices made

- **Status.** Active for a finding the record believes as scoped in its
  title, or a proved result: the G-CNN and MoE symmetry results, the
  lattice theorem's triviality, the Li programme's width, which the NOTEs
  derive from the papers' own remarks. Proposed where the NOTE rates the
  evidence weak, where the result is reported second-hand ([LIT-672](../../record/literature.d/LIT-672.md)'s
  perceptron), or where the interesting part is this record's inference
  ([LIT-879](../../record/literature.d/LIT-879.md)).
- **Boundary.** Several of these works carry practice (Gemma Scope's
  engineering, test-time training, order selection, path repair, per-class
  tuning). Each THEORY states the finding only and names the practice as
  the anthology's. THEORYs on ML-system behaviour carry
  `anthology-candidate` last, as their LITs do.
- **One account from three papers.** Li's three papers were read jointly as
  one programme, so they source one THEORY, [LIT-376](../../record/literature.d/LIT-376.md) first as the paper whose
  proofs are cleanest.
- **[LIT-676](../../record/literature.d/LIT-676.md) sources two accounts**, the curved-path connectivity and the
  data-dependence of the linear barrier, which are different claims.

neuroscience or philosophy-of-biology, each with a `Read` or `Skimmed`
NOTE and no THEORY citing it as `source`. Each NOTE was read in full; no

## What entered

Twenty-two THEORYs from twenty-four of the twenty-five readings: eleven
`Active`, eleven `Proposed`. Codes are the temporary ones `luria new`
assigned.

**Social science.**
- [THEORY-674](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-674.md) (Proposed, [LIT-079](../../record/literature.d/LIT-079.md)): the share of design-identified

- [THEORY-429](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-429.md) (Proposed, [LIT-489](../../record/literature.d/LIT-489.md)): North's account of institutions,

- [THEORY-456](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-456.md) (Active, [LIT-004](../../record/literature.d/LIT-004.md)): Ollivier–Ricci flow separates
  communities, with the theorem's narrow scope and the SBM failure.
