  candidate.

**Compositionality.**
- [THEORY-405](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-405.md) (Active, [LIT-770](../../record/literature.d/LIT-770.md)): Composable Diffusion composes
  positions but not relations, and its product-of-experts reading holds
  only under stated conditions.
- [THEORY-522](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-522.md) (Active, [LIT-782](../../record/literature.d/LIT-782.md), [LIT-783](../../record/literature.d/LIT-783.md), [LIT-798](../../record/literature.d/LIT-798.md)): 2022–23 text-to-image
  models fail most on position, then on binding, on two independent
  benchmarks.
- [THEORY-678](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-678.md) (Proposed, [LIT-806](../../record/literature.d/LIT-806.md), [LIT-798](../../record/literature.d/LIT-798.md)): Attend-and-Excite's account
  of why subjects go missing.

**Neuroscience.**
- [THEORY-682](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-682.md) (Proposed, [LIT-034](../../record/literature.d/LIT-034.md)): a single threshold stage cannot read
  frequency, two can, and a delayed motor loop read this way can hold an
  axon's length.
- [THEORY-571](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-571.md) (Proposed, [LIT-080](../../record/literature.d/LIT-080.md)): brain states as dwell among
  metastable substates; depression and psychedelics at opposite ends.
  `answers: QUESTION-079`.
- [THEORY-697](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-697.md) (Active, [LIT-269](../../record/literature.d/LIT-269.md)): SDM's read approximates softmax
  attention over a local window, with a regression-fitted temperature.
- [THEORY-618](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-618.md) (Proposed, [LIT-875](../../record/literature.d/LIT-875.md), [LIT-872](../../record/literature.d/LIT-872.md), [LIT-876](../../record/literature.d/LIT-876.md)): the general
  hyperbolic-geometry hypothesis. It `extends` [THEORY-191](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-191.md) and [THEORY-192](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-192.md).

**Philosophy of biology.**
- [THEORY-628](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-628.md) (Proposed, [LIT-1017](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1017.md)): Di Paolo's adaptivity.
  `answers: QUESTION-087`.
- [THEORY-666](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-666.md) (Proposed, [LIT-1018](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1018.md)): Weber and Varela's intrinsic
  teleology. The two are declared `rivals`.
- [THEORY-514](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-514.md) (Proposed, [LIT-167](../../record/literature.d/LIT-167.md)): Baedke's argument that persistence
  does not single out organisms, with the overcomer proposal.

## What did not enter, and why

- **What Lives? ([LIT-211](../../record/literature.d/LIT-211.md), [NOTE-109](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-109.md)).** Its reading calls it a dataset: 68
  hand-picked definitions of life. Its computed "landscape" is one run of
  an unvalidated LLM pipeline, with silhouette 0.079 at the chosen k. The
  one sound count, that 17 of 68 definitions invoke autonomy or agency,
  describes a curated, unrepresentative sample and comes from a single
  coder. No account of life or of expert opinion can rest on it. It is
  named in the Baedke THEORY's Connections, and it was already named in
  [THEORY-072](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md)'s.

So 24 of 25 readings became sources, which fits the owner's hypothesis
for this group. Three caveats:
- Several of the eleven `Active` THEORYs are findings of narrow scope: a
  dataset, a benchmark, a proved special case.
- Two readings, [LIT-091](../../record/literature.d/LIT-091.md) and [LIT-028](../../record/literature.d/LIT-028.md), had already named their THEORY.
- Two notes said "no THEORY" for reasons this batch did not follow, given
  below.

## Choices made

- **Notes that said no THEORY.** [NOTE-670](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-670.md) ([LIT-875](../../record/literature.d/LIT-875.md)) said its claims are
  conjectures. The conjecture was filed as `Proposed` because the record
  holds two tests of it ([THEORY-191](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-191.md), [THEORY-192](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-192.md)) and no general statement,
  and the THEORY says the Zipf argument fails. [NOTE-639](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-639.md) ([LIT-806](../../record/literature.d/LIT-806.md)) declined
  because the method is machine-learning practice. The account of why
  subjects go missing is a finding about the model, so it was filed as
  `Proposed`, and the THEORY says what the NOTE said.
- **Respected, not filed.** [NOTE-593](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-593.md), [NOTE-592](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-592.md) and [NOTE-610](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-610.md) each name a
  candidate: holistic image–text embedding similarity does not track human
  judgement of composition, where decomposed checks do. They left it
  unfiled because it is a claim about how to evaluate generators, which an
  anthology topic holds. It is named in [THEORY-522](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-522.md)'s "does not say"
  and not filed. [NOTE-597](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-597.md)'s noise-level bias candidate was left unfiled
  for its own reason: no source states and tests it.
- **Relations.**
  - `rivals`: Di Paolo against Weber and Varela.
  - Not declared, with reasons in the bodies: the discrete-substate view
    against [THEORY-088](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-088.md), because [THEORY-088](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-088.md) leaves continuity open; North
    against rules in equilibrium ([THEORY-414](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-414.md)), because the two answer
    different questions; Baedke against [THEORY-072](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md), which says itself
    that it answers a different question.
  - `extends`: the hyperbolic hypothesis on its two instances.
- **`answers`.** Two were added: [QUESTION-079](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-079.md), for the discrete side of
  the question, and [QUESTION-087](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-087.md), for organisms only. Three were
  considered and not added. [QUESTION-025](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-025.md): [NOTE-670](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-670.md) finds nothing toward
  it. [QUESTION-035](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-035.md): Baedke answers which system is the organism, a
  different question. [QUESTION-096](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-096.md): the SDM account names the mechanism
  but does not say how to tell an addressing effect apart.
- **Grounds.** Five claims had grounds pointed at the THEORY that states
  the reading they rely on:
  - [CLAIM-317](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-317.md) to the boyd THEORY;
  - [CLAIM-321](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-321.md) to the three compositionality THEORYs;
  - [CLAIM-123](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-123.md) to Composable Diffusion;
  - [CLAIM-298](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-298.md) to the SDM account;
  - [CLAIM-288](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-288.md) to Di Paolo.

  [CLAIM-180](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-180.md) was left alone, because it relies on the critical distance,
  which comes from Kanerva's book, not from [LIT-269](../../record/literature.d/LIT-269.md).
- **[THEORY-088](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-088.md)** gained a paragraph saying the discrete-substate view it
  set aside is now filed.

## Errors found in the record

- **[NOTE-719](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-719.md) and [NOTE-720](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-720.md)** each called the other paper unread. Both were
  read on 2026-10-13. Both lines are corrected, with version bumps.

unchecked, and [LIT-048](../../record/literature.d/LIT-048.md) did not carry `causality`.

## The record's own argument

- [TERM-058](../../record/terms.d/TERM-058.md) fixes the word: predictive, relative to an information set,
  its lags and, for the measure, a model class.
- [CLAIM-333](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-333.md) answers C5. Measuring every relevant variable is
  necessary and not sufficient. Two series with nothing hidden, where a
  acts on b within one sampling step, give Granger noncausality and an
  intervention effect of ργ. It was checked by hand and by simulation.
- [CLAIM-334](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-334.md) is the disclaimer the Seth reading called for. Granger
  causation from a macro variable to the micro variables it supervenes on
  is not an interventional effect, because no intervention on the macro
  variable holds its micro base fixed.
- No QUESTION was filed. C5 was the open question, and the claim answers
  it.

## What the readings changed

- [NOTE-010](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-010.md)'s C5 and its limitations line are annotated. [NOTE-053](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-053.md)'s C7 is
  checked against its source.
- [LIT-048](../../record/literature.d/LIT-048.md) carries `causality` and `extends` Barnett, Barrett and Seth.
  The topic's blurb names causal inference, and the predictive status of
  its subject is said in its THEORY, so the tag does not mislead.
  [THEORY-641](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-641.md) `extends` [THEORY-700](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-700.md).

## Boundary

None of the five is held in the anthology. A grep of its `record/`
(clone of 2026-10-12, d1573d2) for "Granger", "transfer entropy",
"Geweke", "Eichler", "Didelez" and the identifiers found nothing, and its
topic vocabulary has no word for causal inference or time series.
Eichler and Didelez appeared at UAI, but it is time-series causal
inference with no instruction for machine-learning practice. None of
the five carries one.

## Transfer entropy: eight works filed, seven read, and whether it measures flow

*2026-10-17 00:25:21 · curation · record*

After the Granger-causality filing (the entry of 2026-10-16 23:59), the
owner asked how the record stood on transfer entropy, and then for the gaps
named to be filled. The record used the measure in a dozen documents and
held one source for it, Barnett and Bossomaier ([LIT-048](../../record/literature.d/LIT-048.md)). Five gaps were
named: Schreiber's paper, which defines it, was not held. There was no
TERM, and the documents' definitions differed. Whether it measures flow at
all had no source. Its estimators were cited but not held. The neighbouring
measures, directed information, interventional flow and local transfer
entropy, were absent.

## What entered

The assistant registered the eight works and read seven in parallel,
four readers taking two each. Each reader wrote only its own LITs, NOTEs
and THEORYs, and the assistant wrote the TERM, the claim and every edit to
an existing document.

- **Schreiber (2000)**, [LIT-1177](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1177.md), arXiv, read in [NOTE-940](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-940.md), filed as
  [THEORY-701](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-701.md). The Letter's tent-map coefficient is twice what its Eq. 4
  gives at lowest order. The reader found it and the assistant rederived
  it; α is fitted, so only the fit is rescaled.
- **Kaiser and Schreiber (2002)**, [LIT-1167](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1167.md), `Unavailable`: ScienceDirect
  only. Read through Barnett, Barrett and Seth.
- **Kraskov, Stögbauer and Grassberger (2004)**, [LIT-1163](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1163.md), arXiv, read in
  [NOTE-938](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-938.md), §§III–IV from prose and captions; filed as [THEORY-709](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-709.md). The
  estimator was checked against −½log(1 − r²) on correlated Gaussians. The
  anthology uses it as a tool in its information-bottleneck readings but
  does not hold it, and it has no topic for an estimator of mutual
  information.
- **Lizier, Prokopenko and Zomaya (2008)**, [LIT-1175](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1175.md), arXiv, read in
  [NOTE-943](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-943.md), filed as [THEORY-702](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-702.md). `published:` is the journal's 15 February
  2008, earlier than the arXiv posting.
- **Williams and Beer (2011)**, [LIT-1176](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1176.md), an arXiv preprint, read in
  [NOTE-942](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-942.md), filed as [THEORY-712](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-712.md). One corner of its three-process
  example is labelled with c and d transposed.
- **James, Barnett and Crutchfield (2016)**, [LIT-1165](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1165.md), arXiv, read in
  [NOTE-945](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-945.md), filed as [THEORY-707](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-707.md). Both its examples were recomputed
  exactly.
- **Massey (1990)**, [LIT-1166](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1166.md), from his ETH institute's archive, read in
  [NOTE-939](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-939.md), filed as [THEORY-711](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-711.md). The reader showed directed
  information is full-history transfer entropy plus instantaneous terms,
  and checked it numerically.
- **Ay and Polani (2008)**, [LIT-1174](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1174.md), the 2006 MPI preprint in the
  Hertfordshire repository, read in [NOTE-946](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-946.md), filed as [THEORY-710](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-710.md).
  `published:` is the preprint's date: Crossref gives only a month for
  print and a later online date. Examples 3–5 reproduce. Example 6 holds
  only at k = 1 or for an intervention on the last step alone.

## The record's own argument

- [TERM-057](../../record/terms.d/TERM-057.md) fixes the word with k, l and the conditioning set explicit.
  [NOTE-053](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-053.md) and [NOTE-788](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-788.md) turned out not to disagree. Both choose within
  Schreiber's free k and l. Only [NOTE-788](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-788.md)'s lag-τ form for τ > 1 falls
  outside his definition.
- [CLAIM-335](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-335.md) answers the flow question. Transfer entropy is unique plus
  synergistic information, so it is directed predictive improvement, not
  flow. This is a second failure, beside [CLAIM-333](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-333.md)'s prediction against
  intervention: in the first worked example an intervention does move the
  target, and what fails is localizing the bit.

## What remains

- Williams and Beer's partial information decomposition (arXiv 1004.2515),
  the source of I_min, is not held, and neither are the critiques of I_min.
  The claim needs only the two-term split, but every number past it rests
  on that measure.
- [NOTE-320](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-320.md) says "the Kraskov k-NN estimator … estimates H(T)". An entropy
  estimate from that paper is the Kozachenko–Leonenko estimator it
  restates, not its mutual-information estimators. Which one Saxe et al.'s
  code uses was not checked, so the note is left alone.

## Boundary

None of the eight is held in the anthology. A grep of its `record/`
(d1573d2) for the authors and identifiers found only Kraskov's estimator
used as a tool. None carries an instruction for machine-learning practice.

## Multivariate redundancy: Griffith's view and the three-source impossibility, read; the record files why the gap cannot close as stated

*2026-10-17 02:53:41 · curation · record*

After [#158](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/158) merged, the owner asked for the gaps it left to be filled
where copies could be had. The three unavailable works are Granger
(1969), Geweke (1982) and Kaiser and Schreiber (2002), and they stay
unavailable. The other two gaps were open. Griffith's view, which Harder,
Salge and Polani argue against, was not held. And no held measure gave ΦID
a redundancy function with the identity property for more than two
sources. The assistant chose four works with open arXiv copies, and two
parallel readers read two each.

## What entered

- **Griffith and Koch (2014)**, [LIT-1204](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1204.md), arXiv v6 read in full, with v1
  and v2 read for the passage v6 withdraws; [NOTE-966](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-966.md), [THEORY-716](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-716.md).
  Table 1 reproduces. Harder, Salge and Polani quote v1 and v2 accurately,
  and v6 concedes their point.
- **Griffith, Chong, James, Ellison and Crutchfield (2014)**, [LIT-1203](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1203.md),
  [NOTE-967](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-967.md), [THEORY-715](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-715.md). I_∧ is defined for any n and is nonnegative,
  but it fails identity and gives negative atoms already for two sources.
- **Rauh, Bertschinger, Olbrich and Jost (2014)**, [LIT-1202](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1202.md), [NOTE-965](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-965.md),
  [THEORY-713](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-713.md). XORCOPY's arithmetic was checked. The reader noted that the
  proof uses two premises not listed as axioms.
- **Ince (2017)**, [LIT-1201](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1201.md), §§1–6 in full and §§7–8 at lower resolution;
  [NOTE-968](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-968.md), [THEORY-714](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-714.md), Proposed. The named examples reproduce.

## The gap's verdict

It cannot close as stated. On the Williams–Beer lattice, which ΦID
inherits, no redundancy function has both identity and nonnegative atoms
from three sources up. The record files this as [CLAIM-343](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-343.md): a ΦID
verdict on three or more parts must name the axiom it gives up. Two-part
analyses are unaffected. [CLAIM-335](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-335.md)'s examples now have the same values
under four measures.

## What remains

- A multivariate decomposition off the Williams–Beer lattice, which Rauh
  et al. leave open. No held work proposes one.
- Granger (1969), Geweke (1982) and Kaiser and Schreiber (2002), until
  copies are supplied.

## Boundary

None of the four is held in the anthology. A grep of its `record/`
(d1573d2) for the authors and identifiers found nothing. None carries an
instruction for machine-learning practice.

## The owner's promotion audit of 2026-10-19: two corrections, two promotions and a split

*2026-10-19 02:41:07*

The owner brought an audit of Proposed entries that might be promoted.
It covered the pending-decisions report, the most-cited CLAIMs and
THEORYs, the formal-apparatus line, and the promotion conditions those
entries record. The owner chose its first pass. The second pass, which
would split the proved parts of [THEORY-008](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md), [THEORY-005](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-005.md), [THEORY-001](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-001.md) and
[THEORY-156](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md), is not done here.

**Checked before acting.** Each entry in the first pass was checked against
the record before its status changed.

- [CLAIM-264](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-264.md). The audit asked for a final check of the density and
  strong-generator statements. One statement failed. A strong generator,
  in a category with finite limits, makes the restricted functor
  conservative, but objects with isomorphic profiles need not be
  isomorphic. (ℤ/p)³ and the Heisenberg group mod p, for p odd, have the
  same profile through ℤ: a set of p³ elements with the same power maps.
  The body's "any other family identifies objects only up to a coarser
  equivalence" was wrong in the other direction as well, because a
  non-dense family can still identify objects: in finite-dimensional
  vector spaces over a finite field, the field alone fixes the dimension.
  The claim was corrected and then promoted. [CLAIM-142](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-142.md) has the same
  sentence and gets a dated note pointing to the correction; its
  application is unchanged.
- [CLAIM-123](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-123.md). The audit pointed out that conditional independence is
  sufficient, not necessary, for s₁₂ = s₁ + s₂ − s₀. The record checked
  this and built an explicit example: three-valued conditions coupled by
  a factor 1 + ε v(y₁)v(y₂), where v is orthogonal to every conditional
  p(·|x). This met the claim's own defeat condition. The derivation
  survives, so the claim was corrected in place rather than rejected. It
  stays Proposed, because the audit did not propose promoting it.
- [THEORY-155](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-155.md). The title was already the conditional theorem. Only
  the promotion condition, a human-chain experiment, held it back, and the
  body already said that the THEORY does not claim human chains converge.
  The record checked the stationarity of the prior again. The condition
  moved unchanged to [QUESTION-137](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-137.md). The title gained the
  ergodicity condition the body already stated.
- [CLAIM-128](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md). The claim was filed as demonstrated, but its defeat
  condition is about which tasks show trade-offs, and its thesis is
  argued. The part that is proved is now [CLAIM-371](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-371.md), with a
  proof, filed Active. [CLAIM-128](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md) rests on it and is interpretive.

**Left alone, as the audit advised.** The audit named [CLAIM-025](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-025.md),
[CLAIM-284](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md) and [THEORY-232](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-232.md) as highly cited and still interpretive or
untested. They stay Proposed. [CLAIM-269](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-269.md) is not narrowed here either:
it depends on [THEORY-008](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md), [THEORY-002](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-002.md) and [THEORY-019](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-019.md), which are Proposed.

**The pattern the audit named.** Some promotion conditions combine two
jobs: checking a proof and showing that the result explains something
beyond itself. Separating them, as [QUESTION-137](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-137.md) does for [THEORY-155](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-155.md),
is the move the second pass would make for the other THEORYs.

## The promotion audit's second pass: the proved parts of THEORY-001, -005, -008 and -156

*2026-10-19 03:41:34*

The owner asked for the second pass of the promotion audit of 2026-10-19
(the first pass is the entry of 02:41 today). It covered four Proposed
THEORYs whose proved parts were held back by promotion conditions that
also asked for something else. Each was checked against the NOTE that read
its source before anything changed. None of the four parents was promoted
whole. In three, the proved part is filed apart, and the fourth is
narrowed to it.

- **[THEORY-008](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md) → narrowed and promoted.** [NOTE-834](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-834.md) met the promote_when's
  first clause and found the population clause unmeetable from [LIT-257](../../record/literature.d/LIT-257.md).
  It named the alternative, "a rewording that confines the claim to finite
  M". The body was already about M stimuli, so only the title changed. The
  population clause is now [QUESTION-136](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-136.md).
- **[THEORY-005](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-005.md) → [CLAIM-370](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-370.md).** The operator identity with the finite-χ²
  condition was, in the THEORY's own words, "the record's own". The
  THEORY's promotion condition asks for a published statement, which a
  reading must meet but a proof does not. A result the record proves is a
  CLAIM ([ADR-032](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)), so it is filed as one with a written proof, demonstrated
  and Active. Writing the proof added the converse, which the THEORY had
  stated without argument: if T is Hilbert–Schmidt, its kernel is the
  density of P⁺ on rectangles, so P⁺ ≪ p⊗p and χ² is finite. [THEORY-005](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-005.md)
  stays Proposed for what the sources show and for trained features.
- **[THEORY-001](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-001.md) → [THEORY-719](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-719.md).** The promote_when recorded the spectral
  and NT-Logistic derivations as done. The new THEORY holds them, sourced
  to [LIT-258](../../record/literature.d/LIT-258.md) App. B.2–B.3. [THEORY-001](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-001.md) extends it and waits, as before, on
  the InfoNCE/NT-Xent minimizer.
- **[THEORY-156](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) → [THEORY-717](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md).** The promote_when concerns the
  arbitrary-outcome case, which rests on Theorems 1–2 quoted from 1951. In
  the finite case Blackwell (1953) proves the converse himself (Theorems
  4–6), and [NOTE-595](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-595.md) followed that proof step by step. The direct
  implication is written in matrix form, Q = PM ⇒ PMD = QD, so the finite
  THEORY does not lean on the quoted theorems. [THEORY-156](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) extends it.

**Not done.** [THEORY-087](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md) was in the audit's table but not in its second
pass, so its regular-model half is not split here. The thirteen claims that
cite [THEORY-156](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) are not re-pointed at the finite THEORY. Whether each one
needs only finite outcomes is a reading of each claim, and [THEORY-156](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md)'s
note says they can be re-pointed.

today).

**[THEORY-087](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md).** The audit said the regular-model Laplace/Occam half "is
established in the sources", and [THEORY-087](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md)'s own promote_when said "the
regular half is derived in the sources". The check found that this holds
for one model class only. MacKay's Occam-factor formula is exact for
linear-in-parameters models with Gaussian noise and prior, and a Gaussian
approximation otherwise ([NOTE-471](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-471.md)). Grünwald & Roos's eq. 16 is cited to
Rissanen and to Suzuki & Yamanishi ([NOTE-760](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-760.md)). Watanabe's Theorem 5 is
about WBIC. The free-energy expansion that would give the regular penalty
is his Theorem 2, also cited ([NOTE-473](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-473.md)). So only the exact case is
promoted: [THEORY-718](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-718.md), with the (k/2) log n step written out as the
record's algebra. [THEORY-087](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md) extends it. Its promote_when now asks for a
held proof of the general regular expansion (Schwarz, or a Laplace or
Bernstein–von Mises argument) as well as the singular one. The promotion
was smaller than the audit proposed, because the premise was overstated.

<a id="20261019235352"></a>

## Five works on the rubber hand illusion and bodily self-consciousness, filed to fill a gap next to Metzinger's self-model

*2026-10-19 23:53:52*

The owner asked how the record stood on the rubber hand illusion. The answer
was that it held nothing directly. Body ownership appeared only as claim C6
of the reading of Metzinger's "Self models" ([NOTE-372](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-372.md)): "body ownership can
be manipulated by multisensory conflict and is the simplest form of
self-awareness". That claim rested on Lenggenhager et al. 2007 and Blanke &
Metzinger 2009, neither of which the record held. The interoception and
active-inference holdings ([LIT-542](../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md), [LIT-135](../../record/literature.d/LIT-135.md), [LIT-1181](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1181.md)) did not touch
ownership at all.

The owner asked for the gap to be filled, told the filer to assume the
anthology did not hold these works, and dropped the boundary rule in the same
exchange ([ADR-048](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-048.md)). No anthology check was made. Each LIT's first history note
says so.

Five works were filed and each was read in full:

- **Botvinick & Cohen 1998** ([LIT-1277](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1277.md), [NOTE-1006](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1006.md)). This is the
  original rubber hand illusion. Its one page was read from Nature's typeset
  page on a UC Davis faculty site. That host is a third party, not the
  authors or the publisher, and Unpaywall and OpenAlex both report the work
  closed. The history notes say so. If the owner does not accept that copy,
  the LIT goes to Unavailable and the NOTE is retired.
- **Lenggenhager, Tadi, Metzinger & Blanke 2007** ([LIT-1279](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1279.md),
  [NOTE-999](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-999.md)), the full-body illusion. The paper, its supplementary
  material and the 2008 e-letters were read from EPFL Infoscience. The
  University of Zurich copy OpenAlex points to sits behind a bot check. The
  e-letters carry Ehrsson & Petkova's objection that participants may have
  simply recognised themselves on video.
- **Blanke & Metzinger 2009** ([LIT-1274](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1274.md), [NOTE-1002](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1002.md)), minimal
  phenomenal selfhood. Read from the publisher PDF on EPFL Infoscience. It
  narrows [NOTE-372](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-372.md)'s "simplest form" to ownership of the whole body, not of
  parts.
- **Apps & Tsakiris 2014** ([LIT-1262](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1262.md), [NOTE-991](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-991.md)), the free-energy
  self. Read from the PMC author manuscript (PMC3848896). It names
  interoception but does not model it, so its tie to the interoceptive
  holdings is thinner than the request assumed.
- **Seth 2013** ([LIT-1263](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1263.md), [NOTE-1000](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1000.md)), interoceptive inference.
  Read from the publisher PDF in the Sussex repository on figshare. This,
  not Apps & Tsakiris, is the bridge from the interoception cluster to body
  ownership.

The readings were done in parallel. One reader's `luria link --fix`, given
only its own paths, linked across the whole tree: "linked 53 reference(s) in
4040 file(s)". It touched [ADR-048](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-048.md), which another contribution was drafting
at the same time, and the reader's revert broke a link the lint wanted. The
link was restored before commit. **Path arguments to `luria link --fix` do
not confine it in luria 1.1.0.** Concurrent fillers should not run it at
all; the integrator should run it once.

No THEORY was filed. The readers proposed three, which overlap:

1. Synchrony between seen and felt touch suffices for ownership and drift.
2. Ownership is a posterior over the common cause of multisensory input.
3. Ownership is inferred from interoceptive as well as exteroceptive
   signals.

A fourth, on whole-body ownership as the core of minimal selfhood, came
from Blanke & Metzinger. These are left for a later pass, with the
anthology-free filing rule now in place.

<a id="20261020001024"></a>

## Four THEORYs from the rubber-hand batch, all Proposed

*2026-10-20 00:10:24*

The owner asked for the THEORYs proposed in the rubber-hand batch (entry of
23:53 yesterday) to be filed. Four are filed, all Proposed. Each one was
written from the five NOTEs, not from the readers' one-line proposals, and
each claims no more than its sources show.

- **[THEORY-765](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-765.md)**, the synchrony effect, from Botvinick & Cohen alone.
  Its promote_when asks for a replication with effect sizes and a control
  for suggestion. The 1998 page does not discuss demand characteristics,
  and its predicted items were guessable.
- **[THEORY-769](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-769.md)**, ownership as a graded belief about the common cause
  of multisensory input, from Apps & Tsakiris. The source has no data and
  grants the account is hard to falsify. Its promote_when asks for a
  model-based test with held-out conditions, and for the real hand's loss
  of ownership to be shown on a measure other than temperature or
  histamine.
- **[THEORY-767](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-767.md)**, interoceptive signals in ownership, from Seth. All
  its evidence is second-hand, and one of the two cardio-visual studies is
  Seth's own. Its promote_when asks for the control the NOTE named: a
  non-bodily periodic signal at heart rate.
- **[THEORY-768](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-768.md)**, minimal selfhood as identification with the whole
  body, from Blanke & Metzinger with Lenggenhager et al. The part–whole
  split rests on what the rubber-hand studies did not measure. The agency
  thesis rests on adults whose agency was intact. The promote_when asks
  for both to be tested.

The fourth sits in tension with the second and third, which treat part and
whole ownership as one inference. No THEORY settles that tension, and it
is named in their Connections.

The Lenggenhager proposal, on self-location shifting partway toward a
seen body, was not filed separately. It is a part of [THEORY-768](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-768.md)'s
evidence, and its own-body result is too inconsistent between the two
studies to stand alone.

No relation is declared on any of them: no open question in the record asks
how body ownership arises or what the minimal self is made of. If such a
question is opened, these four answer it.

## Nine experimental works on the rubber hand illusion, and the THEORY they correct

*2026-10-20 00:59:22*

The owner accepted the UC Davis copy of Botvinick & Cohen ([LIT-1277](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1277.md)'s
history now says so). The owner then asked for experimental work, in the
spirit of experimental philosophy, that builds on the rubber hand
illusion. A search found almost no x-phi in the strict sense of folk-
intuition surveys about body ownership. What does build on the illusion is
experimental work aimed at the questions the THEORYs of the entry of 00:10
left open. Nine works were filed in three groups, and each was read in full
from a lawful copy.

- **Suggestion.**
  - Lush 2020 ([LIT-1276](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1276.md)), from the PsyArXiv final manuscript.
  - Lush et al. 2020 ([LIT-1271](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1271.md)), with its supplement and peer-review
    file.
  - Ehrsson et al. 2022 ([LIT-1264](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1264.md)) and Lush & Seth 2022 ([LIT-1267](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1267.md)),
    filed as rivals.
  - Roseboom & Lush 2022 ([LIT-1280](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1280.md)), from the accepted manuscript and
    the authors' OSF notebooks.
- **Drift.** Rohde, Di Luca & Ernst 2011 ([LIT-1281](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1281.md)) and Abdulkarim &
  Ehrsson 2016 ([LIT-1268](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1268.md)).
- **Structure.** Longo et al. 2008 ([LIT-1275](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1275.md)), from the published PDF
  on the first author's lab site, and Kalckert & Ehrsson 2012
  ([LIT-1273](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1273.md)).

**What changed.** [THEORY-765](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-765.md) had named its own refutation: drift
toward the rubber hand "as strongly under asynchrony". Rohde et al. found
exactly that, with asynchronous brushing interrupted every 10 s, and found
as much drift with the hand only seen. The THEORY is Rejected, and
[THEORY-766](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-766.md) corrects it. The new THEORY claims a difference in reports.
It ranks the ownership report as weaker than referred touch, and it says
drift is not a measure of either report. It leaves open whether the
stimulation or expectation produces the difference.

The old promotion test also had a flaw that the 2022 exchange exposed. The
test accepted "trait suggestibility measured and the synchrony effect
survives it". Ehrsson et al. met that clause on 353 participants. Lush &
Seth then showed that uniform but unequal expectations predict the same
result. The new test requires expectations to be matched in the
participants who were actually stimulated.

[THEORY-769](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-769.md), [THEORY-767](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-767.md) and [THEORY-768](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-768.md) keep their claims. They
take version 2 with tighter promotion tests: expectations measured or
matched, drift not standing in for ownership, and, for the interoceptive
one, the sensitivity relation surviving trait suggestibility. None moves
status.

**Who is on which side.** The record's two predictive accounts of ownership
have source authors on opposite sides of the 2022 exchange. Tsakiris, of
Apps & Tsakiris, signs Ehrsson et al. Seth, of Seth 2013, signs the reply.
Longo signs Ehrsson et al. and is first author of Longo et al. 2008.

**Not done.**
- The readers proposed revising [THEORY-458](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-458.md)'s refutation clause after
  Kalckert & Ehrsson, who show agency without ownership with a rotated
  hand. [THEORY-458](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-458.md) predates this batch and rests on other readings, so the
  proposal is left for its own pass.
- The strict-sense x-phi found in the search (Starmans & Bloom 2012;
  Nichols & Bruno 2010; the folk-pain-location studies) and the experiments
  by philosophers (Hohwy & Paton 2010; Alsmith & Longo 2014) are not filed.
  The owner was offered them separately.

**Process.** The readers were told not to run `luria link`, after the
tree-wide link bug found yesterday. One `luria link --fix` at the end
linked 211 references in the new files and touched nothing else.

Eyink 2005 matters most among these, since [THEORY-754](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-754.md)'s bounds are

**Dates corrected.** The ACHA papers' `published:` had been OpenAlex days,
which are Crossref deposit dates. The publisher's PDFs give 2006-06-08
for diffusion wavelets and 2006-06-19 for diffusion maps. Eyink 2005's
date may be a deposit date too, and could not be confirmed.

**Corrections to what the record said before reading:**
- [THEORY-661](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-661.md) said Simon–Ando gives a separation of time scales "to order
  ε". The open statement of the theorem gives no rate, so the phrase is
  withdrawn.
- Eyink and Aluie's LIT said the paper "proves" its bounds. It sketches
  them; the proofs are Eyink 2005's.
- Parish and Duraisamy's summary is corrected: the memory length is
  fitted, not derived.

**What the readings gave the record's own argument:**

- *Aggregation is not decomposition, exactly.* [THEORY-755](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-755.md): a
  partition's block sums close for every state iff the partition is
  column-equitable, which is a symmetry condition, not weak coupling.
  [CLAIM-388](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-388.md)'s uniform-coupling system turns out to be aggregable
  along every partition. [QUESTION-218](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-218.md) gains a third kind of unit.
- *Near-decomposability against dynamical dependence.* [CLAIM-390](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-390.md): for
  a block's full state, dependence is of second order in the coupling into
  the block. [CLAIM-386](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-386.md): the Simon–Ando aggregate's closure defect is
  exactly QA(I − VQ), and its intra-block part vanishes iff column sums are
  equal. Together they answer the forward half of [QUESTION-221](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-221.md) in
  part.
- *Memory against dynamical independence.* [CLAIM-389](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-389.md): in VAR(1),
  independence implies zero memory, not conversely.
- *Augmentation, in practice.* [THEORY-760](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-760.md): the finite-memory LES
  closure is a finite Markovian augmentation whose extra coordinate is the
  subgrid force. Its error is not controlled.
- *Scale locality is banded, not gapped.* [THEORY-754](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-754.md), conditional on
  an unproved scaling hypothesis.

Four demonstrated claims ([CLAIM-390](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-390.md), [CLAIM-386](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-386.md), [CLAIM-389](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-389.md)
and the earlier [CLAIM-388](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-388.md)'s note) were re-checked numerically from
scratch before filing. The readers' scripts are not kept in the record.

What it gave the argument:
- *Nesting of optimal abstractions.*
  - Optimal deterministic IB partitions at two budgets can be
    incomparable ([CLAIM-387](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-387.md), re-run here).
  - Every IB optimum nests under the causal partition, its β → ∞ limit
    ([THEORY-743](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-743.md)).
  - Rate–distortion refinability is a Markov condition on some optimal
    pair ([THEORY-751](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-751.md)).
  - [QUESTION-220](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-220.md)'s deterministic half is answered; the stochastic
    half is open.
- *The three orders.* Diffusion maps are the case where they agree
  exactly, because they share an eigenbasis ([THEORY-745](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-745.md)). Refinement
  and relevance to parameters share a chain under coarse-graining
  ([THEORY-742](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-742.md)).
- *Emergence criteria.* Rosas et al.'s Ψ and dynamical independence
  diverge both ways ([THEORY-764](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-764.md)). The paper's Proposition 1 claims
  more than its proof shows ([NOTE-987](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-987.md)).

Errors found in the papers are listed in each NOTE. Among those that bear
on the record:
- Coifman and Lafon's truncation bound is absolute, not relative.
- Crutchfield and Shalizi's logistic-map dive figure is the single-symbol
  entropy, not the entropy rate.
- Raju et al.'s relevant directions lose information when 0 < λ < d/2.

## Six more: philosophers' experiments on the rubber hand and self-location, and folk-concept x-phi on the self and pain

*2026-10-20 01:49:17*

The owner asked for the two groups left out of the entry of 00:59 to be
filed. Six works were filed, each read in full.

**Philosophers running rubber hand and self-location experiments.**

- **Hohwy & Paton 2010** ([LIT-1272](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1272.md)), from PMC. After the illusion
  starts, touch is reported as caused by a finger hovering over a rubber arm,
  or on a cardboard box. Before it starts, a box takes no touch. It is also
  the study Apps & Tsakiris cite for cooling of the real hand. That result
  is 0.13 °C in one comparison of four, one-tailed, under a real foreign
  arm. [THEORY-769](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-769.md) now says so; its claim and status are unchanged. No
  item asks about ownership, and expectations were not measured.
- **Alsmith & Longo 2014** ([LIT-1266](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1266.md)), from the published PDF on
  Longo's lab site. People pointing "directly at you" divide between the
  upper face and the upper torso, and which one wins depends on where the
  pointer starts. It gives [THEORY-768](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-768.md)'s self-location a measure other
  than drift, one a task factor moves. Its reanalysis prints "p = .53" for
  an F that gives about .053.

**Folk-concept experimental philosophy.** These sit near the topic rather
than building on the rubber hand. Each NOTE says what a folk judgement can
and cannot establish ([QUESTION-048](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-048.md)).

- **Starmans & Bloom 2012** ([LIT-1265](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1265.md)), from the Yale lab site. The
  record's citation is *Cognition* 123(2); the brief had given 124(3).
  Children and adults judge a drawn character to be "closer" to things near
  its eyes. Read beside Alsmith & Longo's first-person result, which puts
  the torso alongside the face.
- **Nichols & Bruno 2010** ([LIT-1269](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1269.md)), from a copy linked on Nichols's
  own site. First- and third-person tellings of Williams's case give the
  same verdict, so Williams's explanation of his two arguments by
  grammatical person does not hold for this sample.
  - The reader proposed that [THEORY-531](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-531.md) note this in "What this does not
    say". [THEORY-531](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-531.md) predates this batch, so the proposal is left for its
    own pass.
  - A reply, Berniūnas & Dranseika 2016, is named in the NOTE and not
    filed.
- **Reuter, Sienhold & Sytsma 2019** ([LIT-1278](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1278.md)) and **Borg, Harrison,
  Stazicker & Salomons 2020** ([LIT-1270](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1270.md)), from repository manuscripts.
  - The Borg copy is labelled accepted but headed "Revise and resubmit".
  - They take opposite sides on whether the folk concept of pain is
    bodily, and both use implicature as their tool.
  - Neither bears on the rubber hand THEORYs.

**A vocabulary gap.** The topics list has no word for experimental
philosophy or for the method of intuitions. The folk-concept works are
tagged with what they are about (personhood, consciousness, philosophy of
language, epistemology), not with how they work. If the record collects
more x-phi, a word for it is a decision to make, not a tag to improvise.

**Process.** One reader's bare codes turned into links while it worked, so
a `luria link` ran somewhere mid-batch. `git status` afterwards showed no
tracked file changed, so it touched only the untracked drafts. The final
`luria link --fix` linked 152 references.

## Lessig's Remix filed and read; the two Jenkins books searched and marked Unavailable

*2026-10-20 01:56:18*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-1121 LIT-1143 — Unavailable; the works this entry searched for and did not reach -->
<!-- inactive-ok-file: CLAIM-332 CLAIM-002 CLAIM-034 — Proposed; claims the reading bears on, cited as open -->
The owner asked how the record stood on remix culture. The answer was
that it held nothing on the subject: no Lessig, nothing on sampling,
appropriation art, fair use or Creative Commons. The nearest works were
Jenkins's *Convergence Culture* ([LIT-1121](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1121.md)) and Jenkins, Ford and Green's
*Spreadable Media* ([LIT-1143](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1143.md)), both registered unread from the sports
fandom exchange (workbench entry of 2026-10-16). The nearest case was the
Juggernaut redub ([CASE-100](../../record/cases.d/CASE-100.md)). The owner then asked for Lessig's *Remix* and
the two Jenkins books to be filed.

**Remix: filed and read, [LIT-1298](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1298.md) and [NOTE-1023](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1023.md).** Lessig released the
book under CC BY-NC, and Bloomsbury Academic published that edition. The
copy read is the publisher's PDF as redistributed under the licence on
the Internet Archive. It has the Penguin Press pagination. The book was
read in full in three parts by three sub-agents, each told to read every
line of its part, and the NOTE was composed from their reports. Every
quotation in the LIT and NOTE was then checked against the extracted text
by script. Four that did not match were corrected. A note number was
also checked and corrected: Patterson is ch. 9 n. 10, not n. 9.

- **Tags.** `society-and-governance` first, since the book is about law
  and policy, then `social-science`. No new topic was needed. The closest
  words, `social-ontology` and `myth-and-folklore`, would be wrong.
- **Not in the anthology.** A grep of its record/ (clone of 2026-10-20,
  commit d1573d2) for "Lessig", "Convergence Culture" and "Spreadable
  Media" found nothing. The book carries no instruction for
  machine-learning practice, so it has no `anthology-candidate` flag.
- **What it bears on.** Its argument that remix needs the original,
  because the meaning is carried by the reference, is the sharpest
  contact with the record's argument. It says that for remix,
  [CLAIM-002](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-002.md)'s "identity of the artifact" is the relation that does the
  work, the reverse of translation. The NOTE raises, without filing, a
  question: can recognizability of the source artifact be a preservation
  target in its own right? For [CASE-100](../../record/cases.d/CASE-100.md) and [CLAIM-332](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-332.md) the book supplies
  vocabulary (sharing economy, hybrid, RW remix) and no answer, because it
  never asks whether a population acts as a population.

**Jenkins: searched, not reached, both now Unavailable ([ADR-041](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-041.md)).**
Neither book has a lawful open copy that this client could find.

- Crossref gives no licence or full-text link for either NYU Press
  Scholarship Online DOI.
- The host, De Gruyter Brill, answered with an empty bot-check page.
- The Internet Archive holds the books only as controlled lending.
- An Internet Archive upload of the Spanish translation of *Convergence
  Culture* carries a CC BY-ND label. It is not the publisher's, and it was
  not used.
- OpenAlex refused the query because the shared daily budget was spent,
  and the DOAB API refused this client. So the search is not complete,
  and the status notes say so.

Both stay Unavailable until a copy is supplied. *Convergence Culture* is
the one to get first: *Remix* takes its Potter Wars account and its split
between "prohibitionist" and "collaborationist" companies from it.

**Not done.** No QUESTION or CLAIM was filed from the reading. The
question about recognizability is in the NOTE's open questions, for the
owner to take up or leave.

**Unavailable ([ADR-041](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-041.md)), no NOTE:**

- Drassinower, *What's Wrong with Copying?* ([LIT-1285](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1285.md)).
- Netanel, *Copyright's Paradox* ([LIT-1286](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1286.md)). Crossref records a CC
  BY-NC-ND licence, so a lawful copy exists, but OUP Academic
  bot-checked this client. The eScholarship item of the same title is
  the book's Introduction only, and it was not taken for the book.
- McLeod & DiCola, *Creative License* ([LIT-1290](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1290.md)).

Drassinower is the one to get first. Balganesh's review reports his
thesis that a work is a communicative act. It does not mention the
publisher's further claim, that an author's rights reach only as far as
"the structure of the dialogue" in which the work takes part allows.
Only the book can settle that.

**The boundary.** The anthology holds nothing on copyright (clone of
2026-10-20, commit d1573d2). The Copyright Office report carries
`anthology-candidate` last ([ADR-005](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-005.md)), because the anthology's
deployment-and-society topic could hold it. It is filed here for this
record's question: whether training is copying in Lessig's sense. *The
Line* is about AI but carries no flag. It is legal and moral theory of
personhood, as [LIT-166](../../record/literature.d/LIT-166.md) is.

**What the batch found, across readings.**

- **Lessig's copy trigger is confirmed from three sides.** *The End of
  Ownership* shows it from the buyer's side: digital transfer and use
  make copies, so first sale and lending fail. The Copyright Office
  accepts it for training's inputs, down to temporary copies. Boyle
  describes the same thing as triggers on "individual footsteps". The
  Office does not extend it to the trained model: the weights infringe
  only where a work can be recovered from them.
- **"Remix needs the original" is narrowed in law.** Boyle and Tushnet
  agree with Lessig that critique and sampling need the actual artifact.
  The *Warhol* majority accepts that only where the original is the
  target, as with parody. Commentary aimed elsewhere counts as satire,
  and it must justify the borrowing. The Court measures purpose of use;
  Kagan's dissent measures meaning.
- **[CLAIM-210](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-210.md) gets independent legal instances.** Copyright's
  independent-creation rule (Balganesh) means sharing a kind without
  being a rendering is no wrong. In *Warhol*, sharing the photograph's
  purpose mattered only once there was copying. The Office's new
  "market dilution" harm is the one place the law reaches outputs that
  share a kind with their sources without copying any one of them.
- **Tushnet adds verbal overshadowing.** Describing an image changes how
  a receiver later sees it. That bears on how [CLAIM-220](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-220.md) names its
  receivers, and it is evidence the translation line lacked.
- **Personhood.** *The Line* keeps human, legal person and moral person
  apart, as [ADR-024](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-024.md) does. But it also takes autonomy as evidence of
  consciousness. Its "inscrutability paradox" predicts that
  understanding a mechanism leads people to deny it agency, so public
  attributions would diverge from [CLAIM-174](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md)'s test.

**Possible entries not filed.** None of these was filed; each awaits the
owner:

- the 1951-to-Katrina melody chain in *The Public Domain* (ch. 6), as a
  CASE for [CLAIM-002](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-002.md);
- *Warhol*'s purpose-against-meaning split, as a CASE for [QUESTION-002](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-002.md);
- the inscrutability paradox, as an objection to [CLAIM-174](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md).

Each NOTE's open questions name what would settle them.

## Three entries from the property-and-expression readings: two cases and an objection to CLAIM-174

*2026-10-20 07:23:42*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: CLAIM-002 CLAIM-034 CLAIM-174 — Proposed; claims the new entries illustrate or object to, open -->
The owner asked for the three entries proposed in the curation entry of
06:48 today to be filed.

- **[CASE-121](../../record/cases.d/CASE-121.md)**, the melody chain in Boyle's *The Public Domain*: from
  the Bailey Gospel Singers' "I've Got a Savior" through Ray Charles,
  Kanye West and Jamie Foxx to The Legendary K.O. It illustrates [CLAIM-002](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-002.md)
  and [CLAIM-210](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-210.md). Its three links are three different relations: a
  rewording, a licensed re-performance and a sample.
- **[CASE-122](../../record/cases.d/CASE-122.md)**, *Warhol v. Goldsmith*: one rendering, measured by
  the purpose of its use (the majority) and by its meaning (the
  dissent), with opposite verdicts. It illustrates [CLAIM-034](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-034.md) and
  [CLAIM-210](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-210.md) and bears on [QUESTION-002](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-002.md).
- **[CLAIM-393](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-393.md)**, a counter to [CLAIM-174](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md) from Boyle's
  inscrutability paradox in *The Line*. It does not dispute the test. It
  says public and legal attributions of agency to artifacts track
  whether the mechanism is understood, so they cannot be the
  "independent marks" [CLAIM-174](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md)'s defeater appeals to.

Each case uses `illustrates`, not `grounds`. Neither was asked to bear
weight, and adding grounds would change the claims' own entries.

Checking corrected the draft in three places:

  at pp. 125–126 and 144, not 143–146.
- The *Warhol* case's first draft said the other tribute covers did not
  copy Goldsmith. People's cover was another Goldsmith photograph, used
